papers.title: Incidental Thyroid Neuroendocrine Carcinoma Revealing a Presumed Occult Gastrointestinal Malignancy.
papers.abstract: In rare cases, a thyroid mass may represent metastatic neuroendocrine disease rather than a primary thyroid malignancy. This case report describes a unique presentation of neuroendocrine carcinoma involving the thyroid with concurrent somatostatin receptor-positive gastrointestinal and mesenteric lesions of uncertain origin, providing insight into the diagnostic and management challenges of this disease. We present a 60-year-old male patient found to have an incidental 11 cm left thyroid mass with airway displacement on neck computed tomography (CT). A left thyroid lobectomy was performed, and surgical pathology confirmed neuroendocrine carcinoma. Immunohistochemical and molecular testing argued against medullary thyroid carcinoma, while site-of-origin markers created a diagnostic challenge with features suggestive of both pulmonary and non-pulmonary origin. Subsequent DOTATATE positron emission tomography (PET) scan demonstrated somatostatin receptor-avid lesions involving the duodenum and mesentery, raising the possibility of a gastrointestinal primary with metastatic spread to the thyroid. The discordance between the immunohistochemical profile and imaging findings highlights the diagnostic complexity of neuroendocrine tumors involving the thyroid and underscores the importance of comprehensive systemic evaluation, including functional imaging and site-of-origin immunohistochemistry, in the setting of atypical thyroid pathology. Prompt recognition of potential systemic neuroendocrine malignancy is essential for staging and therapeutic planning.

papers.title: Adrenal Incidentalomas: Do All Patients Require a Biochemical Workup?
papers.abstract: Adrenal incidentalomas are common findings on cross-sectional imaging, and most represent benign adrenocortical adenomas. The traditional approach has been to perform biochemical testing in essentially every patient to exclude pheochromocytoma, cortisol excess, and, when clinical suspicion is present, primary aldosteronism. However, this algorithmic approach may result in overinvestigation in light of improved adrenal imaging, recognition of the low prevalence of clinically important hormone excess, and concerns about false-positive testing. The 2023 European Society of Endocrinology guideline continues to recommend clinical and endocrine assessment for all patients but provides an important imaging-based nuance: in a homogeneous adrenal mass with ≤10 Hounsfield units on unenhanced computed tomography, the probability of pheochromocytoma is extremely low, and biochemical testing for metanephrines may reasonably be omitted. In contrast, testing for mild autonomous cortisol secretion remains broadly recommended because clinically silent cortisol excess is associated with metabolic syndrome and potential morbidity. This review examines the arguments for and against universal biochemical workup and proposes a risk-stratified approach for clinicians.

papers.title: Third-degree atrioventricular block secondary to intracardiac paraganglioma in a dog.
papers.abstract: A 14-year-old, 6-kg dog was referred for lethargy, exercise intolerance, and syncope. Electrocardiography revealed complete atrioventricular (AV) block with a narrow QRS escape rhythm at 40 bpm. Echocardiography identified a solitary mass involving the interatrial septum with extension into the interventricular septum, associated with valvular regurgitation and chamber enlargement. Despite medical management of congestive heart failure, the dog died suddenly 10 days later. Necropsy revealed a large mass infiltrating the interatrial and AV septa, including Koch's triangle and the septal vestibule. Histopathology and immunohistochemistry supported the diagnosis of an intracardiac paraganglioma exhibiting locally invasive histological features. This case describes an intracardiac paraganglioma associated with an AV block and illustrates that intracardiac neoplasia is a rare differential diagnosis for AV conduction disturbances in older dogs.
papers.journal: Journal of veterinary cardiology : the official journal of the European Society of Veterinary Cardiology

papers.title: Calmodulin kinase-like vesicle-associated protein (CAMKV) autoimmune encephalitis: Neurological & oncological accompaniments, treatments & outcomes.
papers.abstract: We previously reported CAMKV-IgG paraneoplastic encephalitis accompanying uterine and neuroendocrine-lineage carcinomas. Here, we describe 7 new cases (12 total) and report CSF cytokine/chemokine profiles and coexisting antibody frequency. Patient samples demonstrating the CAMKV-specific murine tissue-based indirect immunofluorescence assay (TIIFA) staining pattern were tested by protein microarray and confirmed CAMKV-specific cell-based assay. CSF cytokines/chemokines were analyzed in 4 patients. Median symptom-onset age was 69 years (range 53-79); 8/12 were women. Common manifestations included altered mental status (7/12), hyperkinetic movements (6/12), seizures (5/12), psychiatric, and insomnia (4/12 each). Five patients had coexisting antibodies: tripartite motif-containing protein-9 (3), N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (2), antineuronal nuclear antibody-type-1 (ANNA-1) and γ-aminobutyric acid B receptor (1 each). All 12 had cancer, including adenocarcinoma (6/12; uterine 4, lung 1, prostate 1), lymphoma (Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin), or other carcinoma (urothelial, Merkel cell, hepatocellular, and poorly differentiated (1 each). All 3 available cancers (uterine, 2; prostate adenocarcinoma, 1) were immunohistochemistry positive for CAMKV. 6/8 had CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis. MRIs revealed mesial temporal and basal ganglia T2 hyperintensities in 6/10 and 5/10, respectively. Among 7 immunotherapy-treated patients, 6 improved initially, although 5/7 with follow-up died from cancer. CSF IL-13 and GM-CSF were significantly elevated compared with non-inflammatory controls (FDR-adjusted P < 0.05). Four of 42 ANNA-1 positive samples with coexisting synaptic TIIFA staining were CAMKV-IgG positive. CAMKV-IgG is a paraneoplastic encephalitis autoantibody associated with diverse cancers. Neurologic improvement with immunotherapy is frequent, but prognosis is driven by cancer outcomes. Elevated IL-13 may indicate metastatic risk.

papers.title: Association between pathological subtypes of PitNETs and postoperative biochemical remission in acromegaly.
papers.abstract: To assess whether transcription factor (TF)- and hormone-defined pathological subtypes of pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs) are associated with postoperative biochemical remission in acromegaly. Consecutive acromegaly patients who underwent surgery between January 2015 and October 2025 with a minimum 3-month follow-up were enrolled. Patients were classified by TF and hormone expression patterns: pure vs. non-pure PIT-1 positive, and pure vs. non-pure GH positive. Drawing on target trial emulation-derived design principles, propensity score overlap weighting (OW) balanced six prespecified confounders and covariate balance was confirmed after weighting. Associations between pathological subtypes and postoperative biochemical remission were examined using weighted Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards analyses. Overall, 93.4% had macroadenomas; the overall remission rate was 51.0%. Pure PIT-1 positive and pure GH positive tumors represented 62.3% and 19.2%, respectively. After OW, for both TF and hormone classification, no statistically significant difference in postoperative cumulative biochemical remission was observed between the pure and non-pure groups (TF: P = 0.824; hormone: P = 0.444). Weighted Cox regression analyses confirmed that neitherthe TF-based (HR = 0.87, 95% CI: 0.53-1.42, P = 0.578) nor the hormone-based (HR = 1.52, 95% CI: 0.62-3.75, P = 0.362) classification of PitNETs predicted postoperative biochemical remission. Higher preoperative IGF-1 index was a significant negative predictor only in the TF-based group (HR = 0.51, 95%CI 0.37-0.74, P < 0.001). Pathological subtypes of PitNETs do not independently predict surgical remission in acromegaly. The preoperative IGF-1 index showed limited, context-dependent prognostic value. Future multimodal models integrating histology, imaging, and genomics may improve prognostic accuracy.

papers.title: Microbiome-derived TOPOSCORE is associated with response to immune checkpoint inhibitor re-induction after chemotherapy in primary resistant metastatic melanoma.
papers.abstract: Primary resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) remains a major challenge in metastatic melanoma. The prospective multicenter PROMIT trial showed that intermittent chemotherapy could restore sensitivity to ICI re-induction in a subset of patients. We investigated whether gut microbiome ecosystem states characterized by TOPOSCORE were associated with tumor response in this setting. In the phase II PROMIT trial (NCT04225390), 24 patients with longitudinal stool samples were included in this exploratory microbiome analysis. ICI-resistant patients received two cycles of dacarbazine followed by ICI re-induction. Stool samples underwent shotgun metagenomic sequencing. Microbiome ecosystem states were classified into SIG1- or SIG2-associated ecosystem states using the TOPOSCORE framework, which is based on species-interacting groups (SIGs) defined by ecological co-abundance patterns. Baseline TOPOSCORE distributions and s-scores were not associated with clinical outcome. In the nine patients with complete BL-CTX-ICI sampling, six retained the same TOPOSCORE category throughout treatment and three changed category. Of the two patients with PR, one remained SIG2 throughout, whereas the other changed from SIG2+ to SIG1+ after chemotherapy and returned to SIG2+ during ICI re-induction. Analyses using all available samples at each phase likewise did not show significant differences in s-score among PR, SD, and PD groups. Baseline TOPOSCORE classification was insufficient to predict treatment outcome in this cohort. Longitudinal TOPOSCORE patterns were heterogeneous, and the small number of complete longitudinal profiles precludes conclusions that chemotherapy induced a favorable microbiome transition. These exploratory findings support further evaluation of microbiome ecosystem dynamics in larger prospective cohorts.

papers.title: Ectopic cushing syndrome caused by intestinal neuroendocrine tumors: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Ectopic Cushing syndrome is a potentially life-threatening disorder most caused by thoracic or pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors. Intestinal neuroendocrine tumors are an exceptionally uncommon and poorly characterized source, creating important diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. We aimed to systematically characterize the clinical presentation, diagnostic pathways, treatment strategies, and outcomes of ectopic Cushing syndrome caused by intestinal neuroendocrine tumors. Systematic review of published case reports, complemented by an illustrative unpublished case. Four electronic databases were searched from inception to February 2026 according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidance. Individual patient data on clinical presentation, tumor localization, treatment, and outcomes were extracted and analyzed descriptively. Twenty-four published cases were identified. Ectopic Cushing syndrome was the initial manifestation in 87.5% of patients and frequently presented with an aggressive clinical phenotype (70.8%). Tumor localization was often challenging. Conventional imaging detected the primary lesion in fewer than half of cases, whereas functional imaging, particularly gallium-68 somatostatin receptor positron emission tomography, showed higher detection rates. Surgical resection was performed in 87.5% of patients and biochemical remission was achieved in 72.7%. However, 50% required medical therapy for hypercortisolism and 20.8% underwent bilateral adrenalectomy. Recurrence occurred in 14.3%. Intestinal neuroendocrine tumors are a rare but clinically relevant cause of ectopic Cushing syndrome. They commonly present with severe hypercortisolism and delayed tumor localization. Management requires both tumor-directed treatment and rapid endocrine control. Recurrence may occur despite initial remission, supporting prolonged surveillance and a multimodal diagnostic and therapeutic approach.

papers.title: Transfemoral transcaval adrenal biopsy: a technical report and review of adrenal biopsy approaches.
papers.abstract: Despite advances in cross-sectional imaging, adrenal biopsy plays a role in a small subset of lesions that remain indeterminate after complete imaging work-up or in which tissue diagnosis would alter management. Anatomic constraints around the adrenal glands can make safe percutaneous access technically challenging. This technical report describes a transfemoral transcaval approach to biopsy of a right adrenal mass directly abutting the inferior vena cava (IVC) that was not safely accessible by conventional percutaneous routes. Additionally, a concise review of contemporary adrenal biopsy indications and access routes is performed. Adapted from transfemoral transcaval liver biopsy, the technique uses right common femoral venous access, positioning of a reshaped metal guide cannula within the IVC at the level of the lesion adjacent to the right renal vein, and deployment of a core biopsy needle across the caval wall under combined fluoroscopic and ultrasound guidance, with cone-beam CT confirmation of needle position and completion venography to exclude caval injury. Diagnostic tissue was obtained without periprocedural complication; histopathology demonstrated an unexpected pheochromocytoma, a finding discussed here in detail due to its implications for pre-procedure biochemical evaluation. This limited experience demonstrates technical feasibility in carefully selected patients. The safety and comparative effectiveness of the technique require evaluation in larger series.

papers.title: Radiochemical Synthesis of 18F-Meta-Fluorobenzylguanidine (18F-mFBG) for PET/CT Imaging in Patients with Pheochromocytoma.
papers.abstract: Pheochromocytoma (PCC) is a relatively rare neuroendocrine tumor. Due to its diverse and often nonspecific clinical manifestations, PCC is frequently missed or misdiagnosed in clinical practice. As a positron-emitting tracer, 18F-meta-fluorobenzylguanidine (18F-mFBG) specifically targets and binds to the human norepinephrine transporter (hNET), and is used for disease diagnosis, lesion localization and assessment, and treatment planning. This study provides a detailed description of the entire process for 18F-mFBG, including radiolabeling, quality control, patient preparation, and positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET/CT) imaging. The radiolabeling of 18F-mFBG was performed using a fully automated labeling module. Patient preparation followed a standardized protocol, which included patient instructions, explanation of the protocol, and intravenous administration of the radiopharmaceutical. The PET/CT imaging section details the acquisition and reconstruction parameter settings. Validated through 32 cases, the study demonstrated that key metrics such as maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) and target-to-background ratio (TBR) effectively distinguished PCC lesions and their uptake characteristics. The results indicate that 18F-mFBG PET/CT imaging is a non-invasive and rapid method that provides information on tumor burden in PCC, offering a basis for auxiliary diagnosis and treatment planning.

papers.title: Cascaded deep learning for synthesis of 18F-FDG PET from 18F-octreotide: model parameter optimization and performance evaluation.
papers.abstract: To investigate a cascaded conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN)-based method for synthesizing 18F-FDG PET images from 18F-octreotide, optimize model parameter configurations, and evaluate the quality of the synthesized images. Imaging data from 71 tumor patients who underwent dual-tracer PET/CT examinations with 18F-FDG and 18F-octreotide between May 2022 and November 2025 were retrospectively collected. A cascaded deep learning architecture (first stage: 3D U-Net; second stage: self-attention 3D V-Net) was employed to evaluate the effects of image preprocessing, resampling size, and patch size on synthesis quality. Three preprocessing strategies (log transformation, normalization, and a combined approach) were compared. Image quality was assessed using five objective metrics (SSIM, PSNR, MSE, MAE, and NMI) and Likert 5-point ratings from three nuclear medicine physicians; liver and lesion-level SUV agreement were further evaluated. In the held-out test cohort (n = 14), the combined preprocessing method (log transformation + normalization) significantly outperformed the individual methods (SSIM: 0.8454 ± 0.0328 vs. 0.7831 ± 0.0337 vs. 0.7438 ± 0.0362, P < 0.001). On the identical held-out test cohort (n = 14), the Group 2 parameter configuration (resampling size: 256 × 256 × 512; patch size: 128 × 128 × 128) outperformed Group 1, with an SSIM of 0.8854 ± 0.0455 and a PSNR of 28.15 ± 3.35 dB, representing relative improvements of 19.1% and 83.5%, respectively, over Group 1 (paired-samples t-test, both P < 0.001). The mean Likert score was 4.53 ± 0.19. Quantitative analysis of liver SUVmean showed no significant difference between synthesized and real images (P = 0.967, paired t-test). Lesion-level quantitative analysis demonstrated high agreement between synthetic and real 18F-FDG images, with Pearson correlation coefficients of 1.0000, 0.9995, and 0.9991 for SUVmax and SUVmean (n = 14) and SUVpeak (n = 13), respectively (all P < 0.001), no significant differences on paired t-tests (all P > 0.05), and all Bland-Altman differences within the 95% limits of agreement. The cascaded deep learning model enabled cross-tracer synthesis from 18F-octreotide to 18F-FDG PET images. In this exploratory, single-center pilot cohort, the optimized configuration demonstrated promising quantitative and visual performance, supporting image-synthesis feasibility and potential clinical utility of a single-injection, dual-parameter molecular imaging approach for neuroendocrine tumors. Prospective multicenter validation is warranted before any clinical application.

papers.title: An m5C-associated NSUN5-YBX1-CENPF programme marks melanoma cell states and immune features.
papers.abstract: RNA 5-methylcytosine (m5C)-associated programmes may help characterise melanoma cell states and their immune context. We investigated an NSUN5-YBX1-CENPF (NYC) programme using patient-matched sequencing, experimental perturbation and multiscale transcriptomic analyses. We analysed m5C-MeRIP-seq and matched Input RNA data from three melanoma-adjacent-normal patient pairs, using a paired edgeR interaction model for regional IP enrichment. Tissue and cell experiments included NSUN5 knockdown, CENPF-targeted MeRIP-qPCR and western blotting. Clinical analyses considered proliferation and sampling site. Trajectory and regulatory inference were restricted to malignant cells from GSE215120, with patient-level summaries. Treatment-associated changes were examined in 43 paired patients from GSE91061. Computational perturbation and transcriptomic signature reversal prioritised candidate regulators and compounds. Two CENPF regions showed increased relative IP enrichment after Input adjustment (4.97- and 5.85-fold; BH q = 0.0457 and 0.0074). NSUN5 knockdown reduced CENPF m5C enrichment and protein abundance. NYC was associated with proliferation; its survival association did not persist after proliferation adjustment. Within malignant cells, NYC-High retained an association with an immune-resistance expression programme after G2M/E2F and depth adjustment (nine patients; BH q = 0.0156). Regulatory analyses prioritised MLX, whose simulated knockout and overexpression produced opposing reference-flow alignments (BH q = 0.0134 and 0.0201). MLX regulon activity was associated with glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation after adjustment. In GSE91061, responders showed a greater treatment-associated NYC decrease than non-responders (mean change difference -0.209; permutation P = 0.0138). Drug screening generated candidates for experimental testing. NYC provides an m5C-associated framework connecting patient-derived molecular observations to malignant-cell states and immune features. YBX1 remains a candidate reader, and regulatory, treatment-associated and drug-prioritisation findings do not establish a complete causal pathway or a clinically validated predictive biomarker.

papers.title: PANCREATIC NEUROENDOCRINE TUMORS: CLINICOPATHOLOGICAL ANALYSIS AND POSTOPERATIVE SURVIVAL FOLLOWING SURGICAL RESECTION-A DECADE OF EXPERIENCE AT A TERTIARY UNIVERSITY HOSPITAL.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (PNETs) are rare neoplasms of the digestive system, with variable prognoses and biological behaviors. Surgical resection remains the mainstay of treatment. Objective: To evaluate the clinicopathological characteristics and surgical outcomes of patients with PNETs who underwent resection at the Hospital de Clínicas, UNICAMP. This is a retrospective cohort study including 24 patients who underwent surgical resection between 2013 and 2023. Clinical, demographic, histopathological, and survival data were analyzed. The primary outcome was overall survival. The mean age was 53.9 ± 14.4 years, with a predominance of female patients (66.7%). Most tumors were nonfunctioning (79.1%), with abdominal pain (79.2%) and weight loss (50%) being the most common symptoms. The surgical procedures performed were distal pancreatectomy (54.2%), pancreaticoduodenectomy (41.6%), and enucleation (4.2%). Histological classification revealed 62.5% grade 2 tumors, 33.3% grade 1, and 4.2% MiNEN. Mean overall survival was 70.4 ± 58 months. There was a trend toward longer survival in grade 1 tumors (98 ± 68.1 months) compared to grade 2 (59.1 ± 49.5 months; P=0.06). Postoperative mortality was 8.3%, associated with pancreaticoduodenectomy. Histological grading remains a key prognostic factor in PNETs. Surgical resection remains the cornerstone of treatment. Multicenter studies are necessary to validate these findings on a larger scale.

papers.title: Merkel Cell Carcinoma Associated With a Longstanding Verrucous Plaque.
Efficacy and safety of sunitinib in treatment of advanced or metastatic pheochromocytomas and paragangliomas: A meta-analysis of sunitinib-treated arms from prospective clinical trials.
papers.abstract: Metastatic pheochromocytomas and paragangliomas (mPPGLs) are rare neuroendocrine tumors with limited treatment options. Among the options for the treatment of mPPGLs are tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), including cabozantinib and sunitinib. However, TKIs have different molecular targets and side effects. Additionally, the evidence supporting their use for these tumors has been limited and of low-quality. To summarize prospective efficacy and safety outcomes of sunitinib among patients with mPPGLs. A literature search was conducted to investigate the effects of sunitinib on progression-free survival (PFS) tumor responses and adverse events (AEs) in prospective studies of sunitinib for mPPGLs treatment. Because only one included study had a comparator, quantitative synthesis was performed at the sunitinib-treatment-arm level. Three prospective clinical trials were included in the meta-analysis. The total sample in these studies was 114 patients given sunitinib. The objective response rate was 21.2% (95% CI, 11.7-35.3%), and all the responses were partial, with no complete responses. The stable disease rate was 51.8% (95% CI, 36.8-66.4%). The progressive disease rate was 27.1% (95% CI, 19.5-36.3%). The 12-month PFS rate was 48.2% (95% CI, 38.1-58.5%). The median PFS duration was 11.9 months (95% CI, 6.9-16.9 months). The rate of treatment discontinuation due to AEs was 13.2% (95% CI, 8.1-20.7%). The rate of grade ≥3 adverse events was 57.8% (95% CI, 36.7-76.4%), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 86%; P = .001). Overall, the available low to very low certainty but prospective evidence suggests that sunitinib provides clinically relevant disease control in a subset of patients, characterized by modest objective response rates.
papers.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism

papers.title: Carotid body carcinoma in a French bulldog treated with toceranib phosphate.
papers.abstract: Carotid body tumors are rare neuroendocrine neoplasms in dogs, and evidence-based treatment options for malignant or unresectable cases remain poorly defined. An 8-year-old castrated male French bulldog was presented with a large cervical mass accompanied by progressive respiratory distress, neurologic abnormalities, and exophthalmos. Computed tomography revealed multiple, highly vascularized cervical masses with extensive local invasion, including nasopharyngeal obstruction and intracranial extension. Partial surgical excision was undertaken for diagnostic purposes, and histopathologic examination confirmed carotid body carcinoma with intravascular invasion. Because of incomplete surgical resection and malignant features, targeted therapy was initiated. Based on in vitro chemosensitivity testing, toceranib phosphate was selected. Following treatment, clinical signs related to mass effect improved, nasopharyngeal obstruction was alleviated, and increased intratumoral necrosis was suspected on follow-up imaging. Adverse effects were mild and manageable. The dog remained clinically stable for ~5 mo after targeted therapy but was subsequently lost to follow-up. On a later follow-up via telephone, the owner reported that the dog had died 6 mo after initiation of targeted therapy. Key clinical message: This case suggests that toceranib may represent a potential therapeutic option for dogs with unresectable or incompletely resected carotid body carcinoma.
papers.journal: The Canadian veterinary journal = La revue veterinaire canadienne

papers.title: Aqueous humor liquid biopsy identifies malignant transformation of retinocytoma in an adult patient.
papers.abstract: To report a rare case of adult-onset retinoblastoma arising from malignant transformation of retinocytoma and to highlight the diagnostic utility of the aqueous humor liquid biopsy. A 34-year-old woman presented with three months of floaters and flashes in the left eye. Examination revealed a peripheral amelanotic retinal lesion with retinal pigment epithelial changes, calcification, and vitreous debris. Aqueous humor biopsy analyzed with the LBSeq4Kids platform demonstrated chromosomal aneuploidy consistent with tumor-derived DNA, although the copy number profile was not characteristic of retinoblastoma or other malignancies. Germline and plasma-based testing were non-diagnostic, and systemic evaluation revealed no evidence of an occult malignancy. Over 3 months, the lesion demonstrated subtle growth from 1.32 to 1.55 mm in thickness with more vitreous debris and calcification, raising concern for retinoblastoma. However, the patient's age, atypical clinical features, and non-canonical molecular findings created diagnostic uncertainty. Following multidisciplinary review, pars plana vitrectomy and retinectomy were performed for histopathologic confirmation. The tumor was completely excised. Pathology demonstrated a neuroendocrine tumor surrounded by well-differentiated "fleurettes," consistent with retinoblastoma arising from retinocytoma. Given the potential risk of occult extraocular extension following biopsy, the patient underwent adjuvant external beam radiation therapy to the left orbit. Three months after surgery, the LBSeq4Kids targeted sequencing panel was clinically validated and became available for the aqueous humor liquid biopsy; the platform enabled detection of pathogenic variants in a panel of cancer-associated genes. Subsequent retrospective analysis of the original aqueous humor biopsy using the newly validated assay identified two pathogenic RB1 variants, confirming the retinoblastoma diagnosis. At more than 1 year after diagnosis, the patient remains disease-free. Adult-onset retinoblastoma is exceedingly rare and may arise through malignant transformation of retinocytoma. This case highlights the complementary roles of two clinically available aqueous humor-based molecular assays: 1) somatic copy number analysis serves as a sensitive marker of intraocular malignancy, and 2) targeted sequencing panel provides greater diagnostic specificity for tumor classification. In the future, these minimally invasive assays can aid in the differential diagnosis of atypical intraocular tumors and may provide an alternative to direct intraocular tumor biopsy.
papers.journal: American journal of ophthalmology case reports

papers.title: Cascade-activatable nano-prodrug amplifies ROS-RNS signaling to target NQO1-associated redox vulnerability for melanoma therapy.
papers.abstract: Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation (LPO), has emerged as a promising strategy for cancer therapy but remains limited by insufficient hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂), restricted catalytic iron availability, and the extremely short lifetime of hydroxyl radicals (·OH) in the tumor microenvironment. Here, we report a self-assembled nano-prodrug designed to amplify oxidative stress through coordinated reactive oxygen species (ROS)-reactive nitrogen species (RNS) cascades. Transcriptomic analyses of melanoma cohorts revealed that the redox enzyme NAD(P)H: quinone oxidoreductase-1 (NQO1) is frequently upregulated and associated with oxidative stress and ferroptosis-related transcriptional programs, suggesting a potential redox vulnerability that can be therapeutically exploited. Guided by this observation, a glutathione-responsive nanoplatform (HFSAL) was constructed from a disulfide-bridged ferrocene-arginine scaffold (Fc-SS-Arg) with β-lapachone (β-lapa) co-loaded and hyaluronic acid coating for tumor-targeted delivery. Upon intracellular activation, β-lapa undergoes NQO1-mediated redox cycling to generate H₂O₂, which is further converted into ·OH through ferrocene-catalyzed Fenton reactions. Meanwhile, arginine-derived nitric oxide (NO) reacts with ROS intermediates to form highly reactive peroxynitrite (ONOO⁻), thereby amplifying oxidative damage and extending the effective range of redox stress. In addition, NO-mediated vascular remodeling alleviates tumor hypoxia and enhances intratumoral drug accumulation. Consequently, the HFSAL nano-prodrug effectively induces synergistic ferroptosis and apoptosis, leading to significant tumor growth inhibition and metastasis suppression in vivo with favorable biosafety. This work presents a redox-amplifying nano-prodrug strategy that exploits NQO1-associated metabolic vulnerability to enhance ferroptosis-based cancer therapy.

papers.title: PROTAC technology for sensitizing melanoma to immune checkpoint therapy.
papers.abstract: Melanoma remains one of the most aggressive malignancies, with limited response to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) due to primary or acquired resistance. Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) have emerged as a novel therapeutic modality that induces selective degradation of target proteins via the ubiquitin-proteasome system, offering distinct advantages over conventional inhibitors. This review summarizes the design principles and molecular mechanisms of PROTACs, and highlights their emerging role in sensitizing melanoma to immunotherapy. Specifically, PROTACs can restore tumor antigen presentation, reprogram the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment by targeting regulatory T cells, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, and tumor-associated macrophages, and suppress key oncogenic signaling pathways. We also discuss combination strategies with PD-1/PD-L1 and CTLA-4 blockade, as well as current challenges including poor cell permeability, off-target effects, and acquired resistance. Finally, future perspectives on rational design, tissue-specific delivery systems, and clinical translation are addressed.
papers.journal: Journal of experimental & clinical cancer research : CR

papers.title: Divergent Schwann cell-immune cell trajectories across vestibular schwannoma subtypes mirror nerve injury-repair programs.
papers.abstract: Although Schwann cells (SCs) are increasingly recognised as active contributors to cancer progression, their cell-autonomous oncogenic mechanisms underlying vestibular schwannoma (VS) development remain poorly defined. Moreover, the roles of heterogeneity within the tumour microenvironment (TME) in VS pathogenesis remain unclear. In this study, we performed integrative multi-omic analyses of sporadic VSs and NF2-related schwannomatosis (NF2-SWN) VSs, using bulk RNA-sequencing, single-nucleus RNA-sequencing (snRNA-seq), DNA methylation profiling, and immunohistochemistry (IHC). Transcriptomic and DNA methylation profiling analyses identified two distinct molecular subgroups, immune-enriched schwannoma (IES) and immune-depleted schwannoma (IDS), independent of syndromic status. We developed multigene and IHC-based classifiers that robustly distinguish the two molecular subgroups. Notably, we found significant differences in clinical characteristics and prognostic outcomes across VS subgroups. Furthermore, snRNA-seq revealed cellular heterogeneity within the VS microenvironment, with phenotypic transitions in SCs and immune cells that closely recapitulated the sequential stages of nerve injury and repair. Collectively, our study reveals that SC plasticity and immune cell dynamics within the tumor microenvironment contribute to intertumoral heterogeneity in vestibular schwannomas, offering insights into the biological processes underlying tumor progression and nerve injury-repair programs.

papers.title: DNA methylation of silencer-annotated regions at the MGMT locus in the context of promoter and enhancer methylation in glioblastoma and melanoma brain metastases.
papers.abstract: MGMT promoter methylation is a well-established biomarker in glioblastoma, its relevance in melanoma brain metastases remains controversial. Recent studies indicate that methylation of MGMT enhancers contributes to MGMT regulation, whereas the role of silencer methylation has not yet been investigated. DNA methylation of 52 CpG sites was analyzed in regions annotated as potential silencers located in the promoter, intronic, and upstream regions of MGMT. These regions were selected based on genomic annotations and their genomic proximity to MGMT, encompassing sites to approximately 1.5 Mb upstream, without experimental validation of direct regulatory activity. Analyses were performed in glioblastoma and melanoma brain metastases using in-house developed assays based on bisulfite conversion, PCR amplification of target regions, and pyrosequencing. By integrating previously published promoter and enhancer methylation data, a DNA methylation landscape of MGMT regulatory elements was established. Associations between CpG methylation and MGMT protein expression, overall survival, patient age, and sex were evaluated. The degree of methylation strongly depended on the genomic location of the respective regulatory element. Both shared and tumor-type-specific methylation patterns were observed in glioblastoma and melanoma brain metastases. Promoter-associated CpGs and selected intronic silencer-annotated regions showed associations with MGMT protein expression. In glioblastoma, several promoter-associated CpGs were associated with overall survival, whereas sex-specific and age-related effects were absent. DNA methylation of MGMT regulatory elements is highly CpG-specific. CpG-resolved analyses reveal a complex epigenetic landscape across the MGMT locus and highlight substantial regional heterogeneity. These findings suggest that extending methylation analyses beyond the classical promoter region provides additional insights into MGMT-associated epigenetic variation and its potentical clinical associations.

papers.title: Meta-analysis and network meta-analysis of time-to-event outcomes with non-proportional hazards: a Bayesian time-varying hazard ratio approach.
papers.abstract: Meta-analyses of time-to-event (TTE) outcomes, particularly in Health Technology Assessment (HTA), commonly use a hazard ratio (HR) scale. However, non-proportional hazards in included trials create difficulties. Existing methods are either too complex or not easily incorporated into economic decision models for cost-effectiveness assessment. An alternative approach assumes a treatment-log(time) interaction within a Cox proportional hazards model, allowing the log HR to vary linearly with log(time). A bivariate meta-analysis of the resulting treatment and interaction coefficients then yields an overall time-varying HR (TVHR) with appropriate uncertainty. The TVHR approach was applied to a meta-analysis of 20 trials (4,069 patients) comparing chemotherapy to Standard of Care (SoC) for advanced recurrent gastric cancer, with Progression-Free Survival (PFS) as an outcome (median follow-up 1.2 years). It was also applied to a network meta-analysis (NMA) of 13 treatments across 13 Randomised Controlled Trials (RCTs) in previously untreated advanced BRAF-mutated melanoma (3,913 deaths in 6,378 participants) evaluating Overall Survival (OS). Both applications were compared against standard Bayesian meta-analysis assuming proportional hazards. Five trials in the gastric cancer meta-analysis showed non-proportional hazards for PFS. A standard Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis yielded a pooled HR of 0.78 (95% CrI: 0.70-0.86). The TVHR model produced a pooled interaction effect of 0.09 (95% CrI: -0.005-0.193), with HRs ranging from 0.83 (95% CrI: 0.75-0.91) at 0.5 years to 0.99 (95% CrI: 0.79-1.23) at 3.5 years. Three studies in the melanoma NMA showed non-proportional hazards for OS. Using the TVHR model, nivolumab plus ipilimumab demonstrated consistent superiority from month 7, with improving HRs from 0.37 (95% CrI: 0.26-0.51) at one year to 0.24 (95% CrI: 0.12-0.45) at five years (mean rank 1.18, 95% CrI: 1-2). Dabrafenib- and vemurafenib-based regimens showed evidence of waning treatment effects, potentially becoming inferior to dacarbazine (HR>1) at five years. The TVHR approach offers a simple, intuitive solution for meta-analysis of TTE outcomes when proportional hazards do not hold, and are readily incorporated into economic decision models. Extensions to a fully Bayesian one-stage model, and spline-based interaction effects are also feasible.

papers.title: Type III gastric neuroendocrine tumor associated with a hyperplastic polyp presenting with severe iron deficiency anemia: a case report.
papers.abstract: Type III gastric neuroendocrine tumors (G-NETs) are rare, sporadic, and aggressive gastric neuroendocrine neoplasms that are typically diagnosed after the onset of gastrointestinal symptoms or metastatic disease. Presentation with isolated severe iron deficiency anemia (IDA) is uncommon. We report a case most consistent with a locally advanced type III G-NET associated with a hyperplastic polyp, diagnosed during evaluation of severe iron deficiency anemia in a young woman without gastrointestinal symptoms. A 39-year-old woman with hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus presented with progressive fatigue and dyspnea on exertion. Laboratory evaluation revealed severe microcytic IDA with a hemoglobin level of 4 g/dL. Esophagogastroduodenoscopy demonstrated a large ulcerated gastric body mass with submucosal tumor-like morphology. Colonoscopy was unremarkable. Histopathological examination revealed a WHO grade 2 NET arising within a hyperplastic polyp, with no evidence of atrophic gastritis on background gastric biopsies. Staging with 68Ga-DOTATOC PET/CT demonstrated regional lymphadenopathy without distant metastases. The patient underwent subtotal gastrectomy with regional lymphadenectomy. Surgical pathology was consistent with a well-differentiated WHO grade 2 gastric NET, with the bulk of the tumor in the submucosa abutting the muscularis propria without infiltrating it, and metastatic involvement of two perigastric lymph nodes. Surgical margins were negative. Surveillance CT imaging at 3 and 12 months, EGD at 12 months, and 68Ga-DOTATOC PET/CT at 24 months showed no evidence of recurrence or metastatic disease. Her IDA resolved completely following supportive hematologic therapy (blood transfusion and intravenous iron supplementation) and surgical resection. Type III gastric NET may rarely present solely with severe IDA in the absence of gastrointestinal symptoms. To our knowledge, only a limited number of similar cases have been reported. This case highlights the importance of considering upper endoscopic evaluation in patients with severe or unexplained IDA, even in premenopausal women. Early recognition of type III G-NET is important because of their aggressive behavior and metastatic potential, and timely surgical management can result in favorable oncologic outcomes with resolution of anemia when combined with supportive hematologic therapy.

papers.title: PET in Theranostics: Patient Selection, Treatment Planning, and Response Assessment.
papers.abstract: Theranostics pairs molecular imaging with a therapeutic radiopharmaceutical directed at the same target, with PET assessing target expression, disease extent, interlesional heterogeneity, and FDG discordance. Three established applications are reviewed: PSMA PET-guided selection for lutetium-177-PSMA-617 in metastatic androgen pathway modulation-resistant prostate cancer, somatostatin receptor PET-guided peptide receptor radionuclide therapy in neuroendocrine tumors, and iodine-124/FDG PET within radioiodine therapy for differentiated thyroid cancer. Practical guidance covers patient selection, image interpretation, treatment planning, response assessment, and reporting. A key paradigm: diagnostic uptake confirms target availability but neither measures delivered dose nor guarantees response; biomarkers, dosimetry, and response frameworks remain variably validated.

papers.title: A Practical Guide to Somatostatin Receptor Imaging with PET/Computed Tomography.
papers.abstract: Somatostatin receptor (SSTR) imaging with PET/computed tomography (CT) is a key investigation for diagnosis, staging, restaging and evaluation of potential suitability for radionuclide therapy in patients with neuroendocrine tumors and other neoplasms. An understanding of the physiologic distribution of somatostatin receptors, patterns of nonmalignant SSTR expression as well as the technical factors that influence lesion intensity are essential for accurate reporting of SSTR PET/CT. Here we present a practical guide to SSTR PET/CT, highlighting important biological concepts and common pitfalls to assist with accurate reporting.

papers.title: Multicenter case series of pulmonary sclerosing pneumocytoma coinciding with typical carcinoid: Shared AKT1 p.E17K mutation in mixed-growth lesions.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary sclerosing pneumocytoma (PSP) combined with carcinoid is rare, and the potential pathogenetic relationship between the two tumor components is unclear. This study investigated the clinicopathological characteristics and explored the molecular features common to the two tumors. We collected six cases from three institutions in China (2020-2023), evaluated histopathological and immunophenotypic features, and performed a review of the literature. Three patients displayed spatially segregated dual-tumor lesions, while the other three exhibited intermixed growth morphology. We performed targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS) on microdissected PSP and carcinoid tissue compartments. Genomic profiling identified AKT1 p.E17K across seven lesion compartments among 12 microdissected PSP/carcinoid pairs from six patients. The three patients with mixed-growth lesions (Cases 4-6) exhibited identical mutations in paired PSP and carcinoid compartments, contributing six mutation-positive compartments (6/12). In contrast, of the three patients with spatially separated biphasic lesions, only Case 1 bore the variant exclusively in its PSP compartment, corresponding to the seventh positive compartment (1/12), whereas the matched carcinoid component lacked this variant entirely. After RNA extraction and library quality control, four PSP samples (Cases 1, 2, 4, 5) and three carcinoid samples (Cases 1, 2, 4) were retained; transcriptomic profiling further revealed that, in these eligible cases, the expression patterns of key marker genes (i.e., SYP, NCAM1, and NKX2-1) were highly consistent with the immunohistochemical findings, and that both components shared activation of major oncogenic signaling pathways, including the PI3K/Akt pathway. In these mixed cases, paired PSP and carcinoid components shared AKT1 p.E17K mutations; very few additional somatic driver mutations and copy-number alterations were shared between them. AKT1 p.E17K mutation and shared PI3K/Akt activation suggest a molecular link between PSP and carcinoid in mixed growth lesions. Further studies are needed to clarify the pathogenetic relationship between PSP and carcinoid.

papers.title: Lymph node whole-slide images provide incremental value beyond primary tumors for AI-based pCR prediction in node-positive breast cancer.
papers.abstract: To investigate whether lymph node histopathology provides incremental value for predicting pathological complete response (pCR) beyond the primary tumor in node-positive breast cancer. In this retrospective study of 1812 node-positive breast cancer patients receiving neoadjuvant therapy, we collected paired whole-slide images from primary tumor and lymph node biopsies. We developed a dual-lesion AI framework (DP-Net) integrating predictions from separate primary-tumor (P-Net) and lymph-node (N-Net) models via decision-level fusion, and evaluated its incremental predictive value over P-Net alone. P-Net predicted pCR with moderate accuracy (AUROC 0.793), while N-Net showed similar performance (AUROC 0.781). DP-Net achieved an AUROC of 0.814, significantly outperforming P-Net in internal (P = 0.003) and preliminary external validation (P = 0.016). Multivariable regression confirmed that lymph node information provided independent predictive value beyond P-Net in both cohorts (internal: χ² = 34.749, P < 0.001; external: χ² = 6.428, P = 0.011). An IHC-Age model (age, ER, PR, HER2, Ki-67) achieved an AUROC of 0.855; adding DP-Net improved it to 0.869, significantly outperforming the IHC-Age model alone (P = 0.014) and the model combining IHC-Age features with P-Net (P = 0.034). Attention heatmaps and transcriptomic analysis revealed distinct profiles between primary tumors and lymph node metastases. Lymph node histopathology provides incremental pCR-predictive value beyond the primary tumor model, a benefit that persists when the IHC-Age model is included. Routinely acquired lymph node biopsies may serve as a cost-effective predictive resource for guiding neoadjuvant therapy decisions.

papers.title: Milestone cancer vaccine success leaves hard questions unanswered.
papers.abstract: Messenger RNA vaccine from Merck and Moderna slashes risk of melanoma's return, but why remains unclear.

papers.title: Synchronous presacral schwannoma and carcinoma cervix: A rare diagnostic and therapeutic dilemma.
papers.abstract: Schwannomas are benign, encapsulated tumors originating from Schwann cells of the peripheral nervous system. Pelvic and presacral schwannomas are rare, often clinically silent, and are frequently diagnosed incidentally or when they attain sufficient size to compress adjacent pelvic structures. Synchronous occurrence of a presacral schwannoma with cervical carcinoma in the same patient is exceptionally rare and poses significant diagnostic and management challenges. We present a 65-year-old postmenopausal woman (P7L7A1) who presented with per vaginal bleeding and was subsequently diagnosed with simultaneous FIGO (International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics) Stage IIIB carcinoma cervix and a 5.3 cm presacral pelvic mass. Biopsy of the cervical lesion confirmed squamous cell carcinoma (p16-positive, human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated). Repeat core needle biopsy of the presacral mass, followed by immunohistochemistry demonstrating strong S100 protein and SOX10 positivity, confirmed schwannoma. A multidisciplinary tumor board decided to prioritise treatment of the malignancy. The patient received definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy (EBRT 50.4 Gy + concurrent cisplatin) followed by three sessions of high-dose rate intracavitary brachytherapy (7 Gy per fraction). Post-treatment imaging revealed excellent local response at the cervix, whereas the schwannoma demonstrated interval growth to 6.5 × 6.4 cm. Surgical resection of the schwannoma was planned following adequate recovery from radiation sequelae. This case highlights the importance of thorough diagnostic workup for incidentally detected pelvic masses in patients with gynecological malignancies, the value of multidisciplinary team discussion in prioritising competing pathologies, and the need to carefully consider how treatment of one pathology may affect the future management of the other.
papers.journal: Journal of cancer research and therapeutics

papers.title: An uncommon intraoral mass: A solitary schwannoma of the tongue.
papers.abstract: Schwannomas, also known as neurilemmomas, are benign, encapsulated neoplasms originating from the Schwann cells of the peripheral nerve sheath. While ubiquitous, oral schwannomas are infrequent, accounting for approximately 1% of all head and neck schwannomas. Within the oral cavity, the tongue represents the most common anatomical location, yet it remains a rare clinical finding. We present the case of a 28-year-old male with a 3-month history of a slowly progressive, asymptomatic mass on the right posterior 1/3 rd of his tongue.
papers.journal: Journal of cancer research and therapeutics

papers.title: Postoperative radiotherapy after resection of esophageal small-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: The role of postoperative radiotherapy after resection of esophageal small-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma remains uncertain. We evaluated associations with survival and recurrence while addressing treatment timing, confounding, and treatment-effect heterogeneity. We retrospectively analyzed 127 patients from three centers. Diagnosis required small-cell morphology plus synaptophysin and CD56 positivity. Radiotherapy and adjuvant chemotherapy were modeled as time-dependent exposures. Sensitivity analyses included a 90-day landmark design and propensity-score overlap weighting. Treatment-effect heterogeneity was assessed using interaction terms with Holm correction, and recurrence was analyzed using competing-risk methods. A cohort of 43 patients was analyzed descriptively. Radiotherapy was not associated with overall survival in the adjusted time-dependent model (hazard ratio, 1.472; 95% confidence interval, 0.820-2.641; P = 0.195), the 90-day landmark model (hazard ratio, 1.734; 95% confidence interval, 0.934-3.221; P = 0.081), or the overlap-weighted model (hazard ratio, 1.001; 95% confidence interval, 0.550-1.820; P = 0.999). Adjuvant chemotherapy showed a protective direction without statistical significance after adjustment (hazard ratio, 0.569; 95% confidence interval, 0.230-1.407; P = 0.222). No clinicopathological or biomarker-defined factor significantly modified the radiotherapy-survival association after Holm correction. First-failure patterns differed by radiotherapy status, with lower locoregional and higher distant-failure incidence among treated patients; these associations were descriptive because of residual treatment-selection bias. External-cohort estimates were nonsignificant and nonconfirmatory. This study did not demonstrate an overall survival benefit from postoperative radiotherapy and does not provide evidence supporting its routine use or patient selection based on nodal or biomarker status.
papers.journal: Diseases of the esophagus : official journal of the International Society for Diseases of the Esophagus

papers.title: Metastatic prostate cancer with neuroendocrine differentiation and liver metastases: prognosis and response to platinum-based chemotherapy.
papers.abstract: Neuroendocrine differentiation represents an aggressive prostate cancer subtype with poor prognosis. Platinum-based chemotherapy (PT) is standard of care, yet responses are often short-lived. This study aimed to define histopathological subgroups and identify predictors of survival in patients with liver-metastatic prostate cancer with neuroendocrine differentiation treated with PT. We retrospectively analyzed 950 patients with metastatic prostate cancer treated between 2006 and 2025, identifying 31 patients with neuroendocrine differentiation, liver metastases and PT. Tumors were classified into four subgroups based on the proportion of neuroendocrine features. Clinical characteristics, treatment response, tumor markers, and molecular alterations (TP53, RB1, PTEN, BRCA1/2) were evaluated. Overall survival (OS) was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier estimates and Cox regression. Median OS following PT initiation was 8.5 months. Disease control was achieved in 81% of patients, but responses were transient. Patients with a high proportion of remaining adenocarcinoma features showed the longest median OS (15 months), while pure neuroendocrine subtypes had the poorest outcomes (6-10 months). Osteolytic bone metastases (HR 2.48; 95% CI 1.08-5.72), TP53 loss-of-function variants (HR 2.43; 95% CI 1.14-5.16), and ≥ 2 concurrent alterations in TP53/RB1/PTEN (HR 2.13; 95% CI 1.03-4.41) were associated with inferior OS. Early reduction in liver metastasis size (HR 0.41; 95% CI 0.19-0.89) and decline in LDH (HR 0.50; 95% CI 0.23-1.09) after two treatment cycles predicted improved survival. Metastatic prostate cancer with neuroendocrine differentiation and liver metastases is characterized by extreme aggressiveness. There seems to be only limited durable benefit from PT especially in the presence of pure neuroendocrine morphology and tumor suppressor gene alterations. Therefore, these characteristics seem to be promising criteria to be investigated in larger prospective trials to further validate their clinical implications.

papers.title: 18F-Fluoro-L-dihydroxyphenylalanine positron emission tomography in the initial staging of medullary thyroid carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Accurate initial staging of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) is critical for surgical planning and long-term outcome. While 18F-Fluorodihydroxyphenylalanine Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography (18F-DOPA PET/CT) is well established in the detection of recurrent disease, its role in the preoperative setting remains unclear. This review aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance and clinical relevance of 18F-DOPA PET/CT in the initial staging of MTC. A systematic literature search was performed to identify studies assessing 18F-DOPA PET/CT in treatment-naïve MTC patients. Four studies met the inclusion criteria and were qualitatively analyzed. Data were synthesized focusing on compartment-specific performance, tumor burden, and potential impact on clinical management. 18F-DOPA PET/CT demonstrated good sensitivity for primary tumor detection (86-88%), although performance was limited in microcarcinomas. A marked heterogeneity emerged across anatomical compartments. Sensitivity for central lymph node metastases was consistently low (28-53%), whereas higher values were observed in the lateral neck (57-81%), with high specificity when reported. Diagnostic performance was strongly influenced by tumor burden, with significantly reduced sensitivity in low-volume disease and improved detection in patients with more extensive nodal involvement. The integration of biochemical markers further supported a burden-dependent behavior, with higher calcitonin levels associated with improved imaging performance. In distant staging, 18F-DOPA PET/CT identified metastatic disease in a subset of patients but showed limited sensitivity for small hepatic lesions compared with dedicated MRI. Importantly, improvements in lesion detection did not consistently translate into meaningful changes in surgical management. The role of 18F-DOPA PET/CT in the initial staging of MTC is selective and context-dependent. While it may provide incremental value in patients with higher tumor burden or suspected lateral nodal disease, its limited sensitivity in the central compartment and in low-volume disease prevents its use as a standalone staging modality. Therefore, 18F-DOPA PET/CT should be considered a context-driven adjunct rather than a routine tool, to be integrated within a multimodal imaging strategy rather than used as a standalone staging modality.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Based Classification of Melanoma Using Dermoscopic Images: Comparative Evaluation of Convolutional Neural Network and DenseNet Models.
papers.abstract: For melanoma, an aggressive form of skin cancer, early and accurate detection is critical to improving clinical outcomes. Deep learning-based image analysis has emerged as a promising approach for computer-assisted evaluation of dermoscopic lesions. However, model performance is often affected by limited dataset size, class imbalance, overfitting, and differences in network architecture and optimization strategies. This study was aimed at developing and comparatively evaluating convolutional neural network (CNN) and DenseNet-based deep learning models for automated classification of dermoscopic skin lesion images. The effects of data augmentation, network architecture, optimizer selection, and training duration on classification performance were examined. Publicly available dermoscopic skin lesion images obtained from Kaggle were evaluated using a conventional CNN, DenseNet169, and DenseNet201. The original dataset contained 2357 images representing multiple benign and malignant skin lesion categories. Images were resized to 250×250 pixels, labeled, and randomly partitioned into training and testing sets at an 80:20 ratio. To address class imbalance, image augmentation using transformations, including ±10° shear, was performed, increasing the dataset size to 6857 images, with approximately 500 additional samples generated per class. Models were trained using adaptive moment estimation (Adam) and root mean square propagation (RMSprop) optimizers, and evaluated after 20, 60, and 100 epochs. Performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall (sensitivity), specificity, F1-score, confusion matrices, and training and validation loss. Data augmentation substantially improved model performance and reduced evidence of overfitting compared with the original dataset. On the augmented dataset, DenseNet169 and DenseNet201 achieved accuracy and F1-scores exceeding 94% after 100 epochs, consistently outperforming the conventional CNN. DenseNet169 achieved up to 95% validation accuracy, with only minor performance differences between the Adam and RMSprop optimizers. The CNN showed greater susceptibility to overfitting on the smaller dataset; its F1-score, calculated over the complete dataset, increased from 31% after 20 epochs to 59% after 60 epochs and 87% after 100 epochs before augmentation. Across the comparative experiments, the DenseNet architectures demonstrated more stable validation performance and better generalization following augmentation. DenseNet169 and DenseNet201 demonstrated stronger and more stable classification performance than the conventional CNN for dermoscopic skin lesion classification, particularly after augmentation of the training dataset. Increasing the dataset size and improving class balance led to reduced overfitting and improved model performance. These findings support further investigation of DenseNet-based approaches as potential clinical decision support tools for melanoma and skin lesion assessment. However, prospective evaluation using independent, multicenter datasets and diverse patient populations is required before clinical implementation.

papers.title: Characteristics and Survival of Patients With Colonic Compared to Rectal Neuroendocrine Tumors: A SEER Registry Analysis.
papers.abstract: Colon and rectal neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) have varying disease behaviors, presentations, and outcomes. Rectal NETs are detected early; colonic NETs present later and more aggressively. We compared demographic, tumor, treatment, and survival characteristics of colonic versus rectal NETs. This retrospective cohort study used SEER data (2000-2022) to identify adults with colonic or rectal NETs. Demographic, tumor, and treatment characteristics were compared by tumor site. Five-year overall survival (OS) and cancer-specific survival (CSS) were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier statistics and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. Additional site-specific analyses evaluated stage and treatment patterns by race, ethnicity, and household income. Twenty-four percent of 30 246 patients had colonic NETs, and 76.0% had rectal NETs. Rectal NET patients were younger (55.7 vs. 62.9 years, p < 0.001) and more often Black, Asian, or Hispanic. Colonic NETs were more frequently poorly differentiated (43.9% vs. 7.0%), larger (median 30 vs. 5 mm), and more likely to have liver metastases (27.7% vs. 3.7%). Rectal NETs underwent local excision (92.1%), colonic NETs required colectomy (72.3%). Rectal NETs demonstrated higher 5-year OS (88.8% vs. 55.8%) and CSS (93.8% vs. 58.2%, p < 0.001). Stage III colonic NETs had higher CSS than rectal NETs (67.3% vs. 53.5%, p < 0.001). Colonic and rectal NETs have distinct clinicopathologic profiles, treatment patterns, and stage-specific outcomes. These findings support site-specific evaluation while emphasizing the importance of stage and tumor biology in prognosis.

papers.title: Giant 12 cm Pancreatic Insulinoma: Tumor Evolution, Management, and Pathologic Considerations.
papers.abstract: Insulinomas are characteristically small pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, though giant variants have been reported. We describe a 63-year-old woman who presented with refractory hypoglycemia attributable to an exceptionally large 12 cm pancreatic mass that failed to respond to medical treatment. She was quickly taken for surgical resection, after which hypoglycemia quickly resolved. Histopathologic examination demonstrated a well-differentiated pT3N0 neuroendocrine tumor demonstrating negative staining for insulin and pancreatic and duodenal homeobox 1, with positive staining for insulinoma-associated protein 1, alpha-thalassemia/mental retardation X-linked, and alpha-1-antitrypsin. Repeat imaging showed no tumor recurrence. This case illustrates an uncommon presentation and highlights key immunostains in delineating different insulinoma phenotypes.

papers.title: Endoscopic Ultrasound-Guided Radiofrequency Ablation for an Adrenocorticotropic Hormone-Secreting Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumor on Antiplatelet Therapy.
papers.abstract: Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS)-guided radiofrequency ablation (RFA) has been used for thermal destruction of precancerous insulinomas and nonfunctioning pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (pNETs) by coagulative necrosis. We report a case of a critically ill patient with an adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)-secreting pNET treated with EUS-guided RFA (EUS-RFA) while on a P2Y12 antiplatelet after temporary stabilization on a titratable continuous etomidate infusion. This case demonstrates the novelty of EUS-RFA as a procedural treatment option for functional pNETs in critically ill, nonsurgical candidates on antiplatelet therapy.

papers.title: VIP-Mediated Syndromes: Contrasting Presentations and Multidisciplinary Management of Two Rare Neuroendocrine Tumors.
papers.abstract: Vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP)-secreting tumors are rare neuroendocrine neoplasms that cause severe secretory diarrhea and electrolyte abnormalities. We describe 2 atypical cases requiring multidisciplinary care. One patient had a VIP-secreting pheochromocytoma with elevated VIP and metanephrine levels; symptoms improved after adrenalectomy. The second had a metastatic small intestinal neuroendocrine tumor with persistent VIP-mediated diarrhea despite debulking and somatostatin analog therapy, complicated by anal fissures, trans-sphincteric perianal fistula, and neuropathic pelvic pain. These cases highlight morbidity and potential complications associated with extrapancreatic VIP hypersecretion and the value of coordinated multidisciplinary management to improve outcomes and quality of life.

papers.title: Mechanism-defined secondary hypertension enables precision diagnosis and treatment: an evidence review.
papers.abstract: Secondary hypertension is under-recognised despite the availability of mechanism-based diagnostic tests and, for several aetiologies, potentially curative or highly targeted therapy. The clinically important question is not only which causes exist, but how reliably mechanisms translate into diagnosis and cause-directed treatment. To systematically synthesise evidence across the principal causes of secondary hypertension using a mechanism → diagnosis → therapy framework; to compare diagnostic performance and cause-directed treatment effects; and to examine concordance between contemporary society guidelines and real-world implementation. This systematic review followed Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020, with diagnostic accuracy reporting informed by PRISMA-DTA. MEDLINE (PubMed), Embase, CENTRAL, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, ClinicalTrials.gov, and the WHO ICTRP were searched from inception to 30 June 2025, supplemented by citation searching. The formal search identified 580 records; after removal of 168 duplicates, 412 records were screened, 106 full-text reports were assessed, and 58 included evidence records were represented across 63 publications. The review was not prospectively registered in PROSPERO. Screening, extraction and structured appraisal were performed by a single reviewer (the first author); therefore, no dual-reviewer agreement statistic was applicable. Risk of bias was appraised with RoB 2, ROBINS-I, QUADAS-2, and AMSTAR 2 as appropriate, and certainty was summarised using GRADE. A targeted post-search surveillance update through 31 July 2026 was used only to contextualise major newly available guidelines and Phase 3 trial reports and did not alter the original PRISMA counts. Primary aldosteronism (PA) is best understood as a continuum of renin-independent aldosterone excess: in Brown et al. [The unrecognized prevalence of primary aldosteronism: a cross-sectional study. Ann Intern Med. (2020) 173:10-20], biochemically overt autonomous aldosterone production was present in 11.3%, 15.7%, 21.6%, and 22.0% across normotensive, stage 1, stage 2, and resistant-hypertension strata, respectively. In unilateral PA, the PASO cohort distinguished complete biochemical success after adrenalectomy (94%; 656/699) from complete clinical success (37%; 259/705), with partial clinical improvement in a further 47%. PATHWAY-2 established spironolactone as the most effective fourth-line drug in resistant hypertension; CORAL, ASTRAL, STAR, and DRASTIC did not support routine revascularisation for stable atherosclerotic renal-artery stenosis; plasma-free metanephrines remained highly sensitive for phaeochromocytoma/paraganglioma; and PA testing in eligible patients with resistant hypertension remained only 1.6%-2.1%. Post-search Phase 3 trials of selective aldosterone synthase inhibition showed approximately 9 mm Hg placebo-corrected office systolic blood pressure reductions, but cardiovascular-outcome benefit has not been established, and electrolyte/renal monitoring remains necessary. Across secondary hypertension, a limited set of pathophysiological effector pathways maps to specific diagnostic tests and cause-directed treatments. The strongest opportunities for clinical gain are earlier recognition of high-yield phenotypes, accurate aetiological subtyping, and implementation of established testing pathways; emerging aldosterone synthase inhibitors expand blood-pressure-lowering options but should not yet be interpreted as proven cardiovascular-outcome therapies.

papers.title: Extrachromosomal circular DNA drives focal amplification of AGAP2-AS1 to promote cutaneous tumorigenesis.
papers.abstract: Extrachromosomal circular DNA (eccDNA) represents a pervasive structural continuum of genomic instability that drives intratumoral heterogeneity; the topography of the eccDNA-encoded non-coding transcriptome remains obscure in ultraviolet (UV)-driven malignancies. We profiled eccDNA from Basal Cell Carcinoma, Inverted Follicular Keratosis, Merkel Cell Carcinoma, and matched adjacent normal tissues using Circle-Seq. Structural data were integrated with the eccDNA Gene Analyzer (ECGA) and The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) clinical cohorts. In vitro siRNA-mediated knockdown assays were used to determine the oncogenic functionality of identified lncRNAs. Circle-Seq revealed genome-wide remodeling of circular DNA with focal hyper-amplification, GC-rich compositional biases, and recurrent hotspots on chromosomes 9, 16, and 20. Integrative screening identified AGAP2-AS1 as a clinically significant, copy-number-associated lncRNA, whose expression correlated with cellular responses to UV radiation and oxidative stress. Depletion of AGAP2-AS1 impaired tumor cell proliferation, migration, and invasion in vitro. The eccDNA landscape serves as a reservoir of functional non-coding elements; focal amplification of AGAP2-AS1 contributes to malignant progression and stress adaptation in cutaneous neoplasia.

papers.title: Genomic Alterations in Pulmonary Carcinoid Tumors: A Targeted Analysis of Gene Rearrangements and Oncogenic Mutations.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary carcinoids (PCs) are rare, well-differentiated, neuroendocrine lung tumors with limited treatment options for advanced disease, underscoring the need for targeted therapies. PCs typically exhibit a low mutational burden. Although MEN1 and chromatin-modifier mutations are known contributors, potentially actionable alterations remain poorly characterized. To better define therapeutic opportunities, we evaluated oncogenic fusions and variants across 17 cancer-associated genes in a large retrospective PC cohort. Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded primary tumors from Helsinki University Hospital (n = 119, collected between 1990 and 2020) were subjected to targeted RNA-based fusion and variant analysis using the Archer FusionPlex Lung v2 assay. The most frequent recurrent genetic rearrangements involved ALK (n = 5), BRAF (n = 3), FGFR2 (n = 3), and NTRK3 (n = 2), each featuring diverse fusion partners. Variant analysis identified BRAF, EGFR, FGFR1, and FGFR3 as the most frequently mutated genes, although only 2.2% (n = 4) of all detected variants were classified as oncogenic. Notably, 66.7% of all oncogenic or likely oncogenic variants occurred in BRAF and EGFR. Oncogenic variants were identified in ALK, BRAF, EGFR, and ERBB2. Although all FGFR1-3 variants were of uncertain significance, their frequency (34.1% of all detected variants), together with the three FGFR2 fusions, suggested that FGFR alterations may be biologically relevant in PCs. Despite the typically muted genomic landscape of PCs, our study revealed a small yet therapeutically relevant subset of alterations. The findings further characterized the molecular profile of PCs and identified potentially actionable molecular subgroups. While these alterations were not associated with disease-specific survival or metastatic status, they support consideration of molecular profiling in selected patients with advanced disease.

papers.title: Bivariate Copula Models With Event-Free Cure Effect for Survival Extrapolations and Individual-Level Correlation Analysis.
papers.abstract: Overall survival (OS) extrapolations from mixture cure models (MCMs) are often sensitive to the cure fraction, which is challenging to estimate when data are immature. Furthermore, in some cancer populations, it may be unreasonable to assume curative effects among patients who are not event-free. We addressed these problems using bivariate copula MCMs to jointly model OS and progression- (PFS) or recurrence-free survival (RFS), with a single event-free cure fraction parameter. We proposed a practical framework for parametric survival copula model selection and interpretation, which involves estimating five representative candidate copula functions and examining OS distributions conditioned on intermediate event times. Bivariate MCMs with event-free cure fraction, based on previously selected marginal distributions, were estimated for two studies of nivolumab with contrasting survival patterns, namely, in previously treated advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (OS-PFS correlation) and resected melanoma (OS-RFS correlation). OS extrapolations from bivariate MCMs with an effective PFS (or RFS) cure fraction were more conservative than from univariate MCMs. Although patient-level OS-PFS/RFS correlation coefficients were sensitive to the copula, model averaging and inspecting estimated conditional OS distributions enabled clinically meaningful inference on the prognostic impact of intermediate events. Bivariate MCMs with event-free cured subpopulation incorporated curative effects into OS extrapolations more cautiously than conventional MCMs, based on a more rapidly maturing composite endpoint. The model is especially useful when OS data are immature and if post-event cure is clinically implausible. Employing alternative copulas that cover archetypal association patterns mitigated model selection bias in patient-level correlation analysis.

papers.title: Investigating Risk Factors for Delayed Melanoma Recurrence Beyond 5 Years Post-Primary Tumor Diagnosis.
papers.abstract: Patients undergoing treatment for cutaneous melanoma are generally considered cured after a period of 5 years, since most recurrences manifest within three to 5 years. However, some patients can present with a delayed recurrence of melanoma beyond a 10-year timeframe. To identify clinicopathologic factors associated with survival in patients with cutaneous melanoma who developed metastatic recurrence at least 5 years after primary diagnosis. We conducted a retrospective single-center cohort study of 30 patients with cutaneous melanoma developing metastatic recurrence at least 5 years post-diagnosis. The cohort contained 18 women and 12 men (mean age 50.2; range 25-76). Variables included age, sex, BRAF status, site, melanoma subtype, Breslow thickness, ulceration, Clark level, regression, and recurrence localization. Overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), and post-recurrence survival (PRS) were evaluated via Cox proportional hazards models. Mean OS, PFS, and PRS were 168.7, 130.4, and 43.7 months, respectively. Eight patients (27%) died. Tumors averaged 2.61 mm Breslow thickness; 50.0% were BRAF-mutant, 53.3% ulcerated, and 50.0% truncal. Recurrences were locoregional (cutaneous, subcutaneous, in-transit, nodal) in eight (26.7%) and distant in 21 (70.0%); one lacked data. Female sex predicted better univariate OS (HR 0.055, 95% CI 0.01-0.47; p = 0.008) and multivariate PFS (HR 0.364, 95% CI 0.14-0.93; p = 0.035). Increasing age predicted shorter multivariate PFS (HR 1.072, 95% CI 1.03-1.12; p = 0.001). Histologic regression (HR 3.557, 95% CI 1.04-12.17; p = 0.043) and BRAF status (HR 0.413, 95% CI 0.18-0.94; p = 0.034) independently impacted PFS. Kaplan-Meier showed longer OS and PFS in women, and longer PFS in patients younger than 50 years. Delayed recurrence can manifest over a decade post-diagnosis. Female sex and younger age correlate with favorable survival. These findings underscore the necessity of continued clinical vigilance and patient counseling beyond 10 years, although larger cohorts are needed to validate late-recurrence risk stratification.

papers.title: [Application of masseteric-to-facial nerve trunk transfer in complete facial paralysis after lateral skull base tumor surgery: an anatomical-based analysis and clinical outcome evaluation].
papers.abstract: Objectives: To evaluate the anatomical feasibility of masseteric-to-facial nerve trunk transfer and obtain the relevant anatomical parameters, and to assess the surgical feasibility and functional outcomes of this technique in complete facial paralysis following lateral skull base tumor surgery. Methods: The first phase is an anatomical cadaveric study. A total of eight masseteric-to-facial nerve trunk transfers were performed on four cadavers to obtain the anatomical measurements and establish a standardized surgical procedure. The second phase was a retrospective clinical case series study. Thirty-eight patients with complete facial paralysis after lateral skull base tumor surgery who underwent masseteric-to-facial nerve trunk transfer at the Department of Neurosurgery, the Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine, between March 2023 and March 2025 were included. There were 12 males and 26 females, with an age (M(IQR)) of 47(22)years (range:26 to 70 years). The underlying pathologies included vestibular schwannoma (n=24), paraganglioma (n=5), cholesteatoma (n=3), facial nerve schwannoma (n=3), cavernous hemangioma (n=2), and meningioma (n=1). The duration of facial paralysis was 12(10)months (range:3 to 72 months). Perioperative complications were recorded. Facial nerve function before surgery and 12 months after surgery was evaluated using the House-Brackmann (HB) grade, the electronic clinician-graded facial function scale (eFACE), and oral commissure movement measurements. Pre-and postoperative outcomes were compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test or McNemar test. Results: In the anatomical study, the median distance between the rotated facial nerve trunk and the masseteric nerve was 1.0(0.5)cm (range:0.4 to 1.4 cm). After complete mobilization of the inferior division of the facial nerve, tension-free coaptation between the facial nerve trunk and the masseteric nerve was achieved, with a median overlap distance of -0.4(-0.2)cm(range:-0.6 to -0.2 cm). In the 38 clinical cases, surgical failure occurred in 2 patients (5.3%), both of whom had severe trigeminal nerve dysfunction following the initial tumor surgery. Two patients (5.3%) developed postoperative salivary fistula, which resolved with conservative management. Among the remaining 36 successfully reconstructed patients, the median HB grade improved from 6(0) (range:4 to 6) preoperatively to 3(1) (range:2 to 4) at 12 months postoperatively (Z=-5.362, P<0.01). The number of patients able to achieve complete forceful eye closure increased from 6 preoperatively to 31 postoperatively (χ2=23.040,P<0.01). The time to initial and obvious oral commissure movement was 108(43)d (range:51 to 218 d) and 160(75)d (range: 77 to 457 d), respectively. Significant improvements were observed in both static and dynamic eFACE scores (all P<0.01).
