The synkinesis score decreased from 100(0) to 90(5) (Z=-4.760,P<0.01), indicating only mild postoperative synkinesis. FACE-gram analysis demonstrated significant increases in dynamic oral commissure excursion and excursion amplitude after surgery (all P<0.01). Conclusions: Masseteric-to-facial nerve trunk transfer is a feasible reconstructive option for complete facial paralysis following lateral skull base tumor surgery. This technique significantly improves both static and dynamic facial function, restores oral commissure movement, and provides additional recovery of eyebrow elevation and eye closure without causing severe synkinesis. In patients with concomitant facial sensory deficits, careful preoperative evaluation of donor nerve function is recommended to reduce the risk of surgical failure.
papers.journal: Zhonghua wai ke za zhi [Chinese journal of surgery]

papers.title: Recent advances in the management of gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors.
papers.abstract: Gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors are becoming increasingly common, and surgeons are an important part of the multidisciplinary management team. As such, it is important to recognize the roles of surgery, medical and endocrine therapies, and nuclear medicine treatments for these patients. Many advances have been made in the past decade, and this article will highlight some of the more meaningful recent developments in the field.

papers.title: Clinical contribution of the PANOMEN-3 classification in predicting prognosis in pituitary neuroendocrine tumor.
papers.abstract: Pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs) are heterogeneous intracranial neoplasms with variable clinical behavior. Reliable prognostic tools are needed for postoperative risk stratification. We aimed to evaluate the prognostic performance of the PANOMEN-3 classification in a real-world surgical cohort of patients with PitNETs. This single-center retrospective observational cohort study included 92 consecutive adult patients with histologically confirmed PitNETs who underwent pituitary surgery at a tertiary academic center in northern Portugal between 2017 and 2024. Postoperative PANOMEN-3 scores were calculated from clinical, biochemical, radiological and histopathological variables. Progression-free survival (PFS) was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier curves (log-rank test) and Cox proportional hazards regression. Median follow-up was 69 months (IQR 36). Postoperatively, 5.4% of patients were classified as grade 0, 27.2% as grade 1, 57.6% as grade 2 and 9.8% as grade 3. Increasing PANOMEN-3 grade was associated with progressively shorter PFS (log-rank p < 0.001). Median PFS was not reached for grades 0 and 1, was 43 months (95% CI 10-NR) for grade 2, and only 5 months (95% CI 1-NR) for grade 3. On multivariate Cox regression, grade 2 tumors showed a more than 6-fold increase in progression risk (HR 6.13; 95% CI 2.15-17.51; p = 0.001) and grade 3 tumors an approximately 15-fold increase (HR 15.58; 95% CI 4.32-56.26; p < 0.001), compared with grades 0-1 combined. Gender and age were not independently associated with outcome. The PANOMEN-3 classification effectively stratified postoperative progression risk in surgically treated PitNETs, supporting its role in personalized postoperative surveillance and treatment planning.

papers.title: Ionic liquid-mediated cellular loading for whole tumor cell vaccines.
papers.abstract: Conventional whole tumor cell cancer vaccines have demonstrated limited clinical success due to insufficient immunogenicity and challenges in adjuvant codelivery, despite their rich antigen repertoire and high patient-specific activity. Here, we introduce a simple, single-step approach to load immunostimulatory CpG oligodeoxynucleotides into tumor cells undergoing immunogenic cell death using an ionic liquid-containing cocktail. Results indicate that these adjuvant-loaded tumor cells (referred to as IL-Vax) enhance the uptake of cell-based vaccines by dendritic cells and their subsequent activation, leading to potent antitumor immunity. IL-Vax offered strong protection against tumor growth in a prophylactic B16F10 melanoma mouse model. Furthermore, IL-Vax synergized with PD-1 blockade to slow tumor growth and extend survival in a therapeutic model. The modularity of IL-Vax enables the loading of different cargos or cargo combinations, which may be conducive for additional tailoring of such vaccines and potentially other cell loading applications.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

papers.title: Molecular landscape of metastatic bronchial neuroendocrine tumors.
papers.abstract: Metastatic bronchial neuroendocrine tumors (MBNET) are rare and poorly characterized. Understanding their molecular landscape is crucial. This pilot study aimed to identify key genetic and epigenetic alterations in MBNET using large scale genomic analyses to uncover potential therapeutic targets. and Methods: Ten patients diagnosed with MBNET and treated at Institut Curie between 2016 and 2021 were included after giving consent. Targeted DNA sequencing, RNAseq and methylation profiling were conducted on formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) and frozen metastatic tissues. Data were analyzed using bioinformatics pipelines to assess genetic mutations, transcriptional alterations and methylation patterns. Mutations in epigenetic regulators genes, including MEN1 (20%), ARID1A (20%), KMT2B (10%) and KMT2C (10%) were identified, along with additional mutations in MGA (30%) and EIF1AX (20%). Transcriptomic analysis revealed significant differential expression of neuroendocrine-related genes (SSTR1, SSTR2, CHGA, and CHGB) in epigenetic regulator mutated tumors, showing an association with neuroendocrine phenotype regulation. Gene set enrichment analysis highlighted upregulation in neuroactive ligand-receptor interaction and cytokine signaling pathways. Methylation analysis showed a distinct clustering of MEN1-mutated tumors, with differential methylation in various cancer genes, including IKBKE, WNT3A, MYOD1, DNMT3A and ZNRF3. Our pilot study highlights an association between epigenetic alterations and molecular features of MBNET, with potential therapeutic implications that warrant further investigation. The higher expression of somatostatin receptors and neuroendocrine markers observed in tumors harboring epigenetic alterations provides a potential rationale for further investigation of targeted therapies. Further research is needed to explore the role of epigenetic modifications in MBNET progression and treatment response.

papers.title: Neuroendocrine Differentiation Mediates Escape from HER2-Targeted Therapy in Breast Cancer.
papers.abstract: Neuroendocrine differentiation (NED) promotes lineage plasticity and therapy resistance in prostate and lung cancers. Here we identify NED as a route of treatment escape in breast cancer: neuroendocrine features emerged or increased in 22% of progressive cases, predominantly, but not exclusively, in HER2-positive subtype. Using patient-derived, epithelial/neuroendocrine organoid and xenograft models, we map the epigenetic and transcriptional divergence between epithelial and neuroendocrine states arising from a shared mutational background and define a breast cancer neuroendocrine signature. NED involves epigenetic silencing of EpCAM and amplified HER2, while NEUROD1 functions as a master transcriptional regulator of the neuroendocrine fate. NCAM-positive putative circulating tumor cells were detected in patients in whom EpCAM-based detection had failed. Neuroendocrine tumor cells exhibit an FGFR1 dependency associated with NCAM-FGFR1 interaction and mesenchymal FGFR1 splicing. Together, these findings establish NED as a mechanism of escape from HER2-targeted therapy in breast cancer, with implications for disease monitoring and intervention.

papers.title: Oncogenic Role of PLOD3 in Melanoma Progression via Wnt/β-catenin Signaling and Tumor Microenvironment Reprogramming.
papers.abstract: Melanoma is an aggressive malignancy, and treatment strategies remain limited for patients with advanced disease, highlighting the need for a better understanding of the driving mechanisms. This study aimed to identify genes associated with melanoma tumorigenesis, characterize their potential mechanisms, and explore the therapeutic relevance and druggability of selected candidates through experimental and computational approaches. Melanoma-related hub genes were screened by integrating weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) with least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression analysis. The biological functions of the candidate gene were validated using proliferation and migration assays in melanoma cells. RNA sequencing was applied to investigate the underlying molecular mechanism, whereas CIBERSORT and xCell analyses were used to investigate the relationship between PLOD3 and immune infiltration. Structure-based virtual screening was performed to explore candidate PLOD3-binding compounds. PLOD3, C4orf48, BUB1, and CD300LF were identified as a melanoma-related gene signature, among which PLOD3 exhibited the strongest association with melanoma progression and metastasis. PLOD3 was significantly upregulated in melanoma and positively correlated with epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) signatures across multiple independent cohorts. Loss-of-function experiments revealed reduced proliferation, migration, and invasion of melanoma cells following PLOD3 depletion. PLOD3 expression was also associated with Wnt/β-catenin pathway activity, and treatment with a pharmacological Wnt/β-catenin activator partially restored the cellular phenotypes suppressed by PLOD3 silencing. Furthermore, elevated PLOD3 expression was associated with reduced CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Structure-based virtual screening identified four candidate compounds-Rosamultin, Actein, Temsirolimus, and Punicalagin-with strong predicted binding affinity to the catalytic glycosyltransferase (GT) domain of PLOD3, supporting its target potential. PLOD3 functions as a critical driver of melanoma progression by promoting Wnt/β-catenin signaling and shaping an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. These findings identify PLOD3 as a promising therapeutic target and provide candidate compounds for further investigation in melanoma-targeted therapy.

papers.title: Outcomes of Chemoimmunotherapy in Metastatic Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Carcinoma: A Single-Center Clinicopathologic Study.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic neuroendocrine carcinomas (PanNECs) are a rare, aggressive subtype of pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms. Based upon similarities to small cell lung cancer (SCLC), advanced PanNECs are commonly treated with platinum and etoposide chemotherapy; however, outcomes remain poor. Although first-line chemoimmunotherapy has improved survival in SCLC, its role in PanNEC is not well defined. We report on a retrospective cohort of 13 patients with metastatic PanNEC treated at Memorial Sloan Kettering with either first-line combined chemoimmunotherapy or first-line chemotherapy alone. In the first-line metastatic setting, patients who received chemoimmunotherapy (N = 5) demonstrated longer median progression-free survival (17.0 months vs. 2.8 months, P = 0.002) and overall survival (31.0 months vs. 16.0 months, P = 0.031) compared with those who received chemotherapy alone (N = 8). In the second line or later setting, five patients received immunotherapy-containing regimens with a median progression free survival of only 3.0 months (95% confidence interval 1.4 months, Not Reached). Radiologic responses observed in patients receiving chemoimmunotherapy in the first-line metastatic setting were 2 complete responses and 3 partial responses. Germline variants included one patient with a BRCA2 mutation, one patient with co-existing BRCA2 and ATM mutations, and one patient with a MUTYH mutation. Exploratory genomic analyses showed common mutations in TP53, RB1, and KRAS, low tumor mutational burden, and microsatellite stability. Exploratory multiplex immunofluorescence demonstrated heterogenous immune cell infiltrates without a consistent biomarker pattern associated with response. In this single-center cohort, early incorporation of chemoimmunotherapy in PanNEC was associated with improved survival. These findings are hypothesis-generating and support prospective, multicenter evaluation of first-line chemoimmunotherapy strategies in PanNEC (SWOG S2012, NCT05058651) [1].

papers.title: Diagnosis and management of thyroid cancer in adult patients. Recommendations of Polish Scientific Societies and the National Oncology Strategy, 2026 update.
papers.abstract: The current update of the "Recommendations for the Management of Thyroid Cancer in Adult Patients" is based on a critical appraisalof whether the recommendations published in 2022 by the Polish Scientific Societies and the National Oncology Strategy remain valid,and which statements require modification or updating in light of the American Thyroid Association (ATA) Guidelines published in 2025. We have also taken into account the most recent National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) recommendations, as well as guidelines from other international and European scientific societies addressing thyroid cancer, adapting them to the specific epidemiologicaland legal conditions in Poland. We decided that the current Recommendations would not include management of medullary thyroid cancer, as, in our opinion, the Polish Guidelines published in 2022 and 2024 remain up to date. The Recommendations are divided into two sections: "General Principles" and "Clinical Management". The "General Principles" sectionoutlines the key principles of thyroid cancer management, whereas the "Clinical Management" section specifies these principlesaccording to the risk of recurrence, incorporating the well-established and highly accurate ATA 2025 risk stratification system. Thus,the reader will find specific management recommendations depending on whether the patient has low-risk or high-risk thyroid cancer. The "Clinical Management" section includes a dedicated subsection outlining the recommended clinical approach to thyroid noduleswith indeterminate cytology. In these Recommendations, the management of anaplastic thyroid carcinoma and thyroid lymphomas is addressed in a separate subsection. In addition, brief information on other rare histological subtypes of thyroid cancer is also provided.

papers.title: Melanoma of the Scalp Harboring a Novel AGFG1::ERBB4 Fusion: A Case Report With Clinicopathologic and Genomic Characterization.
papers.abstract: ERBB4 (HER4) gain-of-function missense mutations have been implicated in cutaneous melanoma. In contrast, structural rearrangements involving ERBB4 are exceedingly rare. We describe a 59-year-old man with a rapidly enlarging 4.2-cm melanoma of the scalp with high-risk pathologic features, including epithelioid to plasmacytoid cytomorphology, ulceration, brisk mitotic activity, and microscopic satellitosis. RNA sequencing identified a novel in-frame AGFG1::ERBB4 fusion joining AGFG1 exon 2 to ERBB4 exon 2. The ERBB4 portion retains the downstream coding sequence, including the tyrosine kinase domain. Concurrent molecular alterations included a pathogenic NF1 loss-of-function alteration, a TERT promoter mutation, CDK4 and STAT6 copy-number gains, and TP53 copy-number loss in a BRAF/NRAS/KIT-wild-type background.

papers.title: Epidemiological, Clinicopathological, and Molecular Features of Melanoma in Oman: A single-institution study.
papers.abstract: Published data on melanoma in Oman are scarce. This study aimed to describe epidemiological, clinicopathological and molecular characteristics of melanoma patients in a single institution in Oman. This retrospective study included patients with a histopathological diagnosis of invasive melanoma who were assessed at Sultan Qaboos Comprehensive Cancer Care and Research Centre, Muscat, Oman, between July 2021 and February 2025. Data on patient demographics, comorbidities, melanoma type, localisation, stage, key histopathological and molecular characteristics were extracted from electronic clinical charts and quantitatively described. A total of 31 patients were included. The median age at diagnosis was 52.9 years (interquartile range [IQR]: 41.6-66.0). Patients from the Middle East comprised 90.3% of the cohort (n = 28), while Western individuals accounted for 9.7% (n = 3). Cutaneous melanoma was the most frequent type, observed in 83.9% of cases (n = 26), followed by ocular melanoma in 6.5% (n = 2). Mucosal melanoma, central nervous system melanoma and melanoma of unknown primary site were each found in 3.2% of patients (n = 1 each). Among cutaneous melanomas, acral and skin non-acral subtypes were equally represented, each comprising 41.9% (n = 13). Staging data were available for 27 patients; Stage III was the most common at presentation (40.7%, n = 11), followed by Stage II (29.6%, n = 8) and Stages I and IV (14.8%, n = 4 each). The median tumour mutational burden (TMB) was 4.95 mutations per megabase (IQR: 3.86-6.4). Activating BRAF mutations were detected in 35.0% of tested patients (n = 7/20). Brisk tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes were present in 28.6% of evaluated cases (n = 4/14). Early-stage diagnosis was uncommon. Acral and sun-unexposed non-acral melanoma subtypes were highly prevalent and median TMB was low. These findings suggest that clinicopathological and molecular features of melanoma in Oman may differ from those in Western and Asia-Pacific countries, with potential implications for treatment and prevention strategies.

papers.title: Cannabis sativa L. extract modulates UVB-induced oxidative stress and MITF transcriptional suppression in B16-F10 melanoma cell line.
papers.abstract: Ultraviolet B (UVB) radiation disrupts skin homeostasis through reactive oxygen species (ROS)-mediated oxidative stress and melanogenic imbalance. The search for effective exogenous photoprotectants has highlighted natural products, including Cannabis sativa L. phytocannabinoids with reported antioxidant activity. However, their role in UVB-induced cellular responses remains to be clarified. Chemical profiling was performed using LC-QTOF-MS and Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy. Biological activities were assessed in B16-F10 pigmented melanoma cells, including cytotoxicity (MTT assay), intracellular ROS generation (DCFDA assay), transcriptional regulation of melanogenic markers (MITF, TYR, TYRP1, TYRP2) by RT-qPCR, and functional melanogenesis outcomes (tyrosinase activity and melanin content). LC-QTOF-MS revealed that the extract was dominated by neutral cannabinoids, with Δ⁹-tetrahydrocannabinol (Δ⁹-THC) and cannabinol (CBN) as major putatively identified constituents based on relative peak area. The extract showed moderate free radical scavenging activity in a cell-free DPPH assay. Importantly, pre-treatment with the extract significantly reduced UVB-induced intracellular ROS accumulation. UVB exposure resulted in suppression of MITF mRNA expression, which was partially restored at higher extract concentrations, whereas transcript levels of TYR, TYRP1, and TYRP2 remained largely unchanged under the experimental conditions. Functionally, the extract attenuated UVB-induced tyrosinase activity at the highest concentration tested, while total melanin content was not significantly altered. Collectively, these findings suggest that a neutral cannabinoid-rich C. sativa extract (CSE) can mitigate UVB-induced oxidative stress and partially restore transcriptional regulation of MITF without inducing significant acute depigmentation. The extract may represent a candidate for further investigation as a bioactive component that may support skin cell homeostasis regarding its potential antioxidant-mediated photoprotective activity in dermatological formulations targeted at photo-oxidative stress.

papers.title: Unusual [18F]FDOPA PET-CT maging of insulinomas in children.
papers.abstract: Insulinomas are rare pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours, causing recurrent episodes of hypoglycaemia. Accurate localisation is essential for surgical management, yet imaging remains challenging. This case series presents unusual findings of paediatric insulinomas on [18F]-dihydroxyphenylalanine ([18F]FDOPA) positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) imaging. We retrospectively reviewed medical notes and investigations of histologically proven paediatric insulinoma cases (n=4) presenting to Royal Manchester Children's Hospital between 2008 and 2024. All patients underwent [18F]FDOPA PET-CT as part of their diagnostic workup. Imaging findings were analysed, with particular attention to tracer uptake patterns. Contrary to the increased tracer uptake typically seen in neuroendocrine tumours, three of the four insulinomas demonstrated focal photopenia at the site of the tumour on [18F]FDOPA PET-CT. Only one case showed increased uptake, suggesting a predominance of reduced, rather than enhanced, tracer activity in paediatric insulinomas CONCLUSION: Photopenia on [18F]FDOPA PET-CT may be a more frequent finding than increased uptake in paediatric insulinomas. Recognizing this atypical pattern is important for accurate tumour localisation before surgical management. Further studies are needed to validate these findings and find a mechanistic explanation.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence (AI) in melanocytic lesions diagnosis: a systematic review of methods incorporating ABCD(E)-derived features.
papers.abstract: Melanoma has a growing incidence, and early and accurate detection can enhance survival rates. However, its complex diagnoses pose challenges that could be overcome by Artificial Intelligence (AI), and the ABCD(E) rule (Asymmetry, Border irregularity, Color variegation, Diameter, and Evolution) is a major screening pattern enabling melanoma detection. This systematic review assessed advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI) for melanoma diagnosis, particularly focusing on systems incorporating or informed by ABCD(E) criteria. Guided by Cochrane and PRISMA guidelines, this review included experimental or observational studies indexed on PubMed, LILACS, Latindex, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials platforms. Independent screening and data extraction were performed by two authors. 2,735 records were assessed and 21 studies were included in the final screening, analyzing over 90,000 images/cases. AI systems, notably CNNs and DCNNs, demonstrated promising diagnostic performance, often matching or exceeding human expert evaluation, achieving an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 90.3% for early melanoma differentiation. Patient selection bias was observed, limiting applicability of the findings. AI shows significant and evolving capability in skin lesion diagnosis, increasingly integrating ABCD(E) criteria. While offering enhanced diagnostic consistency, challenges persist, including data limitations, model generalizability, and interpretability.
papers.journal: Journal of cancer research and clinical oncology

papers.title: Thyroid surveillance practices in GLP-1 receptor agonist use and its potential influence on thyroid cancer detection: A scoping review.
papers.abstract: Rodent data prompted a boxed warning for medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), yet human findings remain inconsistent and may reflect how intensively patients are screened. We mapped reported thyroid screening practices and detection bias reporting. Following JBI methodology and PRISMA-ScR reporting guidance, we searched PubMed, Scopus, Embase, CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov from 2010 to July 2026. Empirical studies and trial registry records reporting thyroid screening in adult GLP-1RA users were eligible. Records were charted and synthesised descriptively. Thirty-nine records were included (29 published studies, 10 registry records). Screening was predominantly biochemical. Calcitonin was reported in 16/29 studies (55.2%) and all registry records, whereas ultrasonography was reported in 13/29 (44.8%) and no trials. 19/29 studies (65.5%) described a screening protocol. Screening intensity was reported in 18/29 (62.1%) but detection bias in 11/29 (37.9%). All registry records excluded personal or family history of MTC or multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 before screening. Thyroid screening in GLP-1RA users is heterogeneous, calcitonin-centred, and inconsistently reported, while patients at highest C-cell risk are excluded from trials. Detection bias is seldom addressed despite documented increases in imaging. Standardised reporting of screening intensity is needed to interpret thyroid cancer rates. OSF Protocol Registration Code: 10.17605/OSF.IO/PEBHS.

papers.title: To Transplant or Not to Transplant: The Ethical Dilemma of Kidney Transplantation in Low-Risk Medullary Thyroid Cancer.
Increased risk of hypocalcemia and RLN injury in patients with medullary thyroid carcinoma after thyroidectomy.
papers.abstract: In general, patients with medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) undergo total thyroidectomy and central neck dissection (CND), whereas only select patients with differentiated thyroid carcinoma (DTC) receive CND. The ACS NSQIP targeted thyroidectomy dataset (2016-2024) was queried for adults with MTC or DTC undergoing total thyroidectomy. Rates of CND, lateral neck dissection (LND) and postoperative complications were compared. Among 23,337 patients, 444 (1.9%) had MTC and 22,893 (98.1%) had DTC. CND was performed more frequently in MTC than DTC (72.1% vs 40.1%, p < 0.01). MTC patients had higher rates of hypocalcemia within 30 days (11.5% vs 6.8%, p < 0.01) and recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) injury/dysfunction (10.4% vs 6.4%, p < 0.01). After adjustment for CND and LND, MTC remained associated with hypocalcemia (OR 1.44, p = 0.03). Patients with MTC have higher rates of post-operative hypocalcemia and RLN injury than those with DTC. MTC remained independently associated with hypocalcemia within 30 days even after accounting for differences in operative extent.

papers.title: Toward risk-adapted surgical de-escalation in sporadic medullary thyroid carcinoma: Integrating desmoplastic stromal reaction, nodal status, and multifocality.
papers.abstract: Risk-adapted de-escalation in sporadic medullary thyroid carcinoma requires identification of patients in whom lymph-node dissection and thyroid preservation can be safely modulated. Desmoplastic stromal reaction predicts nodal metastases, but whether desmoplastic stromal reaction, nodal status, and multifocality can be integrated into a staged clinical decision framework remains unclear. This retrospective cohort study included adults with sporadic medullary thyroid carcinoma undergoing index surgery between January 2018 and March 2026 at a referral endocrine surgery center. Factors associated with lymph node metastases, multifocality, and the pN0-unifocal phenotype were assessed using univariable analyses and exploratory machine-learning models. Among 331 patients operated for medullary thyroid carcinoma, 94 met inclusion criteria. Lymph node metastases were present in 29 patients (30.9%). All node-positive tumors were desmoplastic stromal reaction positive, whereas no desmoplastic stromal reaction-negative tumor had lymph node metastases (P < .001). Lymph node metastases were also associated with higher basal calcitonin and carcinoembryonic antigen, larger tumor diameter, male sex, advanced pT category, high-grade medullary thyroid carcinoma, extrathyroidal extension, vascular invasion, and multifocality. Multifocality occurred in 14 patients (14.9%) and was associated with male sex, advanced pT category, lymph node metastases, and extrathyroidal extension. The pN0-unifocal phenotype was associated with female sex, lower biochemical markers, absence of desmoplastic stromal reaction, smaller tumor diameter, absence of extrathyroidal extension, and absence of vascular invasion. Desmoplastic stromal reaction negativity identifies negligible nodal risk but does not exclude occult contralateral disease. We propose a staged clinical decision framework integrating preoperative selection with intraoperative pathologic assessment to explore thyroid preservation in highly selected patients. This framework is hypothesis generating and requires prospective validation.

papers.title: Optimizing inferior petrosal sinus sampling: results of a multicenter study.
papers.abstract: Inferior petrosal sinus sampling (IPSS) confirms a central source of adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) secretion in Cushing's disease (CD). We explored IPSS protocols to optimize diagnostic sensitivity and reduce laboratory testing burden. Patients from the multicenter Registry of Adenomas of the Pituitary and Related Disorders (RAPID) who underwent IPSS for management of CD, and in whom central:peripheral (C:P) ACTH levels were evaluated, were included. A total of 93 patients (mean age 44 ± 13 years, 17% male; 78% MRI-negative, 84% long-term remission) were analyzed. At baseline, 77% of patients showed a C:P ACTH ratio ≥2X, and all of these patients reached ≥3X C:P ACTH after stimulation. Among patients with a baseline ratio <2X, 57% (n = 12/21) crossed the ≥3X threshold after stimulation, prolactin normalization confirmed one additional patient, with two further patients remaining indeterminate. Stimulation produced 3.1-, 2.8-, and 1.9-fold increases in C:P ACTH at 2, 5, and 10 min post-stimulation, respectively, with the best response at 2-5 min. Cumulatively, 77%, 79%, 88%, 90%, and 91% of patients met criteria for CD by 0, 2, 5, 10, and 15 min, respectively. In this confirmed-CD cohort these proportions represent test sensitivity, rising from 77.4% (95% CI 67.6-85.4%) at baseline to 91.4% (95% CI 83.8-96.2%) by 15 min. Because all patients had surgically confirmed CD, these values reflect test sensitivity rather than overall diagnostic accuracy. Diagnostic yield plateaued by 15 min with negligible gain thereafter, and baseline together with a limited number of early post-stimulation samples captured most cases. These retrospective, hypothesis-generating findings suggest that a streamlined protocol may reduce laboratory and interpretive burden while preserving sensitivity, pending prospective validation.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia

papers.title: Genomic Landscape of Gastroenteropancreatic Neuroendocrine Neoplasms Using Panel Sequencing.
papers.abstract: The clinical utility of genomic profiling in gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (GEP-NENs) remains incompletely defined, particularly for clinically relevant annotated alterations and prognostic stratification. We performed a multi-institutional analysis to characterize genomic alterations across GEP-NEN subtypes, generate prevalence estimates to inform precision oncology efforts, and evaluate associations with clinical actionability and survival. We performed a retrospective analysis of 1,691 GEP-NENs from the American Association for Cancer Research Project Genomics Evidence Neoplasia Information Exchange database. Tumors were classified into neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) or neuroendocrine carcinomas (NECs) and stratified by primary site. Genomic alterations, including single-nucleotide variants, insertions/deletions, copy number alterations, and structural variants, were analyzed using a panel-adjusted approach. Alterations were annotated for clinical relevance using multiple knowledge bases. Overall survival was evaluated in a subset (n = 502) with available data. Genomic alterations were identified in 86.5% of patients. NETs were enriched for alterations in chromatin-remodeling genes (MEN1, DAXX) and mTOR pathway regulator TSC2, whereas NECs were characterized by canonical drivers (TP53, RB1, KRAS, APC, and BRAF). Annotated alterations were identified in 34.1% of all patients, with higher rates in NECs compared with NETs (74.4% v 28.5%, P < .001). Notable annotated targets included BRAF V600E (2.2%; 14.8% of all colorectal NECs), KRAS-activating mutations (6.8%; 0.35% G12C), and NTRK fusions (0.2%). Annotation rates varied by primary site with the highest rates observed in colorectal, gastric, and esophageal NECs. In NETs, the presence of NEC-associated driver alterations was associated with worse overall survival (hazard ratio, 3.67 [95% CI, 2.49 to 5.42], P < .001). Genomic profiling reveals meaningful differences in biomarker prevalence and prognosis across GEP-NEN subtypes. These findings support integrating genomic profiling with histologic classification to refine risk stratification and inform biomarker-driven clinical trials.

papers.title: Histopathological findings in laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy specimens and their relation to preoperative endoscopy: A retrospective cross-sectional study of 954 patients.
papers.abstract: Laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG) is the most frequently performed bariatric surgery. Although it is generally considered safe, a thorough preoperative assessment is essential to minimize the risk of complications. The need for histopathological examination of resected gastric specimens in bariatric surgery remains a subject of debate, particularly regarding the role of preoperative esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD). This study aimed to determine the prevalence of histopathological findings in resected specimens following sleeve gastrectomy and to assess their agreement with preoperative EGD findings at a tertiary center. This retrospective cross-sectional study examined patients who underwent LSG between 2009 to 2021. The data included demographics, comorbidities, preoperative EGD findings, and routine postoperative histopathology of the resected specimens. Diagnostic accuracy of preoperative EGD was assessed against resected-specimen histopathology. Among the 954 patients who underwent LSG, 67.1% were female, and 84.7% were Saudi nationals. Abnormal histopathological findings were observed in 45.5% (434/954) of the resected specimens, with gastritis being the predominant finding, present in 98.2% (426/434) of these. Preoperative EGD was performed in a subgroup of 357 patients (37.4%); in these, gastritis was the most prevalent EGD finding (50.1%). Helicobacter pylori was identified in 9.5% of patients who underwent preoperative EGD and in 8.0% of all resected specimens. Less common histopathological findings were metaplasia (0.6%), gastrointestinal stromal tumors (0.3%), gastric polyps (0.2%) and grade 1 gastric carcinoid (0.1%). Among the 357 patients who underwent preoperative EGD, sensitivity was 99.5%, specificity 98.3%, positive predictive value 98.4%, negative predictive value 99.4% and accuracy 98.9% against resected-specimen histopathology. Gastritis is the most prevalent histopathological finding in resected specimens following sleeve gastrectomy and on preoperative EGD, although significant pathologies are infrequent. In the selected subgroup of patients who underwent preoperative EGD, a normal EGD showed high agreement with normal histopathology of the resected specimen; these findings do not support omitting histopathological examination of resected specimens, and prospective multicenter studies are needed. Helicobacter pylori was frequently identified and was strongly associated with gastritis in unadjusted analyses; premalignant findings were too few to assess.

papers.title: Correction to: Alternative lengthening of telomeres in small well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors: independent validation and crossplatform concordance.
papers.journal: Virchows Archiv : an international journal of pathology

papers.title: International expert consensus on perioperative management of carcinoid crisis.
papers.abstract: Carcinoid crisis is a critical concern for patients with neuroendocrine tumours undergoing invasive procedures. Guidance is needed to standardize and optimize perioperative care for patients at risk of carcinoid crisis. Consensus-based expert recommendations were developed for the perioperative management of carcinoid crisis among patients with midgut and bronchopulmonary neuroendocrine tumours undergoing non-cardiac surgery. A modified Delphi approach was used with four rounds of voting to reach expert consensus on statements about perioperative management of carcinoid crisis. A multidisciplinary international panel of 44 experts was formed, and 3 patient partners were engaged. Statements addressing preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative considerations were created. Panellists rated statements on a Likert scale (from 1 to 7). Three additional rounds of iterative rating and feedback were completed anonymously. Consensus was defined with median score between 5 and 7, and ≤ 13 panellists rating outside the score category containing the median. Final consensus was reached on 41 statements. Of these, 12 focused on preoperative work-up and optimization, 27 on intraoperative management including monitoring, prophylaxis, and treatment of crisis, and 2 on postoperative management. The principal practice-shifting recommendations were that somatostatin analogues are not necessary for prophylaxis before surgery or on the day of operation, and treatment in the event of carcinoid crisis should start with vasopressors, with short-acting somatostatin analogues used as an adjunct. Using modified Delphi methodology, recommendations to guide the perioperative management of carcinoid crisis were developed. Considering the importance of carcinoid crisis on the management and outcomes of patients undergoing surgical resection for neuroendocrine tumours, this guidance can help standardize care and optimize outcomes.

papers.title: Characterizing bone metastases and skeletal-related events in patients with well-differentiated neuroendocrine neoplasms utilizing 68Gallium-DOTATATE positron emission tomography.
papers.abstract: Tumors of neuroendocrine origin are a heterogenous group of related neoplasms which can arise from anywhere in the body. Neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) are categorized by site of origin, differentiation status and grade (Ki-67 expression and/or mitotic rate), with significant prognostic variability accordingly. Historically, the prevalence of bone metastasis is reported to be 6%-12% based on "first generation" (i.e., 111Indium pentetreotide [Octreoscan®]) somatostatin receptor imaging (SSRI). We conducted a retrospective cohort study including patients with well-differentiated NENs to determine the clinical and imaging characteristics of osseous metastases when evaluated with higher-sensitivity 68Gallium-DOTATATE positron emission tomography (PET) scans, as well as determining fracture prevalence in selected sub-cohorts. We also developed a risk score analysis to assess risk of fracture in this cohort. Four hundred twenty-four patients were identified for inclusion. The median age was 61 years. Most patients were asymptomatic (64%), had sclerotic lesions (77%), Krenning 4 (71%), and had >3 sites (69%) of osseous disease. A high proportion of patients had osseous metastases at sites with high risk for fracture, including vertebra (82%), pelvis (63%), and peri-trochanteric femur (34%). Fifty-seven patients (13%) in the entire cohort suffered a fracture. Fracture prevalence was significantly lower in small bowel neuroendocrine tumors (NETs, 7%) and Grades 1 and 2 disease (8% and 9%, respectively), with higher prevalence in pancreatic NETs, paragangliomas/pheochromocytomas, lung carcinoid, and Grade 3 disease (≥20% for each; p-values <.05). Our study showed that the rate of osseous metastatic disease approximates 20% in well-differentiated NENs. Most bone metastases are asymptomatic and the risk of fracture is variable based on the primary site of disease and tumor grade. Our novel risk score analysis for fracture was designed to assist clinician decision making as to management of bone metastasis in this patient population.

papers.title: Perioperative Glycemic Changes Following Partial Pancreatectomy for a Pancreatic Islet Cell Neoplasm in a Dog: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Canine insulinomas are functional pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors that typically cause hypoglycemia, but blood glucose may fluctuate before surgery and increase after resection. This report describes the diagnostic evaluation, surgical treatment, and perioperative glycemic course of a 12-year-old female Miniature Schnauzer with a pancreatic islet cell neoplasm considered clinically consistent with insulinoma. Intermittent low or low-normal blood glucose concentrations ranging from 54 to 72 mg/dL were documented before surgery, and the blood glucose concentration on the day of surgery was 73 mg/dL. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography identified a mass in the left pancreatic limb, and partial pancreatectomy was subsequently performed. Blood glucose reached 416 mg/dL 2 h after pancreatic mass removal while surgery was ongoing, then initially declined without insulin administration. Recurrent postoperative hyperglycemia was treated with regular insulin on postoperative days (PODs) 2 and 3, whereas subsequent decreases in blood glucose were treated with dextrose supplementation. Blood glucose continued to fluctuate on POD 4; no additional insulin was administered after POD 3. Histopathologic examination identified a pancreatic islet cell neoplasm. Although a paired serum insulin concentration during documented hypoglycemia was not available and immunohistochemical staining for insulin or other neuroendocrine markers was not performed, the clinical, imaging, glycemic, and histopathological findings were considered consistent with a clinicopathologic diagnosis of insulinoma. Blood glucose was 150 mg/dL on POD 7; subsequent recorded concentrations through POD 150 ranged from 107 to 133 mg/dL. Serial glucose monitoring helped characterize the perioperative course and guide postoperative insulin and dextrose treatment.

papers.title: Prunus mume Extract Cooperates with Cisplatin to Induce Melanoma Apoptosis and Regulate Immune Responses.
papers.abstract: This study investigated the potential of Prunus mume (P. mume) extract as an anticancer adjuvant by evaluating its direct apoptotic effects on A375P human melanoma cells and its immunomodulatory impact on peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). Furthermore, the extract demonstrated additive and chemosensitizing effects when combined with a sub-toxic dose of cisplatin, significantly enhancing the growth inhibition of A375P cells. Selective growth inhibition was confirmed using crystal violet assays, where the 80% ethanol (EtOH) extract exhibited significant dose-dependent inhibition of A375P viability while leaving human adult low-calcium high-temperature keratinocytes (HaCaT) largely unaffected. Apoptotic cell death was characterized by DNA fragmentation and disrupted mitochondrial membrane potential, which decreased to 77.3% of the control as evidenced by JC-1 staining. At the molecular level, quantitative real-time reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) analysis demonstrated the upregulation of pro-apoptotic markers, including Bax (2.08-fold at 30 h) and Caspase-3 (2.12-fold in 16 h floating cells), alongside significant downregulation of the anti-apoptotic gene Bcl-2 (down to 0.10-fold at 16 h adherent cells). Notably, initiator Caspase-9 expression was suppressed in co-treated cells, suggesting late-stage transcriptional attenuation during sustained drug exposure. The extract suppressed the NF-κB pathway and reduced PD-L1 mRNA levels by 2.63-fold (compared to 3.55-fold with cisplatin alone), suggesting a mechanism to mitigate chemo-induced inflammatory stress and immune dysregulation. Furthermore, while cisplatin induced an excessive inflammatory response in PBMCs, co-treatment with the extract normalized the cytokine profile by modulating IFN-γ (2.21-fold), TNF-α (3.37-fold), and IL-2 (1.60-fold) back toward baseline levels. The attenuation of cytotoxic effectors, Granzyme B (1.16-fold) and Perforin (0.73-fold), along with the costimulatory molecule CD80 (4.44-fold), suggests the modulation of excessive inflammatory activation and attenuation of immune hyper-responsiveness. Finally, biomolecular docking predictions using the Boltz-2 framework (an open-source biomolecular interaction prediction model) demonstrated high-affinity binding between key plum constituents (e.g., chlorogenic acid, citric acid) and target proteins such as Caspase-3, Bcl-2, Nrf2, and Keap1, providing a structural basis for their bioactivity. In conclusion, P. mume extract (PME) serves as a promising multi-target adjuvant that simultaneously triggers cancer cell apoptosis while mitigating cisplatin-induced inflammatory perturbations in immune cells.

papers.title: Molecular Mechanisms of the Anticancer Activity of Hinokitiol in C32 Melanoma Cells: Transcriptomic Analysis and Modulation by a Static Magnetic Field.
papers.abstract: Many studies confirm that natural substances derived from plant materials, at appropriate concentrations, can exhibit anticancer effects against various types of cancer cells. One such substance is hinokitiol, which has been proven to have anticancer effects against malignant melanoma. However, the molecular mechanisms of this effect are unknown. Therefore, the aim of this study was to determine the probable molecular mechanism of the anticancer effect of hinokitiol through gene expression analysis. Additionally, it was examined whether a ubiquitous static magnetic field could modify the anticancer properties of hinokitiol. Transcriptome analysis was performed using oligonucleotide microarrays, followed by validation of the obtained results for five genes using RT-qPCR. Fifty-six statistically different transcriptomes were found in melanoma cultures treated with only hinokitiol (p < 0.05, FC > 1.5). To confirm the results obtained from the microarray, RT-qPCR was performed for five genes: the ARNTL, CRYAB, MAT2A, HSPA8 and NR1D1 genes. In summary, our studies indicate that the addition of hinokitiol to melanoma cells changes the expression of numerous genes, including those associated with the biological clock. The presented results are preliminary and point out a direction for future research. The presence of a static magnetic field does not cause statistically significant changes in gene expression. Only in ARNTL was a statistically significant decrease in expression levels observed in the H+SMF group compared to the H group.

papers.title: CCKBR (Gastrin Receptor) as a Theranostic Target in Oncology: Biological Rationale, Diagnostic Imaging, and Next-Generation Peptide-Based Drug Development.
papers.abstract: Cholecystokinin B receptor (CCKBR) is a promising theranostic target because of its overexpression in several malignancies, including medullary thyroid carcinoma, small-cell lung cancer, gastric cancer, and pancreatic cancer. Its high-affinity ligand binding and efficient receptor-mediated internalization provide a strong biological basis for molecular imaging and peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT). Recent advances in radiolabeled gastrin and mini-gastrin analogues have improved tumor targeting, metabolic stability, and pharmacokinetic profiles, supporting their application in both diagnostic imaging and radionuclide therapy. This review summarizes the molecular biology and tumor expression of CCKBR, recent progress in SPECT/PET imaging and targeted radionuclide therapy, and advances in ligand and pharmacokinetic engineering. Despite substantial progress, CCKBR-targeted theranostics remain less clinically established than SSTR- or PSMA-based platforms. Major challenges include heterogeneous receptor expression, renal and gastric uptake, limited prospective clinical evidence, and the lack of standardized imaging, dosimetry, and treatment protocols. Addressing these limitations will be essential for the broader clinical translation of CCKBR-targeted theranostics.

papers.title: Clinical and Demographic Characteristics of Patients with Pulmonary Large-Cell Neuroendocrine Carcinoma: A Single-Center Experience.
papers.abstract: Background and Objectives: Pulmonary large-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (pLCNEC) is a rare malignancy, accounting for approximately 2-3.5% of surgically resected primary lung cancers. Given its rarity, pLCNEC has been less extensively studied than other, more common lung cancer subtypes. In this study, we evaluated and compared the diagnostic and therapeutic approaches to pLCNEC. Materials and Methods: Patients with pLCNEC were evaluated with respect to age, sex, smoking history, primary tumor site, surgical history, tumor stage, histological subtype, metastatic sites at initial diagnosis and during follow-up, first- and second-line chemotherapy regimens, and disease survival parameters. Results: A total of 55 patients diagnosed between 2012 and 2024 were retrospectively analyzed. The median age at diagnosis was 63 years, the mean smoking exposure was 45.8 pack-years, and the median overall survival (mOS) for the entire cohort was 9 months (95% CI, 7-11). At presentation, 12.7% of the patients had stage I-II, 29.1% had stage III, and 58.2% had stage IV disease. Primary tumors were located peripherally in 85.5% of cases and centrally in 14.5%. A platinum plus etoposide regimen-standard for small-cell lung cancer (SCLC)-was the most commonly administered first-line chemotherapy (n = 40). Among all patients, 19 had undergone upfront surgical resection, whereas 36 had not. In univariate analysis, patients with a history of surgery (n = 19) had a significantly longer mOS than those without surgery (n = 36): 16 months (95% CI, 8-NR) versus 7 months (95% CI, 3-9), respectively (p = 0.003). On multivariate analysis, stage IV disease, ECOG PS ≥ 2, and advanced age were independently associated with poorer survival. In multivariable analyses, surgery showed a borderline association with survival that did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.052). Furthermore, median survival was significantly longer in patients with T1 stage disease compared with those with T3 and T4 stage, and in those with T3 compared with T4 stage (p = 0.045). Conclusions: Overall, early-stage diagnosis and surgical intervention may be associated with favorable clinical outcomes and a survival benefit.

papers.title: Pituitary Carcinoma Revisited: A Systematic Review and Individual Patient Data Analysis of Clinicopathological Features, Treatment, and Survival.
papers.abstract: Pituitary carcinoma (PC) is a rare and aggressive pituitary neuroendocrine tumor (PitNET) defined by non-contiguous craniospinal or systemic metastatic spread. Evidence guiding treatment is limited to case reports and case series. This systematic review aimed to characterize the clinicopathological features, treatment patterns, and prognostic determinants of PC through pooled individual patient data (IPD) analysis. A systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Embase (January 1990 to March 2026) was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD420261402665). Individual patient data were extracted for 56 pre-specified variables from the identified literature. Two additional institutional cases were analyzed separately as illustrative clinical examples and are not part of the pooled statistical cohort. Survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method with log-rank tests. Univariate and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression and binary logistic regression (outcome: long-survivor status, defined as OS > 24 months) were performed on the pooled literature cohort. A total of 111 patients from 93 papers were included (51 males (45.9%); median age at PC diagnosis 54 years (IQR 40-61)), with corticotroph lineage predominating (47.7%). Median OS from PC diagnosis was 19 months (IQR 9.5-46); one-year OS was 67.7% and two-year OS 52.0%. Multimodal treatment was associated with significantly longer OS (median 45 vs. 12 months; log-rank p = 0.004). In multivariable Cox regression (n = 88; C-index 0.725), any objective treatment response (HR 0.245, 95% CI 0.101-0.593, p = 0.002), functional tumor status (HR 2.041, 95% CI 1.017-4.095, p = 0.045), and age at PC diagnosis (HR 1.018/year, p = 0.049) were independently associated with OS. Logistic regression identified multimodal treatment (OR 5.29, p = 0.009), any treatment response (OR 5.47, p = 0.006), and early metastasis (OR 0.18, p = 0.024) as independent predictors of long-survivor status. Ki-67 increased significantly from initial to PC-stage diagnosis (median 7% vs. 12%; Wilcoxon p < 0.001), which is, to our knowledge, the first demonstration of this longitudinal rise in a pooled pituitary carcinoma cohort. PC carries a poor prognosis, with a median OS of 19 months. Multimodal therapy and achievement of objective response are the strongest determinants of prolonged survival. Prospective registries with standardized molecular profiling are needed to advance precision management of this ultra-rare malignancy.

papers.title: Ferroptosis-Related GPX4 and CD71 and Immune Checkpoint PD-L1 in Cutaneous Melanoma: Associations with Clinicopathologic Features and Survival Outcomes.
papers.abstract: Ferroptosis-related pathways and immune checkpoint signaling may contribute to melanoma progression, but their clinicopathologic and prognostic interplay remains incompletely characterized. To investigate GPX4, CD71, and PD-L1 expression in primary cutaneous melanoma and evaluate their associations with clinicopathologic features and survival outcomes. This retrospective single-center cohort included 44 patients with primary cutaneous melanoma. PD-L1, GPX4, and CD71 expressions were assessed immunohistochemically. Associations with clinicopathologic parameters were analyzed, and overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses. PD-L1, GPX4, and CD71 positivity was were observed in 25.0%, 38.6%, and 36.4% of tumors, respectively. PD-L1 expression was associated with Breslow thickness (p = 0.004), whereas CD71 expression was associated with perineural invasion, Clark level, and disease stage (p = 0.019, p = 0.034, and p = 0.045, respectively). GPX4-positive tumors showed significantly shorter OS (40 vs. 103 months; p = 0.003) and DFS (42 vs. 86 months; p = 0.009). Triple-positive tumors (PD-L1+/GPX4+/CD71+) demonstrated significantly shorter OS and DFS than triple-negative tumors (p = 0.035 and p = 0.040, respectively). In multivariable analysis, GPX4 positivity remained independently associated with poorer OS. GPX4 expression was associated with adverse survival outcomes in cutaneous melanoma, while combined GPX4, CD71, and PD-L1 expression identified a subgroup with particularly unfavorable outcomes. These findings support further investigation of ferroptosis-related markers alongside immune checkpoint pathways as candidate prognostic biomarkers in melanoma.

papers.title: Development of an Experimental Protocol for Combined Electroporation and Phototherapy Treatment Against Melanoma Cells.
papers.abstract: Melanoma is the most common cutaneous tumor with significant challenges for successful pharmacological treatment. The aim of this study was to determine the optimal treatment conditions using a combined therapy based on electroporation and the photoactivation of acridine orange (AO) with a blue LED lamp, designed by Biopulse srl. The effect of combined therapy was investigated by MTT assay and optical microscopy observations. Drug uptake and apoptosis induction were analyzed by flow cytometry. The best treatment schedule was obtained using electric pulses (sequences of eight biphasic pulses lasting 50 + 50 μs with 300 μs interpulse, at a voltage of 300 V), an AO concentration of 0.01 μg/mL, and LED exposure for 30 s. The combined treatment was more effective against melanoma cells than human dermal fibroblast-adult cells. The results demonstrated that electroporation increased AO accumulation, allowing for reduced drug concentrations and exposure times. This combination induced programmed cell death consistent with apoptotic features in melanoma cells, as shown by cell cycle analysis. These preliminary results demonstrated the efficacy of combination therapy based on electroporation and phototherapy with AO on melanoma cells, and they encourage the possibility of testing efficacy on melanoma models in veterinary oncology.

papers.title: Autophagy in Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumors (PitNETs): Molecular Mechanisms, Secretory Homeostasis, Therapeutic Resistance, and Translational Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs) are usually indolent but may show invasive growth, recurrence, hormonal hypersecretion, and treatment resistance. Autophagy intersects with nutrient sensing, lysosomal homeostasis, mitochondrial quality control, and secretory-granule turnover, but its biological effects in PitNETs are context-dependent. This narrative review synthesizes PitNET-specific and mechanistically relevant evidence on macroautophagy, mitophagy, crinophagy, non-coding RNA and epigenetic regulation, treatment resistance, and pharmacological modulation, emphasizing the distinction between static autophagy markers and dynamic autophagic flux. Evidence is interpreted across human tissue, primary human cells, pituitary tumor cell lines, animal models, and clinical observations, while preserving clear separation between human observations and mechanistic evidence derived from experimental models. Across experimental systems, autophagy activation is associated with antitumor effects in selected settings, whereas completed basal flux may support stress adaptation and late-stage or selective-autophagy inhibition may enhance cytotoxicity. Biological outcome therefore depends on tumor lineage, treatment, the pathway stage affected, and whether flux is completed. Recent studies extend this framework to selective mitophagy, ncRNA/exosomal resistance networks, epitranscriptomic regulation, somatostatin-analogue resistance, and tumor-microenvironmental signaling. Clinical translation remains limited, and no autophagy-modulating strategy is validated for routine PitNET management. Future studies should integrate dynamic flux measurements, lineage-specific biomarkers, pharmacodynamic target engagement, and prospective clinical endpoints.

papers.title: Licochalcone A Inhibits Melanoma Cell Survival by Suppressing HSP75 (TRAP1) and Disrupting Cellular Redox and Energy Homeostasis.
papers.abstract: Heat shock protein 75(HSP75), a mitochondrial chaperone of the HSP90 family, sustains tumor cell survival by restraining oxidative phosphorylation, favoring aerobic glycolysis, and limiting mitochondrial ROS to preserve redox homeostasis. Although Licochalcone A (LCA), a flavonoid isolated from licorice root, displays anticancer activity across diverse tumors, whether HSP75 suppression contributes to its anti-melanoma effects remains undefined. This study assessed HSP75 expression in melanoma and evaluated the anti-melanoma efficacy of LCA. Expression of HSP75 was compared between melanoma and normal skin specimens by Western blotting. G361 melanoma cells were exposed to LCA, after which HSP75 expression, cell viability (MTT and trypan blue assays), intracellular ROS, the GSH/GSSG balance, ATP-associated luminescence, AMPK phosphorylation, MMP2, and apoptosis-related proteins were examined. HSP75 was also silenced by siRNA in normal melanocytes (HEMn-MP) and G361 cells, alone or combined with LCA treatment, with HSP75, p-AMPK, MMP2, cleaved PARP, and cleaved caspase-3 assessed by Western blotting. Melanoma tissue showed elevated HSP75 relative to normal tissue. LCA reduced HSP75 expression and viability while raising ROS, shifting the GSH/GSSG ratio toward oxidative stress, and reducing ATP-associated luminescence. AMPK phosphorylation rose, MMP2 declined, and pro-apoptotic markers (Bax, cleaved caspase-3, cleaved PARP) increased. HSP75 knockdown alone reproduced the LCA-induced changes in ATP-associated luminescence, p-AMPK, cleaved PARP, cleaved caspase-3, and MMP2, and combined knockdown with LCA further enhanced these changes in G361 cells, which were largely attenuated in normal HEMn-MP melanocytes. LCA suppresses melanoma cell survival by inducing cellular oxidative stress, reducing ATP-associated luminescence, and promoting apoptosis, with HSP75 suppression contributing to the ATP/AMPK and apoptotic responses. These findings support further evaluation of LCA and HSP75 in melanoma.

papers.title: Gangliosides in Cutaneous Melanoma: Molecular Mechanisms, Translational Evidence Gaps, and Preclinical Natural-Compound Leads.
papers.abstract: Cutaneous melanoma remains lethal once metastatic despite advances in immune checkpoint blockade and BRAF/MEK-directed therapy. Gangliosides are surface-accessible sialylated glycosphingolipids that regulate membrane organization, adhesion, and signaling, representing potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets. This narrative review evaluated the translational readiness of ganglioside-directed strategies in cutaneous melanoma, without assuming that evidence from other GD2- or GD3-positive cancers is directly transferable. We synthesized melanoma-specific evidence on GD3-linked focal adhesion signaling, p130Cas/paxillin activity, PI3K-AKT and MAPK outputs, and distinct phenotypes associated with GD3, GD2, and GM3. We then applied an evidence-gated framework distinguishing melanoma clinical evidence, melanoma preclinical evidence, cross-tumor translational evidence, and hypothesis-generating claims. Direct contemporary clinical evidence in melanoma remains limited. Antibody, cellular, and biosynthetic enzyme strategies require diagnostic-quality antigen profiling, demonstration of surface accessibility and functional dependency, and prospective monitoring for antigen escape and neurotoxicity. Natural compounds, particularly quercetin, are mechanistic probes or formulation-enabled leads: a 2024 study reported reduced GM3/GD3 abundance and FAK/paxillin/AKT signaling in melanoma cell lines, but high in vitro concentrations and the lack of pharmacokinetic or in vivo validation preclude therapeutic conclusions. We proposed a minimum evidence package and go/no-go criteria for clinical translation, specifying experiments needed to advance ganglioside biology into biomarker-defined melanoma interventions.

papers.title: Transcriptome Analysis of Linalool-Induced Hypopigmentation in B16 Melanoma Cells.
papers.abstract: Plant-derived phytochemicals exhibit significant pharmacological potential in chronic diseases, including melanoma. Since hyperactive melanogenesis is closely linked to melanoma progression, targeting this pathway with natural bioactive agents represents a major therapeutic strategy. The plant-derived terpene linalool induces cancer-specific oxidative stress in colon cancer cells, as we have previously reported. Here, we characterized the effects of linalool on B16-F10 melanoma cells to establish a transcriptomic baseline of hypopigmentation networks using phenotypic assays and high-throughput RNA-seq profiling. Non-toxic doses of linalool significantly inhibited melanin synthesis, accompanied by a marked reduction in tyrosinase protein abundance. RNA-seq identified 31 significantly upregulated and 48 significantly downregulated genes (p < 0.05), with PCA and cluster analysis demonstrating a distinct transcriptomic profile. Functional GO enrichment revealed candidate regulatory networks involving lysosomal components, the neurofilament cytoskeleton, and cell-cycle checkpoints. While core melanogenesis transcripts (Mitf, Tyr, Dct) showed only minor, non-significant variations, key stress-adaptation and cell-plasticity regulators (Mir210, Dll1) were significantly suppressed. This profile indicates a state of latent molecular vulnerability, mirroring the oxidative responses in colon cancer cells. Taken together, these findings provide a foundational transcriptomic repository of linalool-responsive networks, uncovering critical candidate pathways that modulate melanin production and antioxidant defenses to guide future functional validation and therapeutic exploration of botanical bioactives in melanoma research.

papers.title: An Overview of Cushing's Syndrome Caused by Ectopic Adrenocorticotropin Secretion.
papers.abstract: Ectopic Cushing's syndrome (ECS) causes 10% to 20% of all cases of endogenous hypercortisolism. It is caused by the aberrant secretion of adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) or corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH) due to the presence of an ectopic tumor. The latter is usually a neuroendocrine (NEN) tumor (mostly thoracic NENs such as bronchial NEN neoplasms, thymic NEN neoplasms, small cell lung carcinoma (SCLC), or pancreatic NEN neoplasms). Clinical presentation is heterogeneous: an aggressive phenotype, typically driven by rapidly growing, poorly differentiated tumors such as small-cell lung carcinoma, manifests with severe symptoms of acute onset, predominant myopathy, resistant arterial hypertension, hypokalemia, and severe hyperpigmentation, usually without the centripetal obesity typical of Cushing's syndrome; conversely, an indolent phenotype, more often related to well-differentiated neuroendocrine neoplasms such as bronchial carcinoids, may present with the classic centripetal fat distribution, facial plethora, and purple striae also seen in Cushing's disease, making clinical distinction between the two difficult. The diagnosis of ECS can be cumbersome and time-consuming. Once hypercortisolism is confirmed, the most critical step is to distinguish patients with an ectopic source of ACTH from those with pituitary adenoma. Dynamic endocrine tests such as the high-dose dexamethasone suppression test, CRH stimulation tests, desmopressin tests, and bilateral inferior petrosal sinus sampling (BIPSS) can be helpful in the differential diagnosis. BIPSS is considered the gold standard for distinguishing a pituitary from a non-pituitary source of ACTH: the absence of a central-to-peripheral ACTH gradient supports, but does not by itself localize or confirm, an ectopic source. Tumor localization is achieved by a multimodality imaging protocol, including initial high-resolution computed tomography (CT) scans, followed by functional imaging, mainly Gallium-68-labeled somatostatin receptor positron emission tomography (PET)/CT scans. However, in 10-20% of these patients, the tumors cannot be localized. The treatment of ACTH-dependent hypercortisolism is two-fold: one is to immediately control hypercortisolism to prevent life-threatening complications (opportunistic infections and thromboembolism), and the second is to definitively treat the tumor. Medical treatment with steroidogenesis inhibitors, including metyrapone, ketoconazole, and osilodrostat, or surgical management (bilateral adrenalectomy) can be effective in immediately controlling hypercortisolism. Definitive surgical resection of the tumor is the hoped-for final treatment. The prognosis is variable, depending on the nature of the underlying neoplasm, ranging from excellent in patients with resected bronchial carcinoids to dismal in those with SCLC.

papers.title: Semaglutide, Other GLP-1 Receptor Agonists, and Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma: A Narrative Review of Risk, Progression, and Mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Semaglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA), is widely prescribed for type 2 diabetes and obesity. Rodent studies showed thyroid C-cell tumors, prompting a boxed warning for medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC); whether this extends to papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), a follicular-cell-derived tumor, is uncertain. This narrative review examines semaglutide and other GLP-1RAs in relation to PTC, distinguishing semaglutide-specific from class-level evidence, and PTC from differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC), MTC, and thyroid cancer overall. Most human studies evaluated GLP-1RAs as a class and reported thyroid cancer overall; semaglutide-specific and PTC-specific estimates are scarce. Pooled trials and national cohorts mostly showed no statistically significant increase in thyroid cancer, although three separate meta-analyses of randomized trials each reported a statistically significant increase in overall thyroid cancer, and case-control and spontaneous-reporting studies reported signals vulnerable to detection bias and confounding. In a matched cohort of 1072 patients with DTC, GLP-1RA exposure (median 16 months) was not significantly associated with progression over 69 months. Receptor-expression findings were inconsistent, and preclinical data did not show proliferative effects. The cohort and progression findings indicate no statistically detectable increase within the available sample sizes, exposure durations, and event numbers; they do not establish oncological safety. Semaglutide-specific, histology-resolved studies with longer exposure are needed.

papers.title: Chemokine and Cytokine Receptor Signatures Associated with Pulmonary Endothelial-Conditioned Melanoma Invasion.
papers.abstract: Background: Pulmonary endothelial cells are increasingly recognized as active regulators of organ-specific metastasis; however, the mechanisms by which they influence melanoma invasion remain incompletely understood. Methods: Six primary melanoma-derived cell lines were first assessed for their invasive responses to HPMEC-conditioned medium. In a separate HPMEC co-culture invasion model, invasive and non-invasive melanoma subpopulations were isolated and analyzed for the expression of 88 chemokine and cytokine receptor genes. Candidate receptors were subsequently validated in primary melanoma tissues (n = 15), while their corresponding ligands were analyzed in patient plasma samples (n = 30). Results: HPMEC-conditioned medium enhanced invasion in half of the melanoma cell lines. Exploratory receptor-expression analyses identified candidate genes, including CCR2, IL11RA, IL15RA, TNFRSF11B, and TNFRSF12A, with expression patterns potentially associated with the observed invasive responses, while CCR4 expression was consistently elevated in all invasive subpopulations. In an exploratory analysis of a small primary melanoma tissue cohort, CCR2 and TNFRSF11B expression was significantly higher in tumors from patients with lung metastases, while IL11RA expression was upregulated compared with that in non-metastatic tumors. Melanoma cells consistently induced endothelial IL-8 expression, whereas plasma concentrations of the corresponding ligands did not differ significantly between patient groups. Conclusions: The elevated expression of CCR2, IL11RA, and TNFRSF11B observed in primary melanomas associated with lung metastases suggests that these factors may contribute to the development or progression of pulmonary metastases. These findings highlight the potential role of bidirectional communication between endothelial cells and melanoma cells in metastatic progression.

papers.title: Somatostatin Analogues Do Not Improve Survival in Grade 3 Gastroenteropancreatic Neuroendocrine Neoplasms: A Registry-Based Analysis with Ki-67 Stratification.
papers.abstract: The efficacy of somatostatin analogues (SSA) in Grade 3 (G3) neuroendocrine neoplasms (NEN) remains controversial, and registry data rarely permit a formal separation of NET G3 from neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC). We analyzed 519 patients with G3 gastroenteropancreatic (GEP) NEN recorded in a national neuroendocrine tumor registry (data export 3 April 2025; 464 de novo G3, 55 transformed G3); bronchopulmonary primaries were excluded. A Ki-67 > 55%, entered as a time-varying indicator, served as a surrogate for NEC. Outcomes were compared using Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards models with all treatments and the Ki-67 > 55% indicator entered as time-varying covariates. Among 410 patients with classifiable Ki-67, 256 (62.4%) ever had a Ki-67 > 55%. Ki-67 > 55% was associated with worse progression-free survival (PFS; HR 1.40, 95% CI 1.06-1.84; p = 0.016) and overall survival (OS; HR 1.65, 95% CI 1.15-2.37; p = 0.006). SSA use was not significantly associated with PFS (HR 1.32, 95% CI 0.85-2.04; p = 0.215) or OS (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.54-1.56; p = 0.744). After adjustment for Ki-67, transformed G3 was associated with worse OS (HR 1.60, 95% CI 1.02-2.51; p = 0.040). SSA therapy was not associated with improved survival in G3 GEP-NEN. As this is an observational analysis subject to confounding by indication, these estimates do not establish a lack of biological efficacy of SSA. A Ki-67 threshold of 55% identified a prognostically distinct subgroup and explains why transformed G3 appears indolent: after adjustment, it was associated with worse overall survival. This finding rests on 55 patients with 29 deaths and is hypothesis-generating.

papers.title: Orlistat Suppresses Small Intestinal Neuroendocrine Tumor Growth Through ATF3-Associated Stress and Ferroptosis-Related Responses-In Vitro and Cell Line Xenograft Evidence.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The incidence of small intestinal neuroendocrine tumors (SI-NETs) has increased in recent years, while effective therapeutic options remain limited. This study aimed to investigate the antitumor effects of orlistat on SI-NETs and elucidate the underlying mechanisms. Methods: The effects of orlistat were evaluated using STC-1 cells, patient-derived primary SI-NET cells, and xenograft models. Functional assays, RNA sequencing, lipidomic profiling, ATAC sequencing, and molecular analyses were performed to assess tumor-related phenotypes and investigate the underlying mechanisms. Results: Orlistat inhibited cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, induced G1-phase arrest and apoptosis, and suppressed tumor growth in vivo. Mechanistically, orlistat triggered endoplasmic reticulum stress, inhibited PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling, and upregulated activating transcription factor 3 (ATF3). Lipidomic profiling revealed alterations in lipid metabolism. Increased reactive oxygen species and lipid peroxidation, together with changes in ferroptosis-related proteins, indicated the involvement of ferroptosis-associated pathways. ATF3 overexpression reproduced the antitumor and ferroptosis-associated effects of orlistat. Integrated ATAC-seq and RNA-seq analyses identified CHAC1 as a potential downstream effector of ATF3. Conversely, ATF3 knockdown reduced CHAC1 expression and attenuated the effects of orlistat both in vitro and in vivo. Conclusions: Orlistat suppresses SI-NET progression and is associated with changes in endoplasmic reticulum stress, ATF3 expression, and ferroptosis-related responses, with CHAC1 identified as a potential downstream effector of ATF3. These findings support further investigation of orlistat as a potential therapeutic strategy for SI-NETs.

papers.title: Photodynamic Hijacking of APE1 Converts Tumor Defenses into Therapeutic Vulnerabilities via a Bidirectionally Gated Prodrug.
papers.abstract: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) for melanoma is chronically undermined by adaptive resistance, a long-overlooked challenge rooted in coordinated antioxidant buffering and DNA repair defenses. Herein, we propose a novel photodynamic sabotage approach that converts tumor defenses into therapeutic vulnerabilities by hijacking one important defense hub, the APE1 protein. This was achieved through creating a bidirectionally gated theranostic prodrug, APE-BDP, which covalently links an iodine-engineered BODIPY to the APE1 inhibitor CRT through a photocleavable bridge. Beyond pioneering the master regulator APE1, as a photodynamic target, the molecular design strategically repurposes the inherent nitro group on CRT as an endogenous quencher that establishes a photoinduced electron transfer process to silence the iodinated BODIPY. Meanwhile, the steric bulk of the conjugate concurrently physically blocks the CRT-APE1 engagement. This bidirectional gating mechanism ensures reciprocal deactivation in the dark. A single green light trigger initiates near-instantaneous (∼100% within minutes) and synchronous liberation of both warheads, enabling a cooperative dual assault that potently disrupts redox homeostasis and inactivates the APE1-mediated DNA repair machinery. This concerted hijacking of the defense network within the tumor triggers multiple cell death pathways. After formulation into a dissolvable microneedle patch for localized delivery, the system effectively suppressed tumor growth in melanoma models with minimal systemic toxicity. This work establishes that the photodynamic hijacking of key regulatory proteins via intelligent molecular engineering offers a potential design strategy to subvert PDT treatment resistance.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

papers.title: Genomic Differences Between Corticotroph and Ectopic ACTH-Producing NETs.
papers.abstract: We aimed to identify and compare key molecular alterations underlying adrenocorticotropin (ACTH)-producing neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) in Cushing's disease and ectopic ACTH syndrome. Whole-exome sequencing was performed on 34 pituitary ACTH-secreting NETs (corticotroph tumors: 30 microadenomas and 4 macroadenomas) and 8 ectopic ACTH-producing NETs of lung, pancreatic, and renal origin. Somatic point mutations, copy-number alterations, and loss of heterozygosity (LOH) were compared between corticotroph and ectopic ACTH-producing NETs. Corticotroph tumors demonstrated significantly more gene deletions and LOH events compared with ectopic ACTH-producing NETs (median 1687 and 2573.5 affected genes in corticotroph tumors, respectively). In corticotroph tumors recurrent subtelomeric deletions and LOH on chromosome 19 affecting FAM98C, RASGRP4, RYR1, MAP4K1, and EIF3K were observed. Notably, TERT deletion was detected in 94% of corticotroph tumors versus only 12.5% ectopic ACTH-producing NETs. In contrast, ectopic ACTH-producing NETs frequently exhibited chromosomal duplications on chromosomes 17 and 21, enriched for keratin-associated protein gene clusters. Recurrent somatic point mutations were identified in BRAF, CACNA1I, KLHL20, MCCC2, LRP1, TCP11X2, USP8, and USP48 genes, explaining the molecular basis of disease in 20 of 34 corticotroph tumors and 2 of 6 lung ACTH-producing NETs (LRP1 R1497Q and CACNA1I S639T). These findings indicate that corticotroph tumors predominantly demonstrated deletions and LOH involving subtelomeric genes, whereas ectopic ACTH-producing tumors more commonly exhibited chromosomal duplications. Potentially relevant somatic mutations were detected in 59% of corticotroph tumors and in 33% of lung ACTH-producing NETs. In conclusion, ACTH-producing NETs of pituitary versus other localizations demonstrate significantly different genetic alterations despite similar clinical and secretory phenotypes.

papers.title: Peripancreatic High-Grade Neuroendocrine Neoplasm Mimicking a Pancreatic Mass in Esophageal Small Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Primary small cell carcinoma of the esophagus (SCCE) is an infrequent aggressive neuroendocrine malignancy. We describe a 60-year-old woman with cirrhosis who presented with weight loss, backache, and night sweats. Histopathology confirmed small cell carcinoma of the esophagus with synaptophysin positivity and Ki-67 ∼90%. Endoscopic ultrasound showed a 38-mm lesion peripancreatically.
