Fine-needle aspiration cytology showed a high-grade neuroendocrine tumor (Ki-67 >50%) with positivity for synaptophysin, AE1/AE3, and insulinoma-associated protein 1, with a lack of tissue adequacy for classification. There was no evidence of pancreatic mass on MRI, thus suggesting metastatic lymphadenopathy. TP53 and RAD50 mutations were identified. Liver dysfunction, thrombocytopenia limited treatment, and the patient died within 6 weeks.

papers.title: Tebentafusp induces systemic immune activation, but tumor immune remodeling remains incompletely validated: a narrative review in metastatic uveal melanoma.
papers.abstract: Tebentafusp improves survival in HLA-A*02:01-positive metastatic uveal melanoma, yet the human evidence linking early systemic immune activation to remodeling of metastatic tumors is dispersed across overlapping translational reports. We performed a PRISMA-style, search-informed narrative review and descriptive evidence mapping of human reports evaluating baseline or on-treatment immune measurements in tebentafusp-treated uveal melanoma. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched for reports published from January 2015 to 9 December 2025, with an updated search on 9 June 2026. Reports were linked to their underlying trial or cohort before synthesis. Overall, 286 records were screened, 21 full-text reports or complete abstracts were assessed, and 10 reports were retained. These represented three principal evidence units rather than 10 independent studies: NCT02570308, NCT03070392, and an independent serial skin-biopsy cohort. Blood-based analyses consistently showed early cytokine induction and transient lymphocyte changes after tebentafusp dosing. Paired metastatic-tissue analyses reported increased CD3 and CD8 cell density and interferon-response programs by day 16, but these observations derived predominantly from overlapping analyses of NCT02570308. Baseline and on-treatment immune features were associated with survival in exploratory analyses. Skin biopsies provided independent evidence of on-target cutaneous pharmacodynamics but only indirect evidence regarding metastatic tumor remodeling. Tebentafusp is associated with consistently observed early systemic immune activation across overlapping analyses, but treatment-associated metastatic tumor immune remodeling remains incompletely validated. The available evidence supports temporal coherence rather than a proven causal systemic-to-tumor pathway. Future studies should use prospective paired blood and liver sampling, harmonized time points, prespecified immune endpoints, and mediation analyses linking immune changes to clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Pulmonary edema during cesarean delivery secondary to Takotsubo syndrome revealing pheochromocytoma: a case report.
papers.abstract: Acute pulmonary edema during delivery is a serious condition with a wide range of etiologies, including Takotsubo syndrome (TTS), a form of transient left ventricular dysfunction most often presenting as apical ballooning. We report the case of a 35-year-old woman who developed severe hypertension (205/130 mmHg), polypnea, and a drop in oxygen saturation to 80% during cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia. She received noninvasive ventilation while the cesarean section continued and was transferred to the intensive care unit. Point-of-care ultrasound showed a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 35% with apical ballooning and diffuse B-lines on lung ultrasound. Computed tomography identified a right adrenal mass. A diagnosis of pulmonary edema complicating TTS was made, and the patient received furosemide and oxygen therapy. Further investigations, including urinary catecholamine metabolites, confirmed the diagnosis of pheochromocytoma. One week later, LVEF had recovered to 57% with mild residual apical hypokinesia and complete clinical recovery. The patient was then transferred to the surgical unit for management of the pheochromocytoma. This case demonstrates that TTS can cause pulmonary edema in the peripartum period, and that timely diagnosis is essential for a favorable outcome. Point-of-care ultrasound can be instrumental in guiding the assessment of such critical situations, and noninvasive ventilation may be of particular value in selected pregnant patients. This case also underscores the importance of an etiological workup and prompt treatment of hypertensive disorders in pregnancy, especially when pheochromocytoma is suspected, since anesthesia and surgery can precipitate decompensation.

papers.title: Second Primary Malignancies After Appendiceal Neuroendocrine Tumors: A Contemporary SEER-Based Standardized Incidence Ratio Analysis (2015-2023).
papers.abstract: Whether contemporary appendiceal neuroendocrine tumor (NET) survivors have an increased risk of second primary malignancies (SPMs) remains uncertain. We assessed relative incidence and the effect of excluding early post-diagnosis events. We identified adults aged ≥20 years with malignant appendiceal NETs diagnosed between 2015 and 2023 in Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) data from 17 registries. Observed and expected SPMs were compared using standardized incidence ratios (SIRs). The primary analysis excluded events occurring within the first two months, with sensitivity analyses using ≥6- and ≥12-month exclusion periods. The baseline cohort included 4,854 patients. At ≥2 months, 4,522 patients contributed 18,273.65 person-years, with 119 observed SPMs compared with 103.03 expected SPMs (SIR, 1.15; 95% CI, 0.96-1.38). Elevated estimates were observed for malignancies of the digestive system (SIR, 1.56; 95% CI, 1.03-2.27), pancreas (2.51; 1.01-5.17), kidney and renal pelvis (2.36; 1.08-4.49), and thyroid (2.73; 1.36-4.89). Overall SIRs were 1.15, 1.10, and 1.03 across the three exclusion thresholds. Several site-specific estimates decreased, but pancreatic SIRs remained similar (2.51, 2.70, and 2.58). No site-specific confidence interval excluded unity at ≥12 months. Overall SPM incidence was not significantly elevated. Early site-specific findings warrant caution because of small event counts, multiple comparisons, and possible detection effects that SEER cannot directly measure. Loss of statistical significance with longer exclusion periods does not exclude persistent site-specific excess incidence. These results do not support additional routine organ-directed screening solely based on appendiceal NET history.
papers.journal: Asian Pacific journal of cancer prevention : APJCP

papers.title: Rethinking evidence generation in gastrointestinal cancer treatment research: the need for both high-quality interventional and observational evidence.
papers.abstract: The current research ecosystem on gastrointestinal (GI) cancers-including anal, colorectal, esogastric, pancreatic, hepatocellular, and biliary tract cancers-relies heavily on randomized controlled trials (RCTs), which involve high costs and limited transportability. Fewer than 10% of therapeutic recommendations for pancreatic adenocarcinoma are based on high-level evidence, a proportion that has not improved between 2011 and 2022. Furthermore, substantial research waste undermines interventional research in GI cancer: 30-37% of completed GI cancer trials lack publicly available results, and only 59% of gastric cancer trials are published as full-text articles. Such waste in research negatively impacts evidence synthesis and guidelines recommendations. While interventional research is the only way to assess the efficacy of a new drug, observational studies and real-world evidence (RWE), using health records, cohorts, registries and/or administrative databases, may offer complementary insights, especially for research questions that cannot be studied by RCTs. In particular, RWE can evaluate treatments in elderly or comorbid patients often excluded from trials, inform decisions for rare tumors such as digestive neuroendocrine neoplasms, and evaluate real-world effectiveness of treatments such as targeted therapies or immunotherapy. While historically RWE reliability was often criticized for biases and data quality issues, methodological advances, such as target trial emulation and data standardization, have enhanced its validity, and it is now increasingly used to support regulatory decisions by agencies like the Food and Drug Administration and the European Medicines Agency. Better integration of high quality interventional and observational approaches is essential in GI cancer research. Guidance on when to use interventional versus observational studies, depending on the clinical question, may help put this integration into practice. This synergy could reduce research waste, accelerate evidence generation, and help identify more effective personalized treatments for GI cancer patients.

papers.title: Safety and efficacy of dual immune checkpoint inhibition for melanoma brain metastases and its comparison to ICI monotherapy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Melanoma brain metastases remain a major cause of morbidity and death despite advances in systemic therapy. Dual immune checkpoint inhibition has shown promising intracranial activity, but the overall evidence is heterogeneous and its benefit relative to monotherapy remains clinically important to define. We performed a PRISMA-based systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective and retrospective studies evaluating dual immune checkpoint inhibition in adults with cutaneous or mucosal melanoma brain metastases. PubMed, Scopus, and Embase were searched from inception to November 5, 2025. Random-effects models were used to pool intracranial progression-free survival, overall survival, intracranial response outcomes, and adverse events. Comparative analyses versus monotherapy were performed when data were available. Twenty-four studies involving 3518 patients were included. In the overall dual ICI cohort, pooled intracranial progression-free survival was 51.9% at 6 months, 44.1% at 12 months, 40.5% at 2 years, and 38.8% at 3 years. Pooled intracranial objective response rate was 42.5%, increasing to 48% in first-line dual ICI recipients. Outcomes were more favorable in asymptomatic patients than in symptomatic patients, with pooled overall survival at 3 years of 52.3% versus 31.5%. Comparative analyses favored dual ICI over monotherapy for overall survival at 6 months, 12 months, and 2 years, while no significant difference was seen at 3 years. Elevated LDH was associated with worse survival, whereas BRAF mutation was not significantly associated with outcome. All-grade treatment-related adverse events occurred in 78% of patients, grade 3 or higher events in 48.2%, and all-grade immune-related adverse events in 65.5%. Across studies reporting adverse events for patients receiving dual and mono ICI, dual ICI therapy was consistently associated with higher rates of treatment-related and immune-related toxicities, which is consistent with the established safety profile of nivolumab plus ipilimumab and highlights the need for close monitoring, and early management of immune-related complications. Dual immune checkpoint inhibition provides meaningful and durable intracranial benefit in melanoma brain metastases, particularly in asymptomatic patients and when used early. Comparative analyses favored dual ICI over monotherapy at 6 months, 12 months, and 2 years. However, the 3-year survival advantage remains uncertain because of limited data and substantial heterogeneity. Symptomatic disease remains a major unmet need, and the potential survival benefit must be balanced against substantial toxicity.

papers.title: Patient Acceptance of Semi-Inpatient Radioligand Therapy: Insights from a Prospective Survey in Nuclear Medicine.
papers.abstract: Radioligand therapy﻿ with lutetium-177 is an effective treatment option for patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer and metastatic neuroendocrine tumors. In Germany, radiation protection laws require hospitalization with isolation, which may cause capacity problems. Internationally, models show the feasibility of non-inpatient radioligand therapy﻿ under strict safety measures. Patient acceptance is crucial for the implementation of flexible care models. This study aimed to assess patient preferences, concerns and requirements for non-inpatient radioligand therapy﻿. An anonymous cross-sectional study was conducted in 46 patients receiving radioligand therapy﻿ in a nuclear medicine department. The questionnaire collected demographic and clinical data, treatment preferences, benefits and limitations of various care settings and factors influencing the acceptance of outpatient treatments. Analysis was done descriptively. Most patients (95.7%) valued inpatient monitoring and safety. However, 53.2% of patients preferred a shortened hospital stay and 54.4% of patients rated semi-inpatient care as ideal. Only 8.9% of patients supported a fully outpatient approach. Key barriers to home-based care are radiation exposure and lack of medical supervision. Patients with better performance status showed greater acceptance to non-inpatient models. Educational materials and guaranteed telephone access to clinical staff were identified as important for increasing acceptance. Patients express a strong interest in individualized, flexible radioligand therapy﻿ with reliable safety structures. Risk-adapted semi-inpatient models may improve patient-centered care and alleviate pressure on inpatient resources. However, potential risks as radiation exposure to family members and subsequent safety measures need to be explored in controlled trials.

papers.title: Endoscopic closure of refractory perforation after duodenal neuroendocrine tumor resection with multiple strategies.
Radiotherapy for skin tumors and soft-tissue sarcomas: Current state of the art and recent advances.
papers.abstract: Radiotherapy plays a pivotal role in the management of skin cancers and soft-tissue sarcomas in both curative and adjuvant settings. Over recent years, several clinical trials and international guidelines have refined its indications and identified new strategies that are likely to influence clinical practice. This review provides an updated overview of the role of radiotherapy in basal cell carcinoma, cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, cutaneous melanoma, Merkel cell carcinoma, cutaneous lymphoma, and soft-tissue sarcoma. Recent evidence highlights the potential benefit of consolidation radiotherapy following hedgehog inhibitors in locally advanced basal cell carcinoma, improved outcomes with the combination of cemiplimab and radiotherapy in cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, integration of stereotactic radiotherapy with immune checkpoint inhibitors for melanoma brain metastases, the importance of minimizing the interval between surgery and postoperative radiotherapy in Merkel cell carcinoma, the limitations of ultra-low-dose radiotherapy for indolent cutaneous lymphomas, and the emergence of hypofractionated preoperative radiotherapy schedules for soft-tissue sarcoma. By distinguishing established indications from emerging evidence, this review summarizes the developments most likely to influence contemporary radiation oncology practice and highlights areas where further prospective studies are warranted.
papers.journal: Cancer radiotherapie : journal de la Societe francaise de radiotherapie oncologique

papers.title: NRAS Mutations in Different Melanoma Histotypes: Molecular and Clinical Implications.
papers.abstract: Melanoma is a highly aggressive skin malignancy with increasing incidence and mortality worldwide. Among its key genetic alterations, NRAS mutations occur in approximately 15-25% of melanomas, defining a distinct molecular subset associated with aggressive tumor behavior and poor prognosis. Unlike BRAF mutations, NRAS alterations remain largely undruggable, posing significant therapeutic challenges. This review examines the histotype-specific distribution of NRAS mutations in melanoma and discusses their molecular and clinical implications. Most NRAS mutations involve codon 61 and result in constitutive activation of the MAPK and PI3K signaling pathways, thereby promoting tumorigenesis and disease progression. Although NRAS-mutant melanomas are associated with an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, they also exhibit high immunogenicity, suggesting potential sensitivity to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). To further characterize the molecular landscape of NRAS-mutant melanoma, we analyzed data from the Catalogue of Somatic Mutations in Cancer (COSMIC), providing insights into the prevalence, distribution, co-mutation patterns, and functional consequences of NRAS alterations across different melanoma histotypes. NRAS mutations represent a major driver of melanoma progression and define a biologically and clinically distinct subset of the disease. Despite encouraging responses to immunotherapy, clinical outcomes remain suboptimal, highlighting the need for novel therapeutic approaches. A deeper understanding of NRAS-driven oncogenesis, histotype-specific mutation patterns, and their impact on therapeutic response is essential for advancing precision medicine and improving outcomes for patients with melanoma.

papers.title: Oxalate Nephropathy in a patient with Neuroendocrine tumor receiving Long-acting Octreotide.
papers.abstract: Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) with 177Lu-DOTA-TATE along with long-acting Octreotide is an established treatment for metastatic neuroendocrine tumours (NETs). Renal dysfunction following PRRT is usually attributed to radiation-induced nephrotoxicity. A 55-year-old man with metastatic somatostatin receptor-positive NET, diagnosed in April 2023, initially received long-acting octreotide, external beam radiotherapy, and six cycles of etoposide chemotherapy. Persistent disease on Ga-68 DOTA-TATE PET imaging in November 2024 prompted treatment with four cycles of 177Lu-DOTA-TATE PRRT between February and December 2025, along with monthly long-acting octreotide injections. Baseline renal function was normal and remained stable at a serum creatinine of 0.9 mg/dL till December 2025. He was referred to nephrology in March 2026 with an asymptomatic rise in serum creatinine to 2.3 mg/dL. Evaluation revealed subnephrotic proteinuria (820 mg/day), normal-sized kidneys, bland urinary sediments. PRRT-related nephrotoxicity and acute interstitial nephritis were initially considered. Kidney biopsy demonstrated extensive tubular calcium oxalate crystal deposition along with acute interstitial inflammation. In the absence of other identifiable causes of enteric hyperoxaluria, octreotide-induced pancreatic exocrine insufficiency was suspected as the most likely aetiology. The patient received a short course of corticosteroids in view of interstitial inflammation in the biopsy. Serum creatinine declined to 1.5 mg/dL on follow-up. Early recognition is critical, as progressive renal dysfunction may compromise eligibility for PRRT, a cornerstone treatment for NETs.

papers.title: "Paraneoplastic syndromes secondary to Νeuroendocrine Νeoplasms".
papers.abstract: Paraneoplastic syndromes (PNS) represent uncommon but clinically significant manifestations of neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) arising from ectopic hormone secretion, aberrant peptide processing, cytokine-mediated effects, or immune-mediated mechanisms. Although NENs are intrinsically capable of producing bioactive substances leading to PNS, the true prevalence of PNS in NENs remains uncertain and is likely underestimated. Paraneoplastic manifestations may precede tumor diagnosis, represent the first indication of an otherwise occult neoplasm, or emerge during disease progression, thereby providing valuable diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic information. Endocrine PNS, including ectopic adrenocorticotrophic hormone secretion, carcinoid syndrome, paraneoplastic hypercalcemia, syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion, hypoglycemia and ectopic acromegaly, account for the majority of cases, whereas neurological PNS are rarer and predominantly associated with high-grade neuroendocrine carcinomas (NECs). Recent advances in molecular biology have revealed the importance of neuroendocrine lineage plasticity, transcriptional dysregulation, epigenetic reprogramming, and abnormal prohormone processing in the pathogenesis of these syndromes. Concurrently, improvements in biochemical testing, functional imaging, liquid biopsy technologies, and molecular profiling have enhanced diagnostic accuracy and disease monitoring. Management requires a multidisciplinary approach combining syndrome-directed therapies with tumor-targeted interventions, including surgery, somatostatin analogs, peptide receptor radionuclide therapy, targeted agents, specific chemotherapy regimens and emerging immunotherapeutic strategies. Despite substantial progress, significant gaps remain regarding epidemiology, accurate biomarkers, prognostic significance, and optimal management. This review summarizes current knowledge on pathophysiology, clinical spectrum, diagnosis, prognostic implications, and treatment of PNS associated with gastroenteropancreatic and lung NENs, while highlighting future research priorities and unmet clinical needs.

papers.title: Diagnosis and Surgical Treatment of Acral Lentiginous Melanoma on Third Toe of 57-Year-Old Male: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: We report a case of a 57-year-old male patient who presented with localized redness with possible cellulitis to the third toe. The podiatrist performed a shave biopsy with a Breslow's depth of at least 1.1 mm. Pathological results confirmed a Clark's Level 4 malignant melanoma over the nail bed area. The surgical oncologist biopsied the sentinel lymph node and left inguinal node, which tested negative for malignancy by immunohistochemistry and multilevel hemotoxylin and eosin. The surgical team performed a left third-toe amputation. During a nine-month follow-up, the patient remained in remission. This paper aims to contribute to the guidelines for recognition of melanoma of the foot and nail unit to prevent delay in diagnosis.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Podiatric Medical Association

papers.title: MicroRNAs in Cutaneous Melanoma: Biological Roles, Clinical Utility, and Future Directions.
papers.abstract: Cutaneous melanoma remains a malignancy with substantial metastatic potential, and conventional diagnostic and surveillance tools such as biopsy and imaging have recognized limitations in sensitivity, specificity, and invasiveness. Circulating microRNAs (miRNAs) have emerged as promising non-invasive biomarkers because of their stability in body fluids and their disease-specific expression patterns. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on the biological roles of miRNAs in melanoma, acting as either oncogenes or tumor suppressors, and their potential clinical utility across diagnosis, prognosis, treatment monitoring, and therapeutic targeting. Individual circulating miRNAs (e.g., miR-21, miR-221, miR-206, miR-125b) and multi-miRNA signatures (e.g., MEL12, MEL38, MELmiR-7) have shown associations with tumor stage, recurrence, and survival, and several panels have demonstrated high diagnostic sensitivity and specificity in liquid biopsy assays. miRNAs also participate in drug resistance and immune modulation, suggesting relevance to immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy and potential as therapeutic targets. However, clinical translation remains limited by the lack of standardized isolation and quantification protocols, tumor and patient heterogeneity, and the predominantly associative nature of current evidence. Continued methodological standardization, larger validation cohorts, and integration with other omics platforms will be needed before circulating miRNAs can be incorporated into routine melanoma management.

papers.title: Inhibitory Effects of Extracellular Vesicles Derived from Sargassum serratifolium on Melanogenesis Partially by Suppressing Melanin Transport.
papers.abstract: Sargassum serratifolium (S. serratifolium), listed in the Food Code, is known for its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties and is used in cosmetic applications. However, due to limited industrial utilization and overaccumulation in marine environments, Sargassum has been designated as a marine pollutant by the UN Environment Agency. To improve resource efficiency and reduce environmental burden, this study developed a dual-extraction strategy to isolate extracellular vesicles (EVs) and extract ethanol-soluble substances from the same S. serratifolium biomass. The extracellular vesicles derived from S. serratifolium (SEVs) were isolated and characterized based on their particle size, morphology, concentration, and cargo molecules, including mRNA and proteins. Their antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities were evaluated using cellular assays, while their effects on melanogenesis and melanosome transport were assessed in B16F10 melanoma cells. Transcriptomic analysis by RNA sequencing was further performed to investigate the molecular pathways involved in SEV-mediated regulation of melanosome transport. SEVs isolation did not affect the yield or biological activity of the S. serratifolium ethanol-soluble fraction. Based on our previous finding that the ethanol extract of S. serratifolium (ESS) suppresses melanin synthesis, the present study focused on investigating the effects and mechanisms of SEVs on melanogenesis and melanosome transport. SEVs were nanoscale vesicles containing mRNA and proteins and showed antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects in cellular assays. Although SEVs did not reduce melanin production in B16F10 cells, they significantly inhibited melanosome transport. RNA sequencing suggested that SEVs regulated melanosome transport through pathways related to the extracellular matrix, actin filament organization, and calcium ion homeostasis. These findings suggest that SEVs exert anti-melanogenic effects by targeting melanosome transport, providing a complementary mechanism to the previously reported inhibition of melanin synthesis by ESS. These findings demonstrate a sustainable strategy for producing functional EVs and bioactive extracts from a single S. serratifolium biomass source and support their potential use in cosmetic or therapeutic applications targeting hyperpigmentation.

papers.title: MRI-Based Radiomics Model for Pretreatment Prediction of Pathological Lymph Node Metastasis in Neuroendocrine Carcinoma of the Cervix: Dual-Center Development and External Validation.
papers.abstract: Objectives: To develop and externally validate MRI-based radiomics and clinicoradiomics models for predicting pathological lymph node metastasis (LNM) in neuroendocrine carcinoma of the cervix (NECC). Methods: This retrospective two-center study included 133 patients who underwent pretreatment pelvic MRI and pathological nodal assessment: 93 for development and 40 for external validation. Intratumoral and peritumoral features were extracted from T2-weighted, diffusion-weighted, and contrast-enhanced T1-weighted images. Stratified nested fivefold cross-validation evaluated the complete revised selection process. Locked models were assessed for discrimination, calibration, and exploratory net benefit, with conventional MRI nodal assessment as a comparator. Results: Pathological LNM was present in 54/133 patients (40.6%). The selected radiomics-only k-nearest neighbors (KNN) model had an external AUC of 0.783 (95% CI, 0.630 to 0.935), accuracy of 0.800, sensitivity of 0.813, and specificity of 0.792. The complete selection procedure yielded an out-of-fold AUC of 0.731. External AUCs were 0.727 for the clinical/MRI model and 0.767 for the clinicoradiomics model; neither fusion model differed significantly from the clinical/MRI comparator. Conventional MRI sensitivity was 0.563, with no significant paired difference from the selected model (p = 0.125). External calibration was imperfect (Brier score, 0.186; slope, 0.672). Conclusions: MRI radiomics showed moderate external discrimination of pathological LNM in NECC. Adding clinical variables did not demonstrate further benefit. Multicenter validation, recalibration, and clinical-impact assessment are needed before clinical application.

papers.title: Induction Systemic Therapy Followed by Response-Adapted Consolidative Radiation in Locally Advanced Non-Melanoma Skin Cancer: A Retrospective Case Series.
papers.abstract: There exists an unmet clinical need to define definitive management strategies for patients with locally advanced non-melanoma skin cancers (NMSC), particularly if not amenable to surgical resection. We retrospectively reviewed a case series of locally advanced unresectable NMSC treated with induction systemic treatment followed by response-adapted consolidative radiation. We identified 15 patients who met study criteria, including seven with basal cell carcinoma (BCC), six with cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC), and two with Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC). Clinical complete response (CR) by physical examination was observed in all 15 patients. No locoregional or distant recurrences were observed in any histologic subtype after completion of radiation (median follow-up from completion of radiation: 18.1 months BCC, 22.5 months CSCC, 22.7 months MCC). The median duration of observed response (DOOR), measured from first clinical response was 26.9 months (26.2 BCC, 29.4 CSCC, 27.1 MCC). Radiation treatment volumes were response-adapted with median gross tumor volume reduction of 55.3% (15.3%-100%). Median treatment-free response was 20.5 months. No unexpected systemic therapy related toxicities were identified. In this single-institution retrospective case series, induction systemic therapy followed by response-adapted consolidative radiation was feasible and associated with durable disease control in selected patients with locally advanced unresectable NMSC.

papers.title: Altered Neural Pitch Encoding in Vestibular Schwannoma: Evidence From Frequency-Following Responses.
papers.abstract: Vestibular schwannomas (VSs) frequently cause hearing dysfunction, yet standard clinical assessments may not fully capture neural processing deficits. To determine whether unilateral VS impairs neural encoding of speech sounds, as measured by frequency-following responses (FFRs), beyond hearing loss alone. Exploratory observational case-control study with both within-subject and matched between-subject comparisons. Tertiary referral center (Antwerp University Hospital, Belgium). Twenty-three adults (mean age 53.7 ± 9.8 years; 13 men) with untreated unilateral VS and sufficient residual hearing for FFR assessment were included. Patients with prior VS treatment, neurological disease, middle ear pathology, or profound hearing loss were excluded. VS ears were matched to a previous sensorineural hearing loss (SNHL) cohort by age, sex, and hearing thresholds.Intervention or Exposures:Magnetic resonance imaging-confirmed unilateral VS. FFR measures of neural encoding of voice pitch were evaluated, with pitch strength as the primary outcome. Additional exploratory FFR measures and formant encoding (F1) were analyzed. Auditory brainstem response (ABR) latencies and thresholds were also recorded. Within subjects, VS-affected ears showed reduced pitch strength compared with contralateral ears for both the /a/ and /o/ stimulus sections (both P = .023). In the matched comparison with SNHL controls, pitch strength remained significantly reduced (P = .049 for /a/, P = .043 for /o/), whereas other FFR measures did not differ significantly. ABR analysis showed prolonged wave V latency and interpeak latency I to V in VS-affected ears. VS is associated with reduced neural encoding of voice pitch, most consistently reflected by reduced FFR pitch strength even after accounting for hearing loss. These findings suggest a selective vulnerability of temporal pitch coding in VS and support the clinical potential of the FFR as an adjunct measure when standard audiological tests do not fully capture patient-reported listening difficulties.
papers.journal: Journal of otolaryngology - head & neck surgery = Le Journal d'oto-rhino-laryngologie et de chirurgie cervico-faciale

papers.title: Mahvash disease: A novel case of apparent monoallelic disease and a novel cause of hypoglycaemia.
papers.abstract: Glucagon cell hyperplasia and neoplasia (GCHN), also known as Mahvash disease (MVAH), is a rare pancreatic neuroendocrine disorder. In most cases, the disorder is autosomal recessive and caused by inactivating mutations in the glucagon receptor (GCGR), leading to pancreatic α-cell hyperplasia and hyperglucagonemia, with sporadic association with hypoglycaemia. We present an adult female patient presenting with recurrent hypoglycaemia: she had an enlarged pancreas and very high levels of glucagon. Severe hypoglycaemia is not generally seen in most cases of Mahvash syndrome; this could suggest the possibility of an occult insulinoma. Genetic testing showed an essential splice variant in GCGR that predicts loss of protein production. It is most likely a single pathogenic variant in the GCGR gene, although the literature reports only a recessive phenotype. We cannot entirely exclude an autosomal recessive condition in terms of mutations in promoter or relevant intronic regions.

papers.title: Contemporary Pathological Classification of Primary Lung Tumors: Integration of Morphology, Immunohistochemistry, and Molecular Pathology.
papers.abstract: This review summarizes the current World Health Organization (WHO) classification of lung tumors, emphasizing key morphological, immunohistochemical, and molecular features relevant to diagnosis and management. REVIEW: Primary pulmonary tumors comprise a heterogeneous spectrum of neoplasms with distinct morphological, immunophenotypic, molecular, and clinical characteristics. The current WHO classification integrates traditional histopathological assessment with immunohistochemical and molecular findings, reflecting advances in our understanding of tumor biology and the growing importance of precision medicine. This review summarizes the major categories of primary pulmonary tumors, including adenocarcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, adenosquamous carcinoma, large cell carcinoma, sarcomatoid carcinomas, neuroendocrine neoplasms, salivary gland-type tumors, and mesenchymal tumors specific to the lung, as well as selected rare pulmonary neoplasms. Particular attention is given to the defining morphological characteristics and diagnostic criteria of individual tumor entities, relevant immunohistochemical profiles, and recurrent molecular alterations with diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic implications. The challenges of diagnosing pulmonary tumors in small biopsies and cytological specimens are also addressed, with an emphasis on the judicious use of immunohistochemistry and preservation of tissues for molecular testing. CONCLUSION: Accurate classification of primary pulmonary tumors requires the integration of morphological, immunohistochemical, and molecular findings within the framework of the current WHO Classification of Thoracic Tumors. Recognition of the characteristic morphological and immunophenotypic features, together with appropriate molecular characterization, is essential for precise diagnosis and optimal patient management. Continued advances in molecular pathology are expected to further refine pulmonary tumor classification and contribute to increasingly personalized therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Clinical and Dermoscopic Features of Subungual Hemorrhage: A Retrospective Study of 420 Cases.
papers.abstract: Subungual hemorrhage (SH) may be difficult to distinguish from nail unit melanoma, onychomycosis, and other nail disorders. Dermoscopy enables non-invasive visualization of subtle subungual structures and provides useful information for differential diagnosis. This study aimed to analyze the clinical and dermoscopic features of SH and explore their associations with lesion location, disease course, and nail involvement. Clinical and dermoscopic data of 420 patients diagnosed with SH between December 2018 and March 2024 were retrospectively collected from two tertiary hospitals in China. Patients aged 18-45 years accounted for 65.5% of the cohort, and 84.3% of lesions were located on the toenails. Most patients (69.5%) had a single lesion, and 73.8% and 79.3% showed no nail margin involvement or nail plate damage, respectively. Toenail involvement was more frequent in female (p = 0.003) and young adult (p = 0.002) patients. The predominant dermoscopic features were purplish-red/black pigmentation (72.9%), irregular morphology (71.0%), and linear or striated pseudopods surrounding the lesion (56.7%). Irregular morphology was significantly more frequent in toenail lesions, whereas linear morphology was more common in fingernail lesions (both p < 0.001). Irregular shapes were predominant (73.6%) in cases with a short-term course (< 3 months), whereas linear lesions accounted for 31.6% of lesions in patients with a long disease course (≥ 12 months). Lesion morphology was significantly associated with disease course (p < 0.001). Irregular morphology was also significantly associated with nail margin involvement (p < 0.001) and nail plate damage (p = 0.007), while linear or striated pseudopod lesions showed a significant association with nail margin involvement (p < 0.001). In this cohort, SH predominantly affected females and young adults and typically presented as a single toenail lesion. Dermoscopic features of SH varied according to lesion location and disease course, and irregular morphology was associated with nail margin involvement and nail plate damage. Recognition of characteristic dermoscopic features, together with clinical history and lesion evolution, may facilitate differentiation of SH from nail unit melanoma and other nail disorders, help avoid unnecessary biopsy in typical cases, and prompt further evaluation of suspicious lesions.
papers.journal: Skin research and technology : official journal of International Society for Bioengineering and the Skin (ISBS) [and] International Society for Digital Imaging of Skin (ISDIS) [and] International Society for Skin Imaging (ISSI)

papers.title: Design, Synthesis, and Evaluation of Halo-Substituted Flavonols Against Melanoma A375 Cells.
papers.abstract: Malignant melanoma is one of the most aggressive forms of skin cancer. Despite advances in targeted therapy and immunotherapy, the emergence of drug resistance and limited therapeutic efficacy in advanced stages remain major clinical challenges. In this study, a series of novel flavonols were synthesized and evaluated for their cytotoxic activity against human malignant melanoma A375 cells. Among the tested compounds, compound 4j exhibited the most potent inhibitory effect, with an IC50 value of 25.07 ± 2.24 μM, outperforming 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) used as a positive control. Furthermore, Western blot analysis revealed that compound 4j modulated the expression of key apoptotic regulators: it downregulated the anti-apoptotic protein Bcl-2, upregulated the pro-apoptotic protein Bax, and activated caspase-3, indicating induction of apoptosis via a caspase-dependent mitochondrial pathway. Molecular docking analysis further showed that the halogenated derivatives exhibited distinct interaction patterns within the Bcl-2 binding groove, supporting the observed positional structure-activity relationship. These findings demonstrate that compound 4j possesses promising anticancer activity against malignant melanoma cells. They support flavonols as valuable scaffolds for the development of new anti-melanoma agents, with compound 4j emerging as a particularly compelling lead candidate.

papers.title: Development of a multi-parameter MRI-based habitat radiomics model for differential diagnosis of vestibular schwannoma and meningioma in the cerebellopontine angle: a multi-center study.
papers.abstract: Vestibular schwannomas (VS) and meningiomas (MM) are the most common benign tumors in the cerebellopontine angle (CPA), often presenting with similar clinical symptoms. Accurate preoperative differentiation is essential for appropriate treatment planning. To develop an MRI-based habitat radiomics model for the differential diagnosis of VS and MM in the CPA, integrating multi-parameter MRI data and clinical features. This retrospective study included 176 patients diagnosed with CPA VS or MM from three medical centers: Guangyuan Central Hospital, Nanchong Central Hospital, and Affiliated Hospital of North Sichuan Medical College. 101 patients (68 VS, 33 MM) met the inclusion criteria. Preoperative MRI scans (T2WI and CE-T1WI) were analyzed using a sliding window method for feature extraction, followed by image preprocessing and Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) clustering for habitat subregion segmentation.Habitat radiomics models based on T2WI, CE-T1WI, and fused T2WI & CE-T1WI were constructed respectively, and a combined habitat-clinical model was developed by integrating clinical features, and the models were compared across multiple different machine learning classifiers. Multi-parameter models, combining T2WI and CE-T1WI features, outperformed single-parameter models, achieving AUC values of 0.987 in the training set and 0.974 in the test set. A combined model integrating habitat radiomics and clinical features showed superior diagnostic accuracy. Decision Curve Analysis and calibration curves confirmed its clinical utility and reliability. MRI-based habitat radiomics, when integrated with clinical features, provides a robust, noninvasive method for differentiating CPA VS from MM, offering potential for personalized treatment strategies.

papers.title: UpTCR: a unified progressive knowledge transfer foundation model for robust T-cell receptor-antigen binding recognition.
papers.abstract: T-cell receptor (TCR) recognition of antigenic peptides presented by human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules underpins adaptive immunity and T cell-based immunotherapy. However, the scarcity of complete interaction data and TCR cross-reactivity challenge robust prediction. Here, we present UpTCR, a unified progressive knowledge-transfer foundation model that learns from incomplete data to predict TCR-antigen-HLA binding. UpTCR progressively transfers knowledge from dimeric and trimeric interactions to tetrameric complexes and uses soft contrastive learning to mitigate false negatives. It outperforms existing methods in predicting TCR binding specificity and antigen-HLA binding affinity, particularly for neoantigens, and reveals pairwise residue-level interactions across the tetramer. UpTCR also transfers effectively to breast cancer cohorts with limited data. Prospective validation against melanoma antigen variants identifies eight immunogenic peptides that elicit T cell responses and one variant associated with immune escape. These findings establish UpTCR as a generalizable and interpretable tool for studying antigen recognition and advancing TCR-based immunotherapies.

papers.title: Paraganglioma and childhood-onset optic atrophy in a SDHA compound heterozygous patient: an example of dual dominant and recessive inheritance.
papers.abstract: SDHA pathogenic variants cause moderate to severe complex II deficiency, which manifests as a mitochondrial disorder in a homozygous/compound heterozygous child, or as hereditary cancer, mostly paraganglioma or pheochromocytoma, in a heterozygous adult. Here, we report the first composite heterozygous SDHA patient (hypomorphic allele p.(Thr508Ile) × null allele p.(Arg451His)) who developed complete congenital optic atrophy and a paraganglioma at the age of 36 yrs. No other germline variants were identified by sequencing panels of genes involved in these two disorders. This raises the question of whether paraganglioma screening should be implemented for carriers of a null SDHA variant.

papers.title: Genetic Features in a Case Series of Gastro-entero-pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors.
papers.abstract: Early diagnosis and the size of gastro-entero-pancreatic (GEP) neuroendocrine tumors (NET) represent prognostic factors in patients with multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1). We aimed to present the genetic features and clinical aspects of a case series of NET patients investigated at the National Institute of Endocrinology C.I.Parhon, Bucharest, Romania. 12 patients with NET and associated pathologies (from 9 families) were monitored during 2021-2025. The germline variants of the MEN1 gene were detected by Sanger sequencing and for two patients, next-generation sequencing analysis was used with a clinical exome kit (TruSight One sequencing panel, Illumina, San Diego, CA). The diagnosis of NET was confirmed by histopathologic analysis. Somatostatin receptor status was verified by immunohistochemistry on tumor samples as well as by functional imaging, in vivo. In our group of NET patients, five patients presented a MEN1 pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) variant, one patient had two heterozygous variants of BLM gene suggesting Bloom syndrome diagnosis, and one patient had a BRCA1 variant; five patients were negative for germline clinically relevant variants for NET using aforementioned methods. According to the RECIST1.1 criteria at 1 year after the initiation of therapy, 2/7 presented stable disease, 1/7 partial response and 4/7 progressive disease, and death occurring in 2 cases. In our study, 7 clinically relevant variants were detected: two classified as pathogenic: one nonsense mutation (MEN1: c.778C>T, p.Gln260*) and one heterozygous large deletion in exon 7 (MEN1:c.928_974del, p.Lys310Trpfs*41), three likely pathogenic: MEN1:c.639C>A, p.Ala213=, MEN1:c.520_521insCA, p.His174ProfsTer12, BLM: c.1237_1240del, p.Glu413*, and two were described as variants with uncertain significance (VUS) (BLM:c.98+6T>G, BRCA1: c.4485-10A>G). Advances in molecular medicine techniques, with the discovery of new genes, open the field to precision medicine, both for the prognosis of patients with a NET as well as the options of response to specific treatments.
papers.journal: Journal of gastrointestinal and liver diseases : JGLD

papers.title: Prevention and management of hormonal crisis in neuroendocrine tumors undergoing PRRT (peptide receptor radionuclide therapy): a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) is an established treatment of advanced well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) expressing somatostatin receptors. Although generally well tolerated, PRRT may precipitate or exacerbate pre-existing hormonal syndromes in patients with functioning NETs, leading to acute endocrine decompensation requiring urgent management. Current recommendations from the most important NET societies for prevention and treatment remain inconsistent, and available evidence is still fragmented. To address this gap, we conducted a comprehensive systematic review of the literature in PubMed, Scopus, and Embase up to May 2025, with the aim of identifying, organizing, and critically appraising the existing evidence on prevention and therapeutic strategies for managing hormonal crises in patients undergoing PRRT. Twenty-eight studies were included, comprising 18 case reports/series, 7 retrospective studies, and 3 prospective studies. Reported events included carcinoid crisis, insulinoma-related hypoglycemia, VIPoma-related secretory crisis, ectopic Cushing syndrome exacerbation, and catecholaminergic crisis in pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma. Carcinoid crisis was the most frequently reported endocrine emergency, with available cohort studies suggesting an incidence ∼1% during PRRT, although definitions and reporting remain heterogeneous. Hypoglycemic crises occurred mainly during the first PRRT cycle in patients with insulinoma, supporting the role of inpatient monitoring and preventive glucose-stabilizing strategies. Evidence for rarer syndromes was limited to small series and case reports but consistently emphasized pretreatment endocrine optimization, syndrome-specific prophylaxis, early recognition, and multidisciplinary management. Overall, available data remain insufficient to support firm recommendations but suggest that structured risk assessment, periprocedural monitoring, and harmonized management algorithms are essential to improve PRRT safety in functioning NETs.

papers.title: Sertoli-Leydig Cell Tumour With Heterologous Elements Presenting as Hyperandrogenaemia and Markedly Elevated Alpha-Fetoprotein: A Challenging Diagnosis.
papers.abstract: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumours (SLCTs) are rare ovarian sex cord-stromal tumours that classically present with features of virilisation due to androgen excess and are frequently misdiagnosed as polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS). We report a case of a 33-year-old woman with a three-year history of progressive hirsutism, weight gain, and secondary amenorrhoea, initially attributed to PCOS. An incidental pelvic ultrasound arranged in the context of an endocrinology review revealed a large complex solid-cystic mass measuring 21.2 × 13.8 × 23.4 cm. Tumour markers demonstrated a markedly elevated alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) of 8,147 KU/L, raising initial suspicion of a yolk sac (germ cell) tumour. CT imaging confirmed a 23 cm predominantly cystic pelvic mass with no evidence of metastatic disease. Following multi-disciplinary team discussion and referral to a specialist germ cell tumour MDT, the patient underwent laparotomy and left salpingo-oophorectomy. Initial histology reported an immature teratoma; however, following expert second-opinion review by Professor McCluggage, the final diagnosis was revised to a moderately to poorly differentiated SLCT with heterologous intestinal-type mucinous elements and a small carcinoid component. Ascitic fluid cytology demonstrated no malignant cells. This case highlights the risk of anchoring bias in attributing hyperandrogenaemia to PCOS, the capacity of SLCT with heterologous mucinous elements to mimic germ cell tumours biochemically and histologically, and the indispensable role of expert pathological review in rare ovarian tumours.

papers.title: Spatial epigenomics reveals stromal niche-associated regulatory programs across pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor grades.
papers.abstract: Non-functional pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (NF-PanNETs) account for the majority of pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms and exhibit substantial clinical and biological heterogeneity, yet their epigenetic regulation and spatial architecture remain poorly understood. Here, we present an integrative analysis of NF-PanNETs across multiple tumor grades using single-nucleus advent of transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (snATAC-seq) and spatial ATAC-seq. snATAC-seq identified grade-associated chromatin accessibility programs characterized by distinct transcription factor activities, including HNF1A and FOXA2 in low-grade tumors, ETS family factors in intermediate-grade tumors, SNAI-associated regulatory programs in high-grade tumors, and CEBPB- and TOX-associated immune states. Spatial ATAC-seq revealed spatially coordinated tumor-stroma interactions, with stroma-proximal regions enriched for MYC/FOX-associated proliferative programs and distal regions exhibiting SNAI-enriched invasive programs. Together, our study provides a spatially resolved epigenomic atlas of NF-PanNETs across tumor grades, offering a resource for understanding epigenetic heterogeneity and generating hypotheses regarding regulatory programs and tumor-stroma interactions for future functional and clinical investigation.

papers.title: Retroviral Transduction of Human T Cells with a Chimeric Antigen Receptor Targeting PD-1 Ligands for Melanoma Immunotherapy.
papers.abstract: T cells are able to target melanoma-associated antigens in an MHC-independent manner through the expression of chimeric antigen receptors. Using retroviral transduction, these receptor constructs can be efficiently delivered into human CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ T cells. In this protocol, we describe the production of retroviral supernatants along with the activation, transduction, expansion, and selection of human T cells engineered to express a chimeric PD-1 receptor. This method can be readily adapted for any human chimeric antigen receptor construct.

papers.title: Generation of Murine Chimeric Antigen Receptor T Cells for Adoptive T Cell Therapy for Melanoma.
papers.abstract: Expression of chimeric antigen receptors enables T cells to be redirected toward melanoma-associated antigens in an MHC-independent manner. Retroviral transduction can be used to introduce these receptor constructs into murine CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ T cells. Here, we outline the generation of retroviral supernatants and the activation, transduction, expansion, and selection of murine T cells expressing the chimeric-PD1 receptor. This protocol can be adapted for any murine chimeric antigen receptor construct.

papers.title: Assessing the Antitumor Immune Effects of Gut Microbiota in a Preclinical Melanoma Model.
papers.abstract: Antitumor immune responses are regulated by a multitude of factors, including the gut microbiota. Specific bacterial taxa and metabolites have been correlated with improved responses to immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy in melanoma patients. Gut microbiota and microbiota-derived metabolites can modulate antitumor immune responses by increasing antigen presentation capabilities and enhancing cytotoxic T-cell effector functions. To assess the effects of gut microbiota on antitumor immune responses, we optimized the following protocols focused on immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy in a preclinical melanoma model. Analysis of tumor-infiltrating and circulating lymphocytes, bacterial translocation and growth, and immune cell activation provides a foundation for microbiota/cancer immunology research.

papers.title: Lipoplex Nanoparticle-Based RNA Delivery to 3D Melanoma Spheroids.
papers.abstract: Lipoplex nanoparticle-based vaccination technologies have shown tremendous efficiency for in vivo transfection during the COVID-19 pandemic and also hold promise for treating melanoma. While pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics need careful in vivo and clinical testing, other parameters of drug performance can be assessed with in vitro systems as well. Spheroids composed of more than one cell type can serve to assess drug penetration, cell-type specificity, and transfection efficiency at an early stage of drug development.

papers.title: In Vivo Reversible Electroporation for Melanoma Therapy.
papers.abstract: Reversible Electroporation (rEP) has been a venerable in vitro lab technique for the transfection of cells. Recent in vivo applications of rEP for manipulating tumors and forcing tumor cell expression of proteins of interest are being explored in clinical trials. The ability to perform in vivo rEP in the lab can create translational opportunities and study mechanisms for optimal outcomes in patients. A general protocol is described and may serve as a template for melanoma researchers.

papers.title: Characterization of an Anti-Tryptophan 2,3-Dioxygenase Monoclonal Antibody and Use in a Melanoma Model.
papers.abstract: Monoclonal antibodies have served as research tools to characterize specific proteins and biomolecules to understand their role in biological processes and disease. However, because of nonspecific reactivity with other components in samples, specific reactivity can be difficult to interpret. Using web-based tools, standard hybridoma technology, and standard immunostaining methods, we describe the development of a tryptophan 2,3-dioxygenase 2 (TDO2)-targeted antibody with high specificity. In addition to providing a unique reagent needed as a research tool to investigate the role of TDO2 in preclinical models and human tissue samples, herein we provide methods to characterize TDO2 expression in human tissue samples and murine disease models. We note also that the general protocol described in this chapter will be useful to investigators interested in developing monoclonal antibodies against other targets of interest as well.

papers.title: High-Throughput Identification of miRNA-Target Interactions in Melanoma Using miR-CATCHv2.0.
papers.abstract: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) have the potential to regulate the expression of nearly every transcript in the cell, making the identification of miRNA-mRNA target interactions crucial for understanding their role in diverse biological processes. However, the identification of the miRNAs that regulate a given mRNA remains a challenge. Here, we describe miR-CATCHv2.0, an innovative method for the high-throughput identification of the miRNAs physically interacting with an mRNA of interest. We further highlight how miR-CATCHv2.0 overcomes key limitations of both current computational predictions and existing experimental strategies, enabling a more accurate and comprehensive characterization of physiologically relevant miRNA-mRNA interactions.

papers.title: Assessment of Cell-Free MicroRNA by NGS Whole Transcriptome Analysis in Cutaneous Melanoma Patients' Blood.
papers.abstract: MicroRNAs (miRs) are small RNA molecules (18-22 nucleotides) that regulate the transcriptome at a post-transcriptional level by affecting the expression of specific genes. This regulatory mechanism is critical to maintain cell homeostasis and specific functions. Aberrant expression of miRs has been associated with pathobiological processes, including cancer. There are few technologies available that are able to profile whole-genome miR expression using minimal amounts of blood samples and without the need for time-consuming extraction steps. Here, we describe the HTG EdgeSeq miR Whole Transcriptome Assay (WTA) in serum and plasma samples. To identify specific cell-free miR (cfmiR) patterns, we have first focused on the analysis of normal donor samples and have then compared these to patients with cutaneous melanoma. The identification of specific cfmiR for melanoma patients will allow for better patient surveillance during targeted and/or checkpoint inhibitor immunotherapy (CII) treatment.

papers.title: Unbiased Microbiome and Metabolomic Profiling of Fecal Samples from Patients with Melanoma.
papers.abstract: Gut microbiota influence and modulate host immune responses. In preclinical cancer models, mice lacking gut microbiota have a markedly diminished response to immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy. Further, in melanoma patients, specific commensal gut microbiota have been associated with a positive clinical response to immunotherapy. In order to study the gut microbiome and metabolome, we have developed methods for fecal sample collection and processing, microbiome and metabolome profiling, and bioinformatic analysis. This protocol will be a useful tool for interrogating the taxonomic composition and functional output of a melanoma patient's gut microbiome.

papers.title: Discovery of Salivary Metabolomic Biomarkers for Canine Oral Melanoma and Squamous Cell Carcinoma via CIL LC-MS Analysis.
papers.abstract: In this case-control cross-sectional study, we examined the diagnostic potential of salivary metabolomics to differentiate canine oral melanoma (OM) and oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) from benign oral tumors (BN). Using high-performance chemical isotope labeling liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (CIL LC-MS) targeting at the amine/phenol submetabolome, we analyzed saliva from 65 dogs across malignant, benign, and healthy groups. Our results revealed distinct metabolic clustering among the groups, identifying 154 significantly altered metabolites in OM and 66 in OSCC compared to BN (Padj < 0.05). Notable biomarkers included elevated tryptophyl-threonine and decreased 1,2-dihydroxynaphthalene-6-sulfonic acid in OM, while OSCC was characterized by reduced seryl-arginine and sarcosine. These findings, and the protocol described herein that was used to obtain them, demonstrate the broad coverage of the salivary submetabolome and emphasize the potential of noninvasive metabolic profiling as a practical, high-throughput approach for accurate diagnosis of canine oral cancers in clinical settings.

papers.title: Serum Peptidomic Profiling for Biomarker Discovery in Canine Oral Melanoma and Squamous Cell Carcinoma via MALDI-TOF and LC-MS/MS.
papers.abstract: Canine oral malignancies, particularly oral melanoma (OM) and oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), present significant diagnostic hurdles due to their aggressive metastasis and the difficulty of early-stage detection. This study establishes a robust methodological workflow for identifying systemic biomarkers by analyzing the serum peptidome, a minimally invasive alternative to traditional tissue biopsies. Using a high-throughput approach that combines matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS) for rapid screening with liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) for precise peptide identification, we successfully differentiated early and late-stage malignancies from benign and healthy controls. Principal component analysis confirmed distinct peptidomic clusters, leading to the identification of four key proteins: FKBP4, ESRRA, IGSF10, and ABCB5. Notably, FKBP4, ESRRA, and ABCB5 were overexpressed in both late-stage OM and late-stage OSCC, while IGSF10 showed specificity for late-stage OSCC. These markers are integral to metastatic pathways and correlate with chemotherapeutic sensitivity, providing a foundation for precision diagnostic and prognostic protocols in veterinary oncology.

papers.title: Integrated Functional and Metabolomic Profiling of Melanoma Cells Treated with Redox-Active Compounds.
papers.abstract: Metabolic plasticity is a hallmark of melanoma progression and therapy resistance. This chapter describes a reproducible protocol for comprehensive metabolic profiling of melanoma cells exposed to redox-active compounds such as emodin and aloe-emodin. The method integrates cell proliferation assays, mitochondrial functional analysis using Seahorse extracellular flux measurements, reactive oxygen species (ROS) quantification, LC-MS-based metabolomics, stable-isotope tracing, and 13C metabolic flux analysis (13C-MFA). The workflow enables quantitative characterization of treatment-induced alterations in energy metabolism, redox balance, and central carbon fluxes in melanoma cell lines with distinct metabolic phenotypes. The procedures are presented in a step-by-step format suitable for researchers unfamiliar with the individual techniques and can be adapted to other cancer models or metabolic perturbations.

papers.title: Methods for Analyzing Immune Infiltrates and Spatial Organization Within the Melanoma Microenvironment Using Multiplex Immunofluorescence.
papers.abstract: Immunotherapies improve survival in patients with melanoma by enhancing the immune system's ability to recognize and eliminate tumor cells. Understanding the immunological effects of these therapies requires evaluation of both changes in lymphocyte composition and activation within the tumor microenvironment (TME) as well as the spatial organization of these cells. Increased lymphocyte infiltration and distinct patterns of immune cell distribution within the TME have been associated with improved survival and enhanced response to immunotherapy in melanoma. However, relatively few methodologies currently enable detailed characterization of both the structural organization and immunological features of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes. In this chapter, we describe multiplex immunofluorescence staining approaches for the identification, characterization, and quantification of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes in melanoma.

papers.title: A Method for Quantifying Immune Infiltrates and Tertiary Lymphoid Structures in Murine Melanoma Tumors by Multiplex Immunofluorescence.
papers.abstract: The presence of tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) and elevated levels of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes have been linked to improved survival outcomes in several solid cancers, including melanoma. Despite this association, the precise function and immunological impact of TLS remain incompletely understood, as do factors that drive their formation and which might potentially be leveraged to enhance patient outcomes. Functional studies using murine models may help clarify the biological roles of TLS; however, relatively few methodologies currently exist that allow for detailed assessment of the structural organization and functional characteristics of TLS within solid tumors. To advance understanding of the biology underlying TLS, this chapter describes multiplex immunohistochemistry panels designed for the identification, characterization, and quantification of TLS and intratumoral immune infiltrates in melanoma. Although these methods are presented in the context of melanoma, they are broadly applicable and can be used to investigate TLS across a wide range of human cancers.

papers.title: Preparation of Melanoma Tissue for Multiplex Immunofluorescence Histology Analysis of Immune Infiltration and Spatial Organization.
papers.abstract: Immunotherapies extend survival in melanoma patients by increasing the immune system's capacity to detect tumors and mediate tumor cell death. Understanding mechanisms of antitumor immunity requires evaluating changes in immune infiltrate composition, activation, and spatial distribution within the tumor microenvironment (TME). Despite this need, relatively few methods allow for detailed analysis of both the structural organization and immunological characteristics of tumor-infiltrating immune cells in preclinical cancer models. In this chapter, we present a multiplex immunofluorescence staining approach for identifying, characterizing, and quantifying tumor-infiltrating immune cells in murine melanoma, allowing evaluation of how therapies influence immune infiltration in preclinical models.

papers.title: PET Imaging of Melanoma Using a Melanocortin 1 Receptor-Targeted Probe.
papers.abstract: The melanocortin-1 receptor (MC1R) is overexpressed in more than 80% of melanoma cells but is expressed at low levels in normal tissues, making it an important target for melanoma imaging and therapy. Recently, MC1R has attracted the interest of numerous researchers as a target for melanoma. Radiolabeled alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH) peptides bind specifically to MC1R and internalize into tumor cells, enabling melanoma diagnosis and therapy. Several radiolabeled α-MSH peptides have been developed. Among those, a cyclized α-MSH peptide produced via an alternative click chemistry cyclization strategy offers faster and more specific bindings to MC1R. It could be labeled with ²0³Pb/²¹²Pb (VMT01) for melanoma single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) imaging and therapy and also could be labeled with 68Ga (VMT02) for positron emission tomography (PET) imaging. Preliminary clinical imaging showed highly sensitive and specific melanoma detection. This chapter describes the synthesis of VMT02 and PET/CT imaging procedures in both mouse models and patients.

papers.title: SPECT Imaging of Melanoma Using a 99mTc-Labeled Melanin-Targeted Probe.
papers.abstract: Melanoma is a highly aggressive cutaneous malignancy characterized by a poor clinical prognosis, making early and accurate detection paramount for patient survival. Melanin, abundantly expressed in most melanoma lesions, serves as an ideal and highly specific biomarker for targeted molecular imaging. While various imaging modalities exist, single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) provides a highly accessible and cost-effective strategy for widespread clinical translation. From our recent studies, 99mTc-SMIC-4006 emerged as the optimal 99mTc-labeled radiotracer, demonstrating exceptional radiochemical purity, highly specific melanin binding, and superior tumor-to-blood contrast in B16F10 melanoma xenografts. Herein, we describe the detailed radiosynthesis protocol for 99mTc-SMIC-4006, alongside comprehensive procedures for its in vitro property evaluation and in vivo SPECT/CT imaging in preclinical melanoma models.

papers.title: PET Imaging of Melanoma Using a Melanin-Targeted Probe.
papers.abstract: Melanin exists in most melanoma lesions. Melanin plays an important role in melanoma progression, metastasis, therapy response, and the overall survival of patients. Therefore, melanin is a critical target for melanoma diagnosis and therapy. Many melanin-targeting probes, such as radioisotope-labeled benzamide analogs, have been developed for melanoma diagnosis using positron emission tomography (PET). The N-(2-(diethylamino)-ethyl)-18F-5-fluoropicolinamide (18F-P3BZA) probe is one of the benzamide analogs and has been preliminarily tested for clinical diagnosis of melanoma in our recent studies. It has shown high specificity and favorable in vivo performance for PET imaging of melanoma. Herein, we describe the detailed synthesis protocol of 18F-P3BZA and the PET/CT imaging procedure for animal models and patients.

papers.title: Radiopharmaceuticals for Melanoma Theranostics.
papers.abstract: Malignant melanoma (MM) remains a formidable clinical challenge due to its high metastatic potential and the eventual emergence of resistance to current BRAF/MEK and immune checkpoint inhibitors. To address these limitations, the theranostic strategy integrating diagnostic imaging with targeted radionuclide therapy to enable personalized treatment has gained significant traction. Current research primarily exploits the overexpression of the melanocortin 1 receptor (MC1R), very late antigen-4 (VLA-4), and melanin as primary molecular targets for radiopharmaceutical development. For MC1R, α-MSH peptide analogs have been engineered with β-emitters such as 177Lu and 90Y for peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT), as well as α-emitters like 225Ac and 212Pb (β- decay to 212Bi and then emit α particles) for targeted alpha therapy (TAT), showing high specificity and rapid clearance. Concurrently, VLA-4-targeted platforms utilizing high-affinity LLP2A ligands have been optimized through PEGylation and albumin-binding strategies to enhance bioavailability and tumor retention. Beyond these primary receptors, this review evaluates alternative strategies, including copper transporter (CTR1) targeting with 64CuCl2 and the use of gold nanocages for multimodal applications. Together, these advancements represent a critical shift toward image-guided, dosimetry-driven radionuclide therapies that may work synergistically with existing immunotherapies to improve survival in metastatic melanoma.

papers.title: Multi-Analyte Responsive Fluorescent Sensing of Pathological Cellular States in Melanoma.
papers.abstract: Melanoma progression involves multiple biomarkers and signaling pathways, and relying on a single marker can lead to incomplete or inaccurate diagnoses. Multi-analyte sensors allow simultaneous monitoring of several biomarkers, providing a more comprehensive picture of the tumor microenvironment, identifying distinct cellular states, and improving diagnostic accuracy. This chapter presents protocols that can be used for fluorescence sensing of the melanoma marker enzyme tyrosinase in conjunction with different In Vitro microenvironmental signals, including hypoxia and reactive oxygen species.

papers.title: Design Strategies for Melanoma-Targeting Fluorescent Probes.
papers.abstract: Melanoma is responsible for most skin cancer-related mortalities, and clinical urgency drives the development of novel diagnostic tools. Precision diagnostics relying on fluorescence output provide many advantages, including easy and noninvasive readout and a high signal-to-noise ratio that is enabled through a change in the intensity or the wavelength of fluorescence in response to disease-associated parameters. This chapter explores the chemical design strategies for fluorescent probes, focusing on the exploitation of melanogenic enzymes, protein biomarkers, and the targeting of the dysregulated tumor microenvironment to achieve unprecedented diagnostic precision.

papers.title: Imaging and Isolation of Extravasation-Participating Endothelial and Melanoma Cells During Angiopellosis.
papers.abstract: Cancer mortality is driven largely by metastatic progression rather than by primary tumor burden. The ability of circulating tumor cells (CTCs) to exit the vasculature and invade surrounding tissues-known as extravasation-is a critical and rate-limiting step in metastasis. Recent advances in high-resolution intravital microscopy have made it possible to directly visualize this process in vivo, enabling real-time imaging of individual CTCs as they interact with, transmigrate through, and recruit components of the endothelium. In this chapter, we describe intravital microscopy approaches that allow for both visualization and isolation of extravasating CTCs, as well as the endothelial cells that actively participate in their transendothelial migration. These methods provide a powerful platform for dissecting the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying metastatic spread. Beyond mechanistic insights, the approach can also serve as a functional screening system for evaluating anticancer therapeutics that target CTC behavior, endothelial interactions, or early metastatic niche formation.

papers.title: Detection of Biomarkers for EMT-Associated Phenotype Switching in Melanoma-Derived Extracellular Vesicles.
papers.abstract: Melanoma cells exhibit epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-like phenotype switching during targeted therapy, which contributes to the development of drug resistance. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) released by melanoma cells carry surface proteins reflective of this EMT-associated transition, providing an accessible window to track therapeutic response. This chapter presents a step-by-step protocol for profiling EMT-related melanoma EV protein signatures directly from unpurified sera using a microfluidic surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) biosensing platform. The method integrates melanoma-specific EV capture, alternating current-electrohydrodynamic nanomixing-enhanced binding, and multiplex SERS nanotag labeling to enable sensitive quantification of EMT surface markers in a streamlined assay. Detailed instructions for reagent preparation, SERS nanotag synthesis, biosensor fabrication and operation, spectral acquisition, and data processing are provided to support implementation in melanoma translational research laboratories. This protocol enables reproducible monitoring of EMT-like phenotypic evolution in melanoma models and patient samples and may assist future studies aiming to predict or mechanistically dissect resistance to targeted therapy.

papers.title: Imaging and Analysis of Melanoma-Secreted Extracellular Vesicles in Tumor-Draining Lymph Nodes.
papers.abstract: Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) are key mediators of intercellular communication and play important roles in both physiological and pathological processes. In cancer, sEVs mediate communication between the tumor and its microenvironment but also contribute to metastatic organotropism and the formation of pre-metastatic niches in regional and distant organs. Lymph nodes (LNs) are central regulators of immune responses and primary sites of early metastasis, and, as such, they are critical targets for understanding cancer progression and improving immunotherapy. sEVs contribute to the conditioning of lymph nodes during pre-metastatic niche formation by altering lymphatic endothelial cell function and modulating immune cell populations, thereby promoting tumor progression. Because these interactions are complex and dynamic, their study requires in vivo models and specifically tailored sEVs-based techniques. In this chapter, we describe several approaches for studying sEVs in the LN context, including biodistribution analysis in the lymphatic system, imaging by immunofluorescence, and uptake measurement by flow cytometry.

papers.title: Post-Lymphadenectomy Analysis of Small Extracellular Vesicles from Lymphatic Drainage/Exudative Seroma of Melanoma Patients.
papers.abstract: Circulating extracellular vesicles (EVs) have emerged as a promising source of disease biomarkers in biofluids. Although multiple isolation methods are available, differential ultracentrifugation remains a gold standard for small EV purification. Small EVs purified using this approach retain functional activity both in vitro and in vivo and are suitable for downstream applications, including proteomics, electron microscopy, mass spectrometry, and nucleic acid analysis. An additional purification step, either by density gradient centrifugation or size-exclusion chromatography, allows for the isolation of highly pure EV fractions for subsequent biomarker analysis. Here, we describe a protocol based on differential ultracentrifugation followed by a density gradient centrifugation or size exclusion chromatography step for the recovery of highly pure small extracellular vesicles (EVs) from lymphatic exudate (seroma) collected following lymphadenectomy, with the aim of supporting biomarker discovery and liquid biopsy applications.

papers.title: A Rapid Exosome Isolation Using Ultrafiltration and Size Exclusion Chromatography (REIUS) Method for Exosome Isolation from Melanoma Cell Lines.
papers.abstract: Cells release extracellular vesicles (EVs) that can be detected both in vivo and in cell culture medium. Among EVs, exosomes are 50-150 nm vesicles that are systematically packaged into multivesicular bodies for release into the external environment. In cancer, these intentionally packaged exosomes carry a payload of molecules such as protein, RNA, and surface receptors that facilitate the reprogramming of proximal cells to assemble a pro-tumor microenvironment. Exosomes have been implicated as an important intermediary extracellular communication pathway between cells, including in melanoma. Human melanoma-derived exosomes (HMEX) have been demonstrated to modulate the extracellular environment and inhibit immune cell activation. There are many methods to isolate and enrich for exosomes, and the method applied can impact yield and purity of the isolates. In this chapter, we describe the REIUS (Rapid Exosome Isolation Using Size exclusion chromatography) method to isolate HMEX from melanoma cell cultures and then demonstrate their enrichment using molecular and microscopic approaches.

papers.title: Capture and Isolation of Circulating Melanoma Cells Using Photoacoustic Flowmetry.
papers.abstract: Early detection of cancer has been a goal of cancer research in general and melanoma research in particular. Early detection of metastasis has been targeted as pivotal to increasing survival rates. Melanoma, though curable in its early stages, has a dramatic decrease in survival rates once metastasis has occurred. The transition to metastasis is not well understood and is an area of increasing interest. Metastasis is always premeditated by the shedding of circulating tumor cells (CTCs) from the primary tumor. The ability to isolate rare CTCs from the bloodstream has led to a host of new targets and therapies for cancer. Detection of CTCs also allows for disease progression to be tracked in real time while eliminating the need to wait for additional tumors to grow.
