Key Messages Functioning as an important regulator, SP maintains physiological balance in health yet drives disease progression in diabetes, pancreatitis, and pancreatic cancer. The SP/NK-1R axis has therapeutic potential with its beneficial actions.

papers.title: Identification and characterization of a novel distinct Pineal Neoplasm with Neuroendocrine and Epithelial Differentiation (PINNED).
papers.abstract: Pineal region tumors are rare neoplasms that occur in all ages and account for less than 1% of all central nervous system (CNS) tumors in adults but are more frequent in children. Here, we describe a previously unrecognized tumor type of pineal origin characterized by a unique and consistent DNA methylation profile that does not match any known CNS tumor class and is distinct from all currently recognized pineal tumor entities. The presented cohort (n = 27) displayed a balanced sex distribution with a mean patient age of 35 years (range 7-75 years). The histopathological analyses demonstrated a highly cellular tumor showing various degrees of necrosis, mitotic activity, papillary structures, rosettes, epithelioid cytology, or signet-ring cells. The tumors consistently expressed cytokeratin 18, synaptophysin, chromogranin A, and OTX2, whereas CRX expression was absent. Four out of 16 tumors (25%) showed ATRX mutations and/or loss of protein expression as revealed by immunohistochemistry. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing confirmed molecular distinctiveness from other pineal neoplasms but revealed the closest similarities to papillary tumors of the pineal region (PTPR). Projection of the transcriptome data onto the cellular trajectory of the developing murine pineal gland suggests that pinealocyte progenitors are the cellular origins. Taken together, our findings define a novel type of pineal region tumor that we provisionally named 'Pineal Neoplasm with Neuroendocrine and Epithelial Differentiation' (PINNED). Recognition of this tumor type appears to be important for the accurate diagnosis of pineal region tumors and may have implications for future tumor classification and treatment strategies.

papers.title: Case Report: A germline SDHB c.268C>T (p.Arg90Ter) variant in a family with very-early-onset colorectal neoplasia
Association of endoscopic and CT response with pathological response after preoperative FLOT-based therapy for gastric and gastroesophageal junction cancer: a retrospective cohort study
Delayed-Onset Malignant Hyperthermia With Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation Following Successful Prior Anesthetic Use: A Case Report
A unique case of thymic indolent T-lymphoblastic proliferation: Redefining the extrathymic boundaries.
papers.abstract: Per the WHO Classification of Haematolymphoid Tumours (5th edition), indolent T-lymphoblastic proliferation (iT-LBP) is defined as an extrathymic non-clonal proliferation of T lymphoblasts that typically presents as isolated lymphadenopathy or an isolated tumor mass in an otherwise healthy individual. Unlike T-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (T-ALL/LBL), an aggressive hematologic malignancy characterized by monoclonal T-lymphoblasts and requiring treatment with chemotherapy, iT-LBP is an indolent process that does not require any specific treatment. We report a case of an indolent T-lymphoblastic proliferation with subsequently diagnosed Graves' disease presenting as a mediastinal mass in a young, otherwise healthy woman. Consistent with this diagnosis, she has had a benign clinical course. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported case of an iT-LBP-like entity in the thymus, suggesting an expansion of the definition of iT-LBP. Therefore, it is critical for pathologists to be aware that this entity can involve the thymus and not mistake it for other malignancies, especially T-ALL/LBL, given the significant differences in prognosis and management.
papers.journal: Pathobiology : journal of immunopathology, molecular and cellular biology

papers.title: Comparison of 68Ga-FAPI PET/CT and 18F-FDG PET/CT in gastric cancer: impact on metastatic detection and stage migration.
papers.abstract:
Objectives

To compare the diagnostic performance of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) PET/CT and ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT in patients with gastric cancer, with particular emphasis on metastatic detection and stage migration.

Methods

Fifty-two patients with histopathologically confirmed gastric cancer who underwent both 18F-FDG PET/CT and ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT were retrospectively analyzed. Primary tumor uptake, metastatic involvement, and tumor staging were evaluated for each modality. Detection rates for lymph node, peritoneal, liver, and bone metastases were compared. Diagnostic performance and stage migration between modalities were assessed. Quantitative parameters including standardized uptake value and tumor-to-background ratio were analyzed.

Results

⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT demonstrated significantly higher uptake in primary tumors compared with 18F-FDG PET/CT (P < .001). Peritoneal metastases were detected in 30.8% (16/52) of patients on ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT compared with 13.5% (7/52) on 18F-FDG PET/CT (P = .004). Nodal metastases were also identified more frequently with ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT. Both modalities showed high diagnostic performance for liver metastases, while ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT demonstrated slightly higher sensitivity for bone lesions and 18F-FDG PET/CT showed slightly higher specificity. Overall stage migration between the 2 modalities occurred in 25.0% (13/52) of patients, predominantly due to upstaging associated with newly detected metastatic disease. In subgroup analysis, 18F-FDG uptake tended to be lower in signet-ring cell carcinoma, whereas FAPI uptake appeared less influenced by histological subtype.

Conclusion

: ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT improves detection of metastatic disease, particularly peritoneal involvement, compared with 18F-FDG PET/CT in patients with gastric cancer and may contribute to more accurate disease staging.

Advances in knowledge

This study highlights the added value of 68Ga-FAPI PET/CT in identifying metastatic disease and altering clinical staging, particularly through improved detection of peritoneal involvement, which may impact treatment decision-making.

papers.title: C3a/C3aR1 axis promotes invasion of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma and is associated with metastasis and poor prognosis.
papers.abstract: Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) is the most common metastatic skin cancer, with poor prognosis of metastatic disease. We investigated the role of the complement axis C3a/C3aR1 in CSCC progression. C3aR1 mRNA levels were elevated in CSCC tumors in vivo compared with normal skin. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed C3aR1 expression in macrophages within CSCCs. In 3D spheroid co-cultures of CSCC cells, fibroblasts, and macrophages, RNA sequencing showed increased C3aR1 mRNA expression in the presence of M2-like macrophages. Immunofluorescence staining localized C3aR1-expressing cells predominantly at the peripheral region of spheroids. Recombinant C3a enhanced CSCC cell invasion, whereas C3aR1 inhibitor SB290157 inhibited their invasion in co-culture with fibroblasts and macrophages. Immunohistochemistry of normal skin, actinic keratoses, CSCC in situ, CSCC, and metastases demonstrated C3aR1 expression on tumor cells in a subset of metastatic CSCCs and metastases. All C3aR1-positive primary tumors were high-risk (Clark level V; AJCC stage III-IV). Multiplexed immunofluorescence showed that increase in C3aR1-positive tumor cells, M2-like macrophages, and cancer-associated fibroblasts in CSCC was associated with metastasis risk and poor disease-specific survival. These findings support a role for C3a/C3aR1 signaling in CSCC invasion and metastasis and identify C3aR1 as a potential therapeutic target in advanced disease.

papers.title: <sup>68</sup>Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT for Detection of Locoregional Lymph Node Metastases in Gynecologic Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract:
Background/aim

Detection of locoregional lymph node (LN) metastases is a critical prognostic factor in gynecologic squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) is limited by insufficient specificity, potentially leading to overtreatment. We evaluated gallium-68 fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (68Ga-FAPI-04) positron-emission tomography (PET)/CT for the detection of locoregional LN metastases in this setting, using CT as comparator.

Patients and methods

In this retrospective single-center study, 68Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT scans of 15 patients with gynecologic SCC (nine cervical, six vulvar carcinomas; mean age 56.3 years, range=38-86 years) were analyzed. PET/CT and CT were read independently by two blinded readers. Histopathology and/or clinical and radiological follow-up (12-18 months) served as the reference standard. Diagnostic performance was calculated on a patient-based level; maximum standardized uptake values (SUVmax) were compared using Welch's t-test and the Mann-Whitney U-test.

Results

Histopathological confirmation was available in 12 patients; three were classified by follow-up. LN metastases were confirmed in five patients. 68Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT achieved a sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV) and accuracy of 100%. CT achieved a sensitivity and NPV of 100% but produced false-positive findings in three patients (specificity=70%, PPV=62.5%, accuracy=80%), caused by tattoo-associated lymphadenopathy, sarcoidosis and reactive nodal enlargement, none of which showed pathological tracer uptake. Metastatic LNs exhibited higher SUVmax (mean 23.2±6.0) than nodes false-positive on CT (mean 4.5±4.6; p=0.004 and p=0.036). Primary tumors were visualized in all patients undergoing initial staging; peritoneal nodules down to 7 mm were detected.

Conclusion

In this small cohort, 68Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT showed a higher observed specificity than contrast-enhanced CT for the detection of locoregional LN metastases in gynecologic SCC, with no false-negative cases observed.

papers.title: Functional Recovery After Severe Postoperative Decline in Glioblastoma: The Importance of Reassessing Treatment Eligibility
Longitudinal Spatial Proteomics of Breast Cancer Reveals Recurrent Phenotypic Clone States and Temporal Trajectories.
papers.abstract: Intratumoral heterogeneity complicates treatment response and relapse in breast cancer, yet longitudinal spatial studies that preserve tissue architecture remain scarce. Here we integrated matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry imaging (MALDI-MSI) with region-resolved dia-PASEF proteomics to map recurrent spatial proteomic programs across serial breast cancer specimens. Forty-seven formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissues from 16 patients were analyzed, encompassing primary tumors, relapses, and metastatic lesions. Cohort-level MSI co-segmentation provided a common reference atlas of 10 recurrent spectral states, and pathologist-guided microextraction of 201 tumor-containing regions yielded 402 extraction-level proteomic datasets. Because no genomic lineage tracing was performed, we use the term recurrent spatial proteomic state to denote a spatially localized, recurrent proteomic phenotype and not a genetically proven clone. Recurrent spatial proteomic states were observed across hormone receptor-positive, HER2-positive, and hormone receptor-negative/HER2-low disease, indicating that similar spatial programs can recur across clinical subtypes. Longitudinal analyses of representative patients showed marked state turnover during therapy, with persistence of some states and emergence of others at relapse or metastatic progression. Feature-ranking models identified proteins associated with each spatial state and with clinical sampling stage, while exploratory enrichment analyses suggested broad shifts from earlier immune- and hormone-associated programs toward later inflammatory, invasive, and stress-adapted programs. Because the cohort is modest, repeated regions from the same patient are not independent, and no external validation cohort was available, all predictive and therapeutic interpretations are presented as hypothesis-generating. These data provide a spatial proteomic atlas of recurrent spatial proteomic states in breast cancer and a framework for studying constrained, but not deterministic, evolutionary trajectories during progression and treatment.

papers.title: Adrenocortical Carcinoma: A Case Report on the Diagnostic and Therapeutic Approach
Delayed intraparenchymal pneumocephalus causing internal capsule injury after endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery for recurrent Rathke's cleft cyst: illustrative case.
papers.abstract:
Background

Pneumocephalus is a rare but serious complication after endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery (ETSS), usually associated with CSF leakage and occasionally progressing to tension pneumocephalus. Delayed intraparenchymal pneumocephalus causing focal brain injury after ETSS for recurrent Rathke's cleft cyst (RCC) is exceptionally rare.

Observations

A 74-year-old woman underwent ETSS for recurrent RCC and was discharged on postoperative day (POD) 10 after an uneventful early course. On POD 37, she developed sudden left hemiparesis and mild dysarthria. Head CT demonstrated pneumocephalus extending from the sella toward the right internal capsule without rhinorrhea. With conservative management, the pneumocephalus gradually resolved, revealing parenchymal injury involving the posterior limb of the right internal capsule on CT and MRI. She later reported repeated nose blowing after discharge, including on the morning of symptom onset. Intraoperative endoscopic review revealed a depression in the anterior perforated substance, anatomically corresponding to the ruptured RCC and subsequent injury site.

Lessons

In recurrent or ruptured RCCs, occult communication between the sellar region and adjacent brain may permit air entry after postoperative Valsalva maneuvers. Strict counseling, recognition of high-risk parenchymal findings, and airtight multilayer reconstruction with a vascularized mucosal flap may reduce this risk. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26647.

papers.title: Beyond breathing: Lung as a sensory organ.
papers.abstract: The lung, one the largest branching organs in our body and vital for survival at first breath, is commonly known as the gas exchange organ. Recent novel findings on lung sensing cells, molecules, and lung-brain crosstalk in the emerging discipline of interoception have highlighted the consideration of the lung as a sensory organ. Acknowledging the central importance of lung sensing to human health and disease, the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute convened a workshop to synthesize the past, current, and future of lung sensing research, with in-person presentations by approximately 20 interdisciplinary experts and a large virtual audience. Here, we highlight the key topics discussed and summarize a blueprint for the future in this important field.
papers.journal: American journal of respiratory cell and molecular biology

papers.title: Multidisciplinary Treatment of Abdominal Wall Recurrence After Bladder Perforation During Transurethral Resection of a Bladder Tumor.
papers.abstract:
Introduction

Sarcomatoid urothelial carcinoma is a rare, highly aggressive bladder cancer subtype. We report the first case of abdominal wall implantation of sarcomatoid urothelial carcinoma after bladder perforation during transurethral resection of a bladder tumor, followed by recurrence at the open repair site requiring further resection.

Case presentation

A 73-year-old woman underwent emergency transurethral resection for a rapidly enlarging bladder tumor complicated by full-thickness perforation. Histopathology revealed sarcomatoid urothelial carcinoma. During intravesical bacillus Calmette-Guérin therapy, she developed a malignant right lower abdominal wall mass attributed to tumor implantation. Enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab did not prevent progression. Preoperative radiotherapy was followed by en bloc resection with partial cystectomy and anterolateral thigh flap reconstruction. Pathology demonstrated extensive treatment-related necrosis and negative margins. She remained recurrence-free at 11 months.

Conclusion

For localized recurrence, aggressive multidisciplinary treatment incorporating radical local resection and reconstructive surgery may provide local disease control in selected patients without metastasis.

papers.title: The evolving landscape of hybrid viral vector architectures: a persisting niche
Left Medial Liver Lobe Torsion Associated With Hepatocellular Carcinoma in a Pembroke Welsh Corgi: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Liver lobe torsion (LLT) is a rare, potentially life-threatening condition in dogs and is reported most often in medium- to large-breed dogs. Neoplasia-associated LLT is unusual, and detailed descriptions of LLT associated with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) are scarce. A 12-year-old spayed female Pembroke Welsh Corgi (9.5 kg) presented with acute collapse after several months of progressive lethargy and inappetence. Laboratory abnormalities included increased alanine aminotransferase and aspartate aminotransferase activities and C-reactive protein concentration. Computed tomography (CT) identified a 7.2 × 6.7 × 6.5 cm mass arising from the left medial liver lobe, a whirl sign at the base of the mass and a non-enhancing hypoattenuating region consistent with necrosis. Midline celiotomy and left medial liver lobectomy were performed without detorsion. Cytology of abdominal effusion was consistent with a culture-negative inflammatory exudate. Histopathology confirmed HCC with extensive necrosis, and the examined surgical margin was free of neoplastic cells. The dog recovered uneventfully, was discharged on postoperative Day 4 and had no recurrence of clinical abnormalities at 1-year follow-up. This case highlights the apparent association between HCC and LLT and the unusual location of the torsion axis at the base of the mass rather than at the hepatic hilus, although causality cannot be established from a single case. CT visualisation of the whirl sign at this atypical site was instrumental in establishing the preoperative diagnosis and guiding surgical planning.

papers.title: Primary Hepatic Neuroblastoma: A Case Report of a Solitary Liver Mass in an Adolescent Male
Surgical Management and Outcomes of Relapsed and Refractory Hepatoblastoma: An Institutional Case Series.
papers.abstract: Relapse occurs in 10%-20% of children with hepatoblastoma and is associated with inferior outcomes, yet standardized management remains limited. Defining risk factors and relapse patterns, as well as the role of surgery, particularly transplantation, is critical to optimizing survival. A retrospective review was performed of patients aged 0-18 years diagnosed with hepatoblastoma from 2007 to 2024. Demographics, tumor characteristics, treatment course, relapse patterns, and outcomes were collected. Analyses included univariable and multivariable logistic regression, Kaplan-Meier survival estimation, and log-rank testing. Among 135 patients, 98 (72.6%) achieved remission without relapse, 32 (23.7%) relapsed, and 5 (3.7%) experienced primary progression without remission. Older age, PRETEXT (pretreatment extent of disease) IV, metastatic disease at diagnosis, and macrovascular invasion were associated with relapse on univariable analysis, but only older age remained independently associated with relapse (adjusted odds ratio 1.27 per year, 95% confidence interval 1.05-1.53); PRETEXT IV and metastatic disease were not significantly associated with overall survival. Lung-only relapse demonstrated favorable survival (100% alive), whereas combined liver and lung or extrahepatic relapse had poorer outcomes (40%-44% alive), although survival did not differ significantly across relapse sites (p = 0.15). Of 54 liver transplant recipients, 44 underwent upfront transplantation, and 10 underwent salvage transplantation, with no significant difference in overall survival (p = 0.90), although the salvage group was small. Relapse or progression after upfront transplantation occurred in 27% of recipients; lung-only relapse again conferred favorable survival. Long-term survival is achievable in relapsed hepatoblastoma, particularly for isolated pulmonary relapse. Older age, likely a surrogate for adverse tumor biology, was associated with relapse but did not preclude survival when aggressive multimodal therapy was used. Salvage transplantation achieved durable survival in selected patients and should be considered for unresectable intrahepatic relapse when extrahepatic disease is absent or controlled.

papers.title: A Prospective Study on Challenges in the Management of Indeterminate Thyroid Nodules Without Molecular Testing.
papers.abstract:
Introduction

Treating indeterminate thyroid nodules (ITNs) without validated molecular testing (MT) has been challenging. However, adding specific clinical and radiological parameters helps us to decide on treatment for a few individuals. The risk of malignancy in ITN after eliminating the obvious risk parameters needs to be studied.

Methods

This prospective single-centre analysis included patients who underwent fine needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) of thyroid between March 2022 and October 2023. The study included patients with thyroid nodules classified as Bethesda III/IV who subsequently underwent surgery. Different clinicopathological and FNAC-related parameters were statistically analysed to predict malignancy, after excluding those factors that would strongly suggest malignancy.

Results

Among 1501 patients who underwent FNAC, 207 met the inclusion criteria. The mean age of the study population was 39 ± 12.1 years, and the majority were women (80.2%). Among the ITNs, 86% were Bethesda III, and 14% were Bethesda IV nodules. The risk of malignancy in Bethesda III and IV nodules was 67.4% and 69%, respectively. On multivariate analysis, it was noted that hypothyroidism was the single independent factor that predicted malignancy associated with a significant odds of 0.309 (95%CI:0.127-0.784, p = 0.013). The most common malignancy among ITNs was the follicular variant of papillary thyroid carcinoma.

Conclusion

Women less than 40 years of age, in this cohort, had a higher risk of malignancy compared to the Western population. More than half of the patients diagnosed with ITN underwent surgery. Hypothyroidism is an independent factor that may predict the risk of malignancy in ITNs, and this needs external validation. Rule-in MT might be important in categorizing patients with ITN in the Indian population.

papers.title: Acute visual deterioration following endoscopic transsphenoidal resection of a pituitary adenoma secondary to a de novo cyst of normal pituitary origin: illustrative case.
papers.abstract:
Background

Pituitary adenomas (PAs) are common benign intracranial neoplasms. Transsphenoidal resection is the standard of care for symptomatic tumors, with surgical complications including CSF leakage, infection, hormonal disturbances, and postoperative hematomas leading to visual decline. Rapid postoperative cyst development leading to acute visual deterioration is a rare but potentially significant complication.

Observations

A 63-year-old female with headaches and pulsatile tinnitus presented with a large PA compressing the optic apparatus. Transsphenoidal surgery (TSS) via an endoscopic endonasal approach was performed. On postoperative day 6, the patient experienced rapid onset of bitemporal hemianopsia, and imaging revealed a new suprasellar cystic lesion. The patient underwent emergency craniotomy for cyst resection, with pathological analysis demonstrating a nonneoplastic anterior pituitary gland. A systematic literature review of rapid cyst formation following TSS yielded only 1 article for inclusion. No cases of a postoperative cyst of normal pituitary gland origin were identified.

Lessons

Visual decline following TSS is typically due to a sellar/suprasellar hematoma, abscess, or CSF accumulation. Few reports attribute acute postoperative visual deterioration to the development of a secondary pituitary mass, typically due to PA recurrence or formation of a suprasellar cyst. Emergency cyst resection via a transcranial approach resulted in restoration of vision and preservation of pituitary function, supporting aggressive surgical management. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26459.

papers.title: Radioembolization for Colorectal Liver Metastases: Indications and Outcomes.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, with the liver representing the predominant site of metastatic spread. For patients with colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) who are not candidates for surgical resection, systemic chemotherapy provides disease control but rarely achieves durable hepatic responses. Radioembolization with yttrium-90 (Y-90) microspheres, delivered via the hepatic artery to exploit the preferential arterial supply of liver tumors, has emerged as an important locoregional option in this setting. This review examines the current evidence base for radioembolization in CRLM, covering patient selection, indications across lines of therapy, dosimetric advances, and clinical outcomes. Appropriate candidacy requires careful assessment of performance status, hepatic tumor burden, tumor biology, lung shunt fraction, and extrahepatic disease extent, with the strongest outcomes observed in patients selected earlier in their disease course. Randomized controlled trials support second-line and third-line use, while unselected first-line use has not demonstrated a benefit. Dosimetric advances, including multicompartment personalized dosing, radiation segmentectomy, and radiation lobectomy, are enabling ablative and bridge-to-resection strategies in appropriately selected patients. Future investigation should prioritize biomarker-driven patient selection, personalized dosimetry, and combination strategies with systemic therapy to determine whether durable hepatic disease control can translate into a survival benefit.

papers.title: A Unique Case of Odontoid Metastasis Reveals Nasopharynx Carcinoma: Case Management With the Posterolateral Epidural Supra-C2-Root Approach (PESCA) Technique in Open Surgery
Immune checkpoints: cross-disease insights and clinical dilemmas.
papers.abstract: The immune checkpoints and their inhibitors are revolutionary advances in tumour immunotherapy. Immune checkpoints, however, have a broad spectrum effect. They not only contribute to tumour immune escape, but also are involved in the regulation of the pathopathological processes of numerous inflammatory illnesses, such as sepsis, autoimmune diseases, organ transplant rejection, and viral infections, among others. Today, a considerable gap in knowledge remains regarding immune checkpoints and immune checkpoint inhibitors in non-tumour inflammatory diseases, which remains largely unaddressed. At the same time, the emergence of immune-related adverse events and resistance challenges related to the clinical use of immune checkpoint inhibitors is becoming increasingly prominent, posing a significant obstacle to their application across various diseases. To overcome such issues, this narrative review establishes a systematic framework that links immune checkpoints to various inflammatory diseases and explores the associated therapeutic and clinical challenges. These diseases pose therapeutic and clinical challenges of immune checkpoint inhibitors, which we explore. The paper not only thoroughly describes the clinical picture, pathophysiology, and interventions in immunologic adverse events but also suggests a prospective strategy to confront the existing problems with immune checkpoint inhibitors in 3 dimensions: evaluation, management, and prevention. It will attempt to present a new conceptual framework for a comprehensive understanding of the dual role of immune checkpoints (in maintaining immune homeostasis and facilitating disease progression) and to provide a solid theoretical foundation for the development of safer and more effective cross-disease immunotherapy.

papers.title: Dynamic control of carbon-ion radiation dose distribution amid respiratory motion challenges: A review of prediction research using geant4 and deep learning physics-constrained models.
papers.abstract:
Background

Carbon ion radiotherapy (CIRT) offers superior dose conformity and biological effectiveness; however, its precision is highly sensitive to respiratory motion, leading to dose uncertainty and interplay effects that compromise treatment accuracy.

Methods

A comprehensive literature synthesis was conducted on studies employing motion-resolved imaging techniques (e.g. SMEIR), dynamic dose prediction, 4D robust planning, and hybrid adaptive methods for CIRT. The study emphasised the use of Geant4 Monte Carlo simulations combined with deep learning models, including physics-informed neural networks, to simulate and predict dose perturbations caused by respiratory motion. This review also examined clinical treatment planning systems, radiobiological modelling, and adaptive strategies to mitigate the effects of motion.

Results

The integration of Geant4 with deep learning enabled high-fidelity, computationally efficient dose prediction under respiratory motion, improving accuracy in dose localization and adaptation. Motion management techniques such as respiratory gating, rescanning, and 4D robust optimization demonstrated enhanced tumor control and normal tissue sparing. Hybrid models combining Monte Carlo data and AI inference show promise for near-real-time adaptive therapy. Despite these advances, challenges remain, including limited motion-rich datasets, computational demands for real-time recalculations, and the complexity of incorporating variable relative biological effectiveness (RBE) into adaptive planning.

Conclusions

Combining Geant4-based Monte Carlo simulations with deep learning frameworks shows emerging promise for controlling carbon ion dose distributions amid respiratory motion, though direct clinical validation for this combination remains limited. These hybrid models may enhance the precision and adaptability of CIRT, offering improved outcomes. Future efforts should focus on clinical validation, standardization, and overcoming computational and data limitations to facilitate clinical translation of motion-adaptive CIRT. These approaches remain at Technology Readiness Levels (TRL 3-5) and require prospective clinical validation before routine implementation.

papers.title: Anaplastic Large Cell Lymphoma of the Brain Mimicking an Extra-Axial Frontal Tumor: A Case Report
Autophagy and intratumoral bacteria abundance influence the prognosis of patients with pancreatic carcinoma.
papers.abstract: The biological and clinical significance of the intratumoral microbiota in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains poorly defined. Using oncogenic Kras-driven mouse models of pancreatic tumorigenesis and human pancreatic tissue from patients with non-metastatic PDAC treated with neoadjuvant (n = 62) or adjuvant therapy (n = 101), along with samples from intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMN, n = 24), chronic pancreatitis (CP, n = 33), and healthy donors (n = 9), we determined tissue lipopolysaccharide (LPS), 16S rRNA sequencing, high-resolution quantitative multiplex immunofluorescence of autophagy markers (LAMP2, LC3B) and LPS, 16S rRNA fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) staining, and TLR4 signaling. In KrasCre mice, we identified significant bacterial accumulation in the pancreas, indicated by elevated LPS, increased FISH signals, enhanced TLR4 signaling, and activation of autophagy. Administration of exogenous LPS further amplified autophagy and TLR4 signaling, supporting a mechanistic link between microbial sensing and autophagy. In human tissue, both adjuvant and neoadjuvant PDAC samples showed significantly increased bacterial alpha- and beta diversity compared with controls, while CP showed a similar enrichment pattern that IPMN lacks; the underlying microbial diversity differs fundamentally across these conditions. Increased LPS levels, along with elevated autophagy markers and abundant FISH-positive bacteria, support the presence of intratumoral bacteria. Across four independent transcriptomic datasets, PDAC samples showed elevated expression of bacteria-associated pathways (including TLR4) and autophagy-related genes. Clinically, higher autophagy-associated LAMP2-LC3B colocalization and increased densities of FISH-positive cells were independently associated with prolonged survival in both adjuvant and neoadjuvant or combined PDAC patients. Collectively, these findings link intratumoral microbial enrichment to increased autophagy-associated signaling and improved patient outcomes, suggesting that microbial signals within the tumor microenvironment were associated with favorable survival.

papers.title: Case Report: Electroencephalography-informed low-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation targeting the supplementary motor area in severe functional movement disorder
Risk factors for venous thromboembolic events at 90 days in hospitalized patients with advanced cancer receiving palliative care: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
papers.abstract:
Purpose

Evidence regarding venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk in palliative care populations remains scarce, and current thromboprophylaxis recommendations are largely extrapolated from non-palliative oncology cohorts. This study aimed to determine the 90-day incidence of VTE and associated clinical risk factors in hospitalized patients with advanced cancer receiving palliative care.

Methods

This multicenter retrospective cohort study included adults with advanced cancer enrolled in a palliative care program who were hospitalized between 2018 and 2024 at two tertiary care centers in Bogotá, Colombia. VTE incidence was calculated, and clinical risk factors were identified using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models.

Results

A total of 782 patients were included (mean age 61 years; 58.7% male). Withing 90 days of admission, 81 patients (10.3%) developed VTE, corresponding to an incidence density of 2.3 events per 1,000 patient-days. Pulmonary embolism accounted for 40.7% of VTE events. In the adjusted analysis, lung cancer was associated with an increased risk of VTE (HR 2.34; p = 0.010), whereas higher Karnofsky Performance Status was associated with a lower risk (HR 0.98; p = 0.020). Age, sex, body mass index, baseline hemoglobin, active anticancer treatment, and white blood cell count were not independently associated with VTE. Overall, 90-day mortality was 66.3%.

Conclusion

VTE was a frequent complication among hospitalized patients with advanced cancer receiving palliative care. Lung cancer and poor functional status were independently associated with VTE, whereas traditional clinical predictors were not associated with VTE. These findings support individualized VTE risk assessment and highlight the need for future prospective studies evaluating thromboprophylaxis strategies in palliative care settings.

papers.title: Breast Cancer Metastasis to the Thyroid Presenting as a Collision Tumor With Papillary Thyroid Microcarcinoma and Oncocytic Adenoma: A Case Report
In Vivo CRISPR Screen Identifies RPS19 as an Immunotherapy Target in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Despite the remarkable clinical success of immunotherapy, its efficacy against hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains severely limited, highlighting an urgent need for novel targets and strategies to overcome immune evasion. Here, we aimed to identify key regulators of HCC immunity via unbiased functional screening and develop a targeted therapy to remodel the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). We performed an in vivo CRISPR-knockout screen using a 4500-gene sgRNA library in syngeneic HCC mouse models. Single-cell RNA sequencing of human HCC tissues and in vivo macrophage-depletion assays were utilized to dissect cellular populations and validate underlying mechanisms. We identified ribosomal protein S19 (RPS19) as a central mediator of HCC immune evasion, whose deletion in HCC cells mitigates the immunosuppressive TME. Mechanistically, scRNA-seq pinpointed tumor-associated macrophages as the key effector subset, whereby complement C5a receptor 1 (C5aR1) transduces RPS19 signals to trigger macrophage-dependent immune suppression. We further constructed SP94-peptide-modified disulfide-bond-containing nanoparticles (SNP<sub>SS</sub>) for targeted CRISPR-Cas9 delivery. SNP<sub>SS</sub> efficiently homes to HCC cells, releases payloads within the glutathione-rich TME, downregulates RPS19, reverses immune suppression, and robustly suppresses HCC progression in vivo. Collectively, the RPS19-C5aR1-macrophage axis fuels HCC immune escape, and SNP<sub>SS</sub>-based RPS19 gene-editing offers a promising strategy to remodel the TME and boost HCC immunotherapy efficacy.

papers.title: Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasonography of Orbital and Intraocular Pathologies in 24 Dogs and 6 Cats.
papers.abstract:
Objective

Contrast-enhanced ultrasonography (CEUS) is a noninvasive and relatively safe imaging technique to assess ocular perfusion, showing high sensitivity and specificity for tumor characterization in human oncology, while reports on its application in canine and feline diseased eyes are limited. This study aimed to describe the CEUS features of orbital and intraocular pathologies in dogs and cats in order to evaluate its diagnostic value in detecting and characterizing various lesions.

Animal studied

CEUS examinations of 30 animals (24 dogs, 6 cats) were evaluated retrospectively.

Procedures

Following B-mode ultrasonography, CEUS examinations utilizing sulfur hexafluoride were performed. Pathologies were categorized in one of the following groups: orbital neoplastic lesions, orbital inflammatory lesions, intraocular neoplastic lesions, intraocular inflammatory lesions and retinal detachment. Qualitative perfusion parameters, contrast intensity, enhancement pattern, perfusion type and time to wash-in and wash-out were evaluated.

Results

CEUS detected vascularization in orbital and intraocular pathologies, with variable enhancement characteristics. Persistent vascularization was observed in all cases of retinal detachment. In orbital and intraocular neoplastic lesions, CEUS improved lesion localization, assessment of interactions with surrounding tissues and tissue perfusion. For inflammatory pathologies such as abscesses, myositis, and steatitis, the additional diagnostic value of CEUS compared to B-mode ultrasonography was limited.

Conclusion

Findings indicated that CEUS could identify a variety of orbital and intraocular pathologies and provided additional diagnostic information to B-mode ultrasonography, particularly for assessing neoplastic lesions and retinal detachments. CEUS has the potential to enhance ophthalmic ultrasonography in differentiating specific pathologies. Prospective studies are warranted to further evaluate its clinical use.

papers.title: Dynamics of IDH1 Mutation and Protein Expression Between Primary and Recurrent Gliomas and Their Prognostic Significance.
papers.abstract:
Background

Isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 (IDH1) mutation is a key molecular marker in gliomas and is generally associated with favorable prognosis. However, its dynamic changes and prognostic significance during tumor recurrence remain incompletely understood.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective analysis of 42 patients with paired primary and recurrent glioma samples. IDH1 mutation status was determined by PCR, and the expression of IDH1 R132H protein was evaluated using a semiquantitative scoring system ranging from negative (-) to strongly positive (+++) based on expression intensity by immunohistochemistry (IHC). Changes in molecular features and WHO grade were analyzed, and their associations with progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and postrecurrence survival (PRS) were evaluated using Cox regression models.

Results

IDH1 mutation status remained largely stable between primary and recurrent tumors, with most patients retaining their original genotype. In contrast, WHO grade progression was observed in 45.2% of cases, indicating ongoing tumor evolution. IDH1 R132H protein expression exhibited dynamic changes, with both upregulation and downregulation detected at recurrence. In primary tumors, IDH1 mutation was independently associated with improved PFS (HR = 0.351, p = 0.016), whereas higher IDH1 R132H expression was associated with improved OS (HR = 0.371, p = 0.032). In recurrent tumors, IDH1 mutation showed a trend toward inferior PRS, although this association did not reach statistical significance, suggesting that the prognostic relevance of IDH1 alterations may vary during glioma evolution.

Conclusions

Although IDH1 mutation remains largely stable during glioma progression, its prognostic associations may vary between primary and recurrent disease. IDH1 R132H protein expression also shows dynamic changes and may provide complementary prognostic information. These exploratory findings support integrating genetic and protein-level biomarkers when evaluating glioma progression and warrant validation before informing the clinical application of IDH inhibitors.

papers.title: LncRNA A1BGAS1 Serves as a Tumor Suppressor in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer by Modulating the Expression of miR-3942-5P.
papers.abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), the leading contributor to global cancer mortality, is associated with a notably unfavorable prognosis. This study aims to explore the regulatory interaction between A1BG-AS1 and miR-3942-5p and its molecular mechanisms. The level of A1BG-AS1 and miR-3942-5p in both tumor tissues and cell lines (BEAS-2B, A549, H226) were measured using qPCR. Functional effects of A1BG-AS1 overexpression in NSCLC cells were evaluated through CCK-8, flow cytometry, and Transwell assays. The interaction between A1BG-AS1 and miR-3942-5p was validated through dual-luciferase reporter assays and rescue studies. A1BG-AS1 expression was markedly reduced in both NSCLC tissues and cell lines. A1BG-AS1 expression was significantly associated with various clinical parameters. Overexpression of A1BG-AS1 suppressed NSCLC cell function. Mechanistically, A1BG-AS1 interacted with and negatively regulated miR-3942-5p, and the antitumor effects of A1BG-AS1 overexpression were reversed by miR-3942-5p mimics.A1BG-AS1 inhibits NSCLC tumor progression by targeting miR-3942-5p.

Guideline Concordance of Antibiotic Recommendations From Large Language Models in Dentistry: A Vignette-Based Evaluation in Georgian and English
ADAM19 Promotes EMT-Related Changes and Serves as a Prognostic Marker in Circulating Tumor Cells of Renal Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Detection of circulating tumor cells (CTCs), particularly characterization of their epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) phenotypes, may improve prognostic accuracy for malignancies. Identification of novel biomarkers for CTC classification may improve the characterization of tumor progression and provide potential therapeutic insights for renal cell carcinoma (RCC). Herein, we identified that a disintegrin and metalloproteinase domain-containing protein 19 (ADAM19) was associated with EMT phenotypes of CTCs. In vitro functional experiments, Western blotting, and RNA sequencing demonstrated that ADAM19 promoted RCC malignant progression and EMT-related changes and was associated with NOTCH and NF-κB signaling pathways. Our findings further suggested potential bidirectional association between ADAM19 and these signaling pathways. CTCs isolated from xenograft mouse models exhibited enhanced proliferative, migratory, and invasive abilities, accompanied by increased ADAM19 expression compared with parental tumor cells. Clinical CTC analysis further revealed that ADAM19-Low-CTCs were associated with unfavorable clinical outcomes in RCC patients. Notably, higher time-updated ADAM19-Low-CTC counts were identified as an independent risk factor for progression-free survival (HR = 1.243, 95% CI: 1.006-1.536).

papers.title: Gastric Cancer: Epidemiology, Risk Factors, Pathogenesis, Clinical Features, Diagnosis, and Management.
papers.abstract: Gastric cancer is a multifactorial disease shaped by diverse risk factors and a complex pathogenesis spanning from chronic atrophic gastritis to invasive malignancy. Its global incidence shows marked geographic disparities, and advances in understanding its pathogenic mechanisms have improved diagnosis and treatment. Although the relationship between gastric cancer and macrophages has been extensively investigated, a systematic review integrating the entire clinical and biological continuum of gastric cancer, from epidemiology to management, with a focus on macrophages remains lacking. This review summarizes the epidemiology and multidimensional risk factors for gastric cancer, including infectious, dietary, genetic, microbiome, and metabolite-related factors. We describe the evolution of precancerous conditions, molecular alterations such as miRNA expression, and the bidirectional interactions between gastric cancer cells and macrophages that drive tumor progression within the tumor microenvironment. We also review clinical features, diagnostic approaches based on screening and endoscopy, and current management strategies, including surgery, systemic therapies, targeted therapies, immunotherapy, macrophage-targeted therapies, macrophage metabolic reprogramming, and recent preclinical and clinical advances. Overall, this review integrates evidence from epidemiology, molecular biology, immunology, and pathology to provide a comprehensive framework for understanding gastric cancer pathogenesis and current as well as emerging therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Synthetic MRI from radiotherapy planning CT images for Head-and-Neck Cancer.
papers.abstract:
Background

Computed Tomography (CT) provides geometric accuracy and electron density information essential for radiotherapy planning; however, it offers limited soft-tissue contrast. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) improves tumor visualization but introduces registration uncertainties when acquired separately from the radiotherapy planning CT (pCT). Cross-modality image synthesis enables the generation of synthetic MRI (sMRI) directly from pCT and may combine the strengths of both modalities, reducing reliance on MRI access.

Purpose

We propose a two-stage deep-learning framework for generating sMRI from pCT image-sets specifically in head-and-neck (H&N) cancers, providing soft-tissue contrast comparable to ground-truth MR images (gtMRI).

Methods

This study included 60 patient cases with H&N cancer treated with radical radiotherapy between March 2022 and April 2024 for model development (50 for training, 10 for validation), plus 10 additional cases, independent of the development cohort for testing. All patients underwent a standard, non-contrast pCT scan followed by an MRI acquired on a 3T Siemens MR simulator. Images were deformably-registered, yielding 10,000 matched CT-MRI slice-pairs for model training. The proposed model utilizes a two-stage architecture, a Pix2Pix conditional generative adversarial network (GAN) for coarse sMRI synthesis, followed by a conditional diffusion model for refinement. To test the model's robustness, 10 patient cases with both pCT and contrast-enhanced CT (ceCT) were used to generate sMRI. Model performance was assessed using structural similarity index (SSIM), multi-scale structural similarity index (MS-SSIM), mean absolute error (MAE), and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR). In addition, the geometric agreement of the primary (GTVp_70) and nodal (GTVn_70) gross tumor volumes delineated on sMRI vs. gtMRI was independently assessed by two radiation oncologists (ROs) using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95), and average symmetric surface distance (ASSD).

Results

The average MS-SSIM, SSIM, MAE and PSNR for pCT-derived sMRI were 0.82 ± 0.02, 0.70 ± 0.03, 0.05 ± 0.01, and 20.42 ± 0.66 dB, respectively. The mean MS-SSIM and SSIM values for ceCT-derived sMRI were 0.02 lower than those for the corresponding pCT-to-sMRI metrics. For the contour-based evaluation, sMRI-derived GTV contours achieved a mean DSC of 0.56 and 0.60 for GTVp_70, and 0.72 and 0.74 for GTVn_70 across the two ROs, relative to gtMRI contours.

Conclusion

Our proof-of-concept study demonstrates the feasibility of pCT-derived sMRI for H&N cancers using a deep-learning framework. The model produces grayscale patterns and soft-tissue contrast that closely resemble the gtMRI.

papers.title: Further Insights Into the Mechanisms of Lymph Node Metastasis.
papers.abstract: Metastasis of malignant tumors arising from epithelial organs to sentinel lymph nodes has important implications for prognosis, staging, and therapeutic decision-making. Recent insights into anatomic pathways, pathogenesis, molecular interactions, and genetic factors have encouraged scientists and clinicians to develop drugs that target mechanisms of lymph node metastasis. We summarize important aspects of the vast literature that pertains to these mechanisms, focusing on five phases that implicate invasion through the epithelial basement membrane and tumor microenvironment, into initial lymphatics, and, after flow through lymphatic trunks, into the sentinel lymph node. Valuable information regarding tumor cell-directed motility, lymphangiogenesis, host cells that enhance metastasis, immune responses to tumor antigens, and tumor-induced changes in sentinel lymph node(s) provides a promising avenue for the continued development of new therapeutic approaches to prevent and treat metastasis. This article reviews these aspects by synthesizing current scientific and clinical advances and translating them for medical professionals.

papers.title: Sociodemographic and clinicopathologic features associated with rapid relapse in triple-negative breast cancer: a Swedish nationwide registry-based study.
papers.abstract:
Purpose

To characterize clinicopathologic, treatment-related, and sociodemographic factors associated with rapid versus late relapse in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), and to evaluate how relapse timing influences metastatic patterns and survival outcomes.

Methods

Using linked Swedish population-based registers, we conducted a retrospective cohort study of women diagnosed with non-metastatic TNBC between 2007 and 2021. Patients were classified into three groups based on time to distant relapse or death: rapid relapse (rrTNBC; ≤24 months), late relapse (lrTNBC; >24 months), or event-free at last follow-up. Tumor characteristics, comorbidity, treatments, and sociodemographic variables were compared across groups. Multivariable logistic regression and survival outcomes were assessed. Sensitivity analyses restricted to healthcare regions with complete relapse data were performed.

Results

Among 8,298 patients, 15% experienced rrTNBC, 18% lrTNBC, and 67% remained event-free. rrTNBC was associated with older age, larger tumors, nodal involvement, advanced stage, and a higher frequency of visceral and multi-organ metastases. Patients with rrTNBC were less likely to receive adjuvant systemic therapy or radiotherapy and more likely to undergo mastectomy. Sociodemographic disparities were observed, with rrTNBC more frequent among patients who were single or widowed, lower educated, or had lower household income. Survival outcomes were substantially worse for rrTNBC compared with lrTNBC and event-free patients.

Conclusions

Rapid relapse defines a particularly vulnerable TNBC population characterized by aggressive tumor biology, early dissemination, inferior survival, and sociodemographic disadvantage, while lrTNBC represents an intermediate phenotype with delayed disease progression. Distinguishing rrTNBC from lrTNBC may improve risk stratification, guide treatment decisions, and support more personalized follow-up strategies.

papers.title: Snake venom toxins in cancer therapy: advances in targeted delivery and peptide design.
papers.abstract: Snake venom represents a potent biological arsenal of cytotoxic compounds. Venom proteins and peptides, including disintegrins, venomous enzymes, three-finger toxins, and serine proteases, have garnered attention as effective anticancer agents. Despite their efficacy at nano- or micromolar concentrations, non-standardized mixtures often limit their therapeutic utilization, necessitating fractionation to minimize side effects. This review examines the antitumor potential of snake venom and its constituent proteins and peptides through a literature search in NCBI PubMed. We highlight the antitumor efficacies of venom polypeptides by correlating them with IC<sub>50</sub> values across various cell lines, demonstrating micromolar cytotoxic concentrations. The review encompasses several key areas: whole venom antitumor efficacy, mechanisms of action of individual proteins and peptides, fractionation and purification methods, cytotoxic effects of low molecular weight peptides, and delivery system approaches utilizing peptide sequences as cell-penetrating mechanisms alongside liposomes and nanoparticles for enhanced polypeptide toxicity. Given that cilengitide contains an RGD sequence analogous to disintegrins and targets integrins, we provide a dedicated analysis of its anticancer potential and clinical trial outcomes. Clinical evidence indicates the necessity for further investigation into the synergistic effects of cilengitide with established chemotherapeutic agents. The scientific data reviewed demonstrate that antimetastatic properties constitute the most extensively studied mechanism of venom polypeptides. This review underscores the therapeutic promise of venom-derived polypeptides while emphasizing the critical need for advanced delivery systems and rigorous clinical validation to translate these findings into viable cancer therapeutics.
papers.journal: Saudi pharmaceutical journal : SPJ : the official publication of the Saudi Pharmaceutical Society

papers.title: Large Oncosomes Induce Pro-Metastatic Stromal-Myeloid Reprogramming.
papers.abstract: Bone metastasis can be facilitated by systemic remodeling, yet the tumor-derived signals that influence the bone marrow microenvironment remain incompletely understood. Large oncosomes (LOs) are atypically large (> 1 µm), tumor-derived extracellular vesicles shed by amoeboid cancer cells. Here, we demonstrate that LOs function as systemic mediators of metastatic niche formation by activating innate immune sensing in bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BM-MSCs). Systemic administration of LOs to immunocompetent tumor-bearing mice did not affect primary tumor growth but increased metastatic burden. LOs induced a robust, dose-dependent interferon-driven inflammatory program, characterized by interferon-stimulated genes and neutrophil chemokines. Mechanistically, this response was driven by LO-associated nucleic acids activating convergent cytosolic DNA- and RNA-sensing pathways in recipient stromal cells. LO-conditioned BM-MSCs promoted the accumulation and polarization of neutrophils toward an immunosuppressive, polymorphonuclear myeloid-derived suppressor cell (PMN-MDSC)-like phenotype. In vivo, genetic suppression of LO shedding in tumor cells reduced PMN-MDSC accumulation in the bone marrow, which was reversed by systemic LO administration. Together, these findings support a model in which LO-associated signals reprogram the bone marrow microenvironment to support metastatic colonization, identifying a previously unrecognized mechanism linking tumor vesiculation to immune remodeling at distant sites.

papers.title: Synaptic transmission and plasticity: molecular mechanisms, biological functions and therapeutic opportunities in neurodegenerative diseases.
papers.abstract: Synaptic transmission impairment and neuronal loss are hallmarks of neurodegenerative diseases (NDDs). To date, the absence of effective therapies for treating or preventing NDDs underscores the critical need to comprehend the mechanisms underlying synaptic loss and impairment to develop novel interventions. Synaptic transmission is a complex communication process between presynaptic and postsynaptic neurons. Separate postsynaptic receptors activated by a variety of neurotransmitters initiate different downstream signaling cascades that are modulated by receptor-associated auxiliary subunits. Moreover, glia-neuron interactions and various neuropeptides can also modulate diverse synaptic functions. In this review, we first summarize the presynaptic and postsynaptic regulatory mechanisms of synaptic transmission in glutamatergic, GABAergic, cholinergic, and dopaminergic neurons in NDDs. We then emphasize the fundamental role of microglia and astrocytes in maintaining neuronal homeostasis and discuss how glia-neuron cross-talk affects synaptic and neuronal function throughout the pathological processes of NDDs, as well as how aging accelerates synaptic dysfunction in NDDs. We also highlight therapeutic strategies aimed at preserving or restoring synaptic integrity, including approaches that enhance plasticity, fine‑tune neurotransmitter signaling, or target immune pathways. Finally, we evaluate the current state of research for each intervention class and consider the major obstacles and opportunities that lie ahead in developing effective synapse‑directed therapies for NDDs.

papers.title: HER2 in solid tumors: microenvironment features and multifaceted advances from mechanisms to clinical translation.
papers.abstract: Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) is a well-established oncogenic driver in multiple solid tumors, most prominently in breast and gastric cancers. Beyond gene amplification-driven signaling through canonical PI3K/AKT and RAS/MAPK pathways, emerging evidence reveals that HER2 functions within a highly dynamic and context-dependent tumor ecosystem. Interactions between HER2-positive tumor cells and immune and stromal compartments actively shape the tumor microenvironment, contributing to immune evasion, therapeutic resistance and disease progression. A central challenge in the clinical management of HER2-altered cancers is pronounced spatial and temporal heterogeneity, which undermines both diagnostic accuracy and the durability of targeted therapies. In response, advances in multi-omics profiling, liquid biopsy technologies and artificial intelligence-assisted analytics are redefining HER2 assessment, shifting it from static tissue-based classification towards dynamic, minimally invasive monitoring. In parallel, the therapeutic landscape has evolved from single-agent HER2 blockade to rational combination strategies. In particular, antibody-drug conjugates have emerged as a transformative modality, extending the therapeutic reach of HER2 targeting beyond traditional indications and offering new opportunities to overcome heterogeneity and drug resistance. This review synthesizes current insights into the molecular and microenvironmental biology of HER2-altered solid tumors and discusses how these advances are reshaping next-generation precision oncology.

papers.title: Treatment options after tumor resistance: exploiting vulnerabilities from genome to tumor microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Most advanced cancers eventually develop therapeutic resistance, often considered as a clinical endpoint but can be interpreted as an evolutionary state that exposes newly acquired dependencies and therefore creates a rationale for vulnerability-based treatment after standard options fail. This review summarizes resistance-associated vulnerabilities across genomic, epigenomic, signaling, cellular, and microenvironmental layers. At the genomic level, homologous recombination deficiency, deficient mismatch repair, chromosomal instability, and replication stress can inform DNA repair-directed, checkpoint-targeting, or immune-based strategies with different clinical evidence levels. At the epigenomic level, we propose chromatin-state maintenance vulnerability as an organizing concept describing adaptive dependence on chromatin-regulatory programs sustaining resistant phenotypes. This concept shifts epigenetic targeting away from isolated epigenetic marks to the machinery required to maintain a resistant phenotype. Compensatory signaling creates dependencies on specific network nodes, providing a rationale for combinations that suppress the pathways required for resistant-cell survival. Cancer stemness links molecular adaptations to persistent disease; interactions with a therapy-remodeled microenvironment create opportunities for intervention beyond direct tumor-cell killing. In this setting, therapeutic vulnerability may lie in reprogramming the surrounding ecosystem to restore antitumor immunity and treatment responsiveness. Additionally, we propose the concept of operational vulnerability biomarkers as measurements linked to a treatment-relevant dependency or functional susceptibility and a prespecified therapeutic decision. This decision-oriented framework complements established functional and dynamic biomarker concepts. By connecting resistant states with measurable dependencies, matched interventions, and clinical-trial strategies, the review provides a practical framework for developing and testing rational subsequent-line treatments while addressing the biological, analytical, and practical barriers to implementation.

papers.title: The synergistic potential of combining PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors with conventional therapies in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
Stroke-Heart Syndrome: Mechanisms, Temporal Phenotypes, and Diagnostic Reasoning.
papers.abstract: Stroke-heart syndrome (SHS) encompasses new or worsened cardiac abnormalities that arise after acute stroke, most often within the first 30 days and with an early peak. Its spectrum includes acute myocardial injury, electrocardiographic changes, arrhythmia, ventricular dysfunction, Takotsubo syndrome, and heart failure, but similar findings may reflect antecedent cardiac disease or systemic illness. This Review defines the accepted clinical boundaries of SHS and integrates central autonomic network disruption, neuroendocrine stress, inflammation, endothelial and microvascular dysfunction, oxygen supply-demand imbalance, and premorbid substrate into a time-resolved framework. Eight provisional, non-mutually-exclusive phenotypic domains are proposed to organize current evidence without implying validated endotypes. A diagnostic approach based on symptom chronology, prior cardiac data, serial troponin and electrocardiography, rhythm monitoring, echocardiography, selective coronary assessment, and cardiac magnetic resonance is presented to distinguish stroke-triggered injury from recent myocardial infarction, pre-existing atrial fibrillation, chronic myocardial injury, and established heart failure. No syndrome-specific treatment is validated; care should prioritize recognized cardiac emergencies, correction of reversible stressors, and coordinated stroke-cardiology decision-making. Prospective studies with documented premorbid status, standardized time points, and blinded adjudication are needed to validate the proposed phenotypes and determine whether they improve outcomes.

papers.title: Cognitive frailty in patients with acute coronary syndromes: A scoping review.
papers.abstract:
Aims

To address a critical knowledge gap, this is the first scoping review to systematically map and describe the evidence on cognitive frailty in patients with acute coronary syndromes (ACS), including its prevalence, assessment tools, associated factors, and clinical outcomes.

Methods

The Joanna Briggs Institute methodology guided the conduct of this scoping review, which has been reported in line with the PRISMA-ScR checklist. Following the PCC framework, a systematic search was conducted across five databases: PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Scopus, and Web of Science. The search was performed up to August 2026. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed quality.

Results

A total of 9 studies were included. The prevalence of cognitive frailty ranged from 8% to 55%, the differences attributed to the heterogeneity of assessment tools and diagnostic criteria. Regarding assessment tools, the FRAIL scale combined with the Short Portable Mental Status Questionnaire was the most commonly used combinations. Risk factors covered sociodemographic, physical health, and clinical domains. Prognostically, cognitive frailty was linked to higher composite short‑term (in‑hospital complications, prolonged stay, 30‑day events) and medium‑term (6‑month MACCE) risks, and also to elevated long‑term mortality and readmission.

Conclusion

Cognitive frailty is commonly reported in patients with ACS, with considerable variation across studies, and an association with adverse outcomes has been noted in multiple reports. However, the lack of standardized assessment tools and criteria makes results difficult to compare and synthesize. Existing prospective studies have primarily relied on baseline measurements of cognitive frailty to predict subsequent outcomes, without repeated assessments over time. This limits the ability to characterise the dynamic trajectory of cognitive frailty during the ACS course. Future research should focus on longitudinal studies, the development of rapid screening tools, and the exploration of multidisciplinary interventions.

papers.abstract: Glucose homeostasis depends on coordinated genetic and epigenetic regulation of pancreatic beta-cells, insulin-sensitive tissues, and neuroendocrine circuits. Histone Lactylation Drives WNK1 Expression to Promote Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma Progression Through Histone H3 Ser10 Phosphorylation.
papers.abstract: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) lacks effective targeted therapies, and how metabolic reprogramming drives oncogenic signaling remains poorly defined. Here, we identify histone H3 lysine 23 lactylation (H3K23la) as a key epigenetic mediator linking lactate accumulation to tumor progression. H3K23la is upregulated in ESCC and correlates with poor prognosis. Mechanistically, H3K23la promotes WNK lysine deficient protein kinase 1 (WNK1) transcription, which increases histone H3 Ser10 phosphorylation (p-H3S10) and enhances AKT transcription, thereby driving PI3K-AKT signaling. This defines a lactate-H3K23la-WNK1-p-H3S10-AKT axis connecting metabolism to oncogenic signaling. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition of WNK1 by CD03017 disrupts this pathway and suppresses tumor growth in vitro and in patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models. In conclusion, our findings define a metabolic-epigenetic-signaling axis in ESCC and establish WNK1 as a potential therapeutic target downstream of histone lactylation.

The relative efficacy of sensory modalities in driving insulin release, salivary secretion, appetite, and food intake: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract:
Background

Food sensory stimulation may influence eating behavior, but the effects of different stimulation patterns have not been systematically compared.

Objective

To quantify the effects of food sensory stimulation on insulin release, salivary secretion, appetite, and food intake, and compare the efficacy of those sensory modalities.

Methods

We systematically searched five databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, and Embase) for controlled human studies comparing visual, olfactory, gustatory, tactile, modified sham-feeding, or multisensory stimulation. Studies without an eligible comparator or relevant outcome were excluded. RCTs and non-RCTs were synthesized separately using random-effects meta-analysis when compatible numerical data were available and otherwise summarized qualitatively.

Results

We included 22 reports comprising 24 studies (6 RCTs, 18 non-RCTs) and 1008 adults (413 men, 595 women). Participants were predominantly healthy; two cohorts were women with obesity. The oldest cohort had a mean age of 72.4 years. RCTs showed increased salivary secretion (SMD=1.04, 95% CI [0.64, 1.45], P<0.0001) but no clear overall effect on food intake (SMD=0.32, 95% CI [-0.25, 0.88], P=0.2742). Insulin release and appetite were each assessed in one RCT and synthesized narratively. Non-RCTs indicated increases in insulin release (SMD=0.95, 95% CI [0.24, 1.66], P=0.0088), salivary secretion (SMD=0.78, 95% CI [0.38, 1.18], P=0.0002), appetite (SMD=0.54, 95% CI [0.29, 0.79], P<0.0001), and food intake (SMD=0.19, 95% CI [0.02, 0.35], P=0.0282).

Conclusion

RCT evidence suggests that food sensory stimulation increases salivary secretion but has uncertain effect on food intake. Non-RCT evidence indicates potential benefits across all four outcomes, although evidence for insulin release and appetite is limited. Further well-designed RCTs are needed to confirm these effects and clarify differences between sensory modalities.

The Association Between Sleep and Obesity in Adults: An Umbrella Review of Meta-Analyses.
papers.abstract:
Background and aims

Short sleep duration, poor sleep quality, and circadian disruption have been linked to obesity, but the proliferation of systematic reviews with meta-analyses (SRMAs) has fragmented the evidence. No prior umbrella review has synthesized all sleep characteristics exclusively in adults or formally graded the credibility of associations. We aimed to evaluate the association between various sleep characteristics and obesity‑related outcomes in adults.

Methods

We conducted an umbrella review of SRMAs. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, Scopus, CINAHL, and Epistemonikos were searched from inception to March 1, 2026. We included SRMAs examining adults (≥ 18 years) reporting any sleep exposure and obesity outcomes. Methodological quality was assessed using AMSTAR 2. Overlap of primary studies was quantified with the corrected covered area (CCA). Evidence was graded using Ioannidis criteria.

Results

Sixteen SRMAs encompassing approximately 13.8 million participants were included. Primary study overlap was very low (overall CCA = 0.024). Short sleep duration was associated with a 40% increased odds of obesity (pooled OR 1.40, 95% CI 1.27-1.55; I2 = 83.7%). Long sleep showed a modest association (OR 1.05, 95% CI 1.02-1.08; I2 = 0%). Both were classified as Class III (Suggestive) evidence. Daytime napping, social jetlag, and insomnia symptoms met only Class IV (Weak) criteria. Objective sleep measurement (polysomnography) yielded substantially larger effects (OR 2.70, 95% CI 1.80-4.05) than self‑report (OR 1.14, 95% CI 0.98-1.33). AMSTAR 2 assessment revealed two high‑quality, four moderate, nine low, and one critically low review.

Conclusions

Short and long sleep durations are suggestively associated with obesity in adults, with short sleep showing a stronger effect. Other sleep characteristics have weak or limited evidence. Clinicians should consider sleep duration a potentially modifiable risk factor for obesity.

trials.title: Comparing Retreatment of 177Lu-DOTATATE PRRT Versus the Usual Treatment in Patients With Metastatic Unresectable Gastroenteropancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors, NET RETREAT Trial
trials.conds: Metastatic Digestive System Neuroendocrine Tumor G1; Metastatic Digestive System Neuroendocrine Tumor G2; Unresectable Digestive System Neuroendocrine Tumor G1; Unresectable Digestive System Neuroendocrine Tumor G2
trials.interventions: Biospecimen Collection; Cabozantinib; Computed Tomography; Everolimus
trials.brief: This phase II trial compares the effect of retreatment with 177Lu-DOTATATE peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) to the usual approach of treatment with everolimus, sunitinib, or cabozantinib in patients who have previously received 177Lu-DOTATATE for gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (GEPNET) that has spread from where it first started (primary site) to other places in the body (metastatic) and that cannot be removed by surgery (unresectable). PRRT is a type of radiation therapy for which a radioactive chemical is linked to a peptide (small protein) that targets tumor cells. When this radioactive peptide is injected into the body, it binds to a specific receptor found on some tumor cells. The radioactive peptide builds up in these cells and helps kill the tumor cells without harming normal cells. In this trial 177Lu-DOTATATE is used for PRRT. 177Lu-DOTATATE PRRT may increase the length of time until worsening of the GEPNET compared to the usual approach. Everolimus is in a class of medications called kinase inhibitors. It is also a type of angiogenesis inhibitor. Everolimus works by stopping tumor cells from reproducing and by decreasing blood supply to the tumor cells. Sunitinib and cabozantinib, block certain proteins, which may help keep tumor cells from growing. They may also prevent the growth of new blood vessels that tumors need to grow. Sunitinib malate is a type of tyrosine kinase inhibitor and a type of antiangiogenesis agent. Retreating with 177Lu-DOTATATE may work better than everolimus, sunitinib or cabozantinib in shrinking or stabilizing tumors in patients with metastatic and unresectable GEPNET who were previously treated with 177Lu-DOTATATE.

trials.conds: Recurrent Small Cell Lung Cancer; Extensive-Stage Small Cell Lung Cancer; Small Cell Lung Cancer; Small Cell Lung Carcinoma; Refractory Small Cell Lung Cancer; Extrapulmonary Small Cell Carcinoma; Neuroendocrine Carcinoma; Poorly Differentiated Neuroendocrine Carcinoma; High-Grade Neuroendocrine Carcinoma
trials.interventions: Autologous B7-H3 CAR T; Cyclophosphamide; Fludarabine
trials.brief:
Background:

Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is the deadliest form of lung cancer. Extrapulmonary neuroendocrine cancer (EPNEC) is a similar type of cancer that develops anywhere other than the lungs. EPNEC is also deadly. B7-H3 is a protein often found in SCLC and EPNEC tumor cells. Researchers can modify a person s own T cells, or immune cells, to target B7-H3. When these modified T cells are returned to the body-a treatment called B7-H3 chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy-they may help kill cancer cells.

Objective:

To test B7-H3 CAR T cell therapy in people with SCLC or EPNEC.

Eligibility:

People aged 18 years and older with SCLC or EPNEC that either did not respond or returned after treatment.

Design:

Participants will be screened. They will have blood tests and tests of their heart function. They will have imaging scans.

Participants will undergo apheresis: Blood will be taken from the body through a needle. The blood will pass through a machine that separates out the T cells. The remaining blood will be returned to the body through a different needle. The collected T cells will be altered to make them attack cells with B7-H3.

Participants will be in the hospital for at least 15 days. They will receive chemotherapy drugs to prepare their body for the treatment. These drugs will be given through a tube attached to a needle inserted into a vein.

The modified T cells will be infused through a vein. Participants will remain in the hospital until they are well enough to go home.

Follow-up visits will continue for 15 years....

trials.brief:
Background:

\- Skin disease can have many causes. It can have widespread consequences, and in rare cases can lead to death. Researchers want to determine the causes of various types of skin diseases and find a way to treat them.

Objectives:

\- To determine the causes of various skin diseases and find ways to treat them.

Eligibility:

* People ages 2 and older who have:

  * A skin disease or at risk of developing a skin disease OR
  * A family member of persons with a skin disease
* Healthy volunteers ages 2 and older

Design:

* Participants will be screened under a separate protocol.
* Participants may take a survey about how their skin condition affects their quality of life.
* Participants will have a medical history and a physical exam including a detailed skin exam. Pictures will be taken of their skin to document any skin disease.
* Participants will have specimens collected. This may include:

  * Several teaspoons of blood taken at each visit
  * Stool samples
  * Nail and body fluid (like saliva) samples
  * Cheek swabs. The inside of the cheek will be scraped for about a minute in each direction to collect cells.
  * Collection of skin samples with:

    * A swab (like a Q-tip)
    * Gently scraping skin to remove the outer layers of cells
    * Applying and removing 1-inch pieces of tape
* Participants may have up to 4 skin biopsies in 12 months, with 4 separate biopsies taken each time.

  * An area of skin will be numbed with an injection.
  * A piece of skin the size of a pencil eraser will be removed using a small instrument.
  * A flat scar usually develops at the biopsy site.

trials.brief:
This study will evaluate members in families with a history of small bowel carcinoid cancer to study the natural history of those family members that have the disease, determine ways to improve early detection by performing surveillance on those at risk but without disease and to identify the gene(s) that may cause the tumors. Familial carcinoid tumors usually originate in hormone-producing cells that line the small intestine or other cells of the digestive tract. The tumors are slow-growing and usually take many years before they cause symptoms. It is known that these tumors occur more often in some families and are then passed from one generation to the next by inherited genes.

Members of families, including all siblings and offspring in which two or more immediate blood relatives have had small bowel carcinoid tumors are eligible for this study. In some cases unaffected spouses of family members diagnosed with carcinoid cancer are also requested to participate by donating a sample of blood only.

Participants undergo a medical evaluation every 3 years during a 3- to 5-day hospital stay at the NIH Clinical Center. All participants have a personal and family medical history obtained and undergo a physical examination, blood and urine tests.

People who already have a small bowel carcinoid tumor or are at risk of developing a carcinoid tumor have some or all of the following procedures to determine the presence of carcinoid tumor and its (omit next two words- location or) spread to other areas of the body:

* Video Capsule Endoscopy: Visualization of the gastrointestinal tract by ingesting a disposable, "vitamin-pill sized" video capsule that has its own camera and light source.
* CT of the chest abdomen and pelvis with oral and IV contrast : X-ray examination of the chest, abdominal and pelvis organs.
* 18 FDOPA Positron emission tomography (PET) with CT for localization: Nuclear imaging scan to look at tumor activity.
* MRI Liver with contrast - to determine if disease has spread to liver
* Gallium 68 PET/CT-limited to individuals that have residual tumor.
* Clinical and research blood work

Should mid gut carcinoid tumors be found every participant will be assisted in determine what the best course of treatment will be for them.
